rules.title: Verify Ohm's Law for AC Circuits
rules.description: In AC circuits, Ohm's Law is extended to use impedance (Z) instead of resistance (R). The voltage across an element is V = I * Z, where Z can be complex.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that the voltage (V) is calculated as the product of current (I) and impedance (Z). Verify that Z is expressed as a complex number in either rectangular form (R + jX) or polar form (|Z|∠θ). Confirm that the phase relationship between voltage and current is consistent with the impedance angle.
common_errors: Using resistance (R) instead of impedance (Z) in AC circuits.
Ignoring the phase angle when using complex impedance.
Incorrect conversion between polar and rectangular forms of impedance.

rules.title: Check Frequency Dependence of Reactance
rules.description: The reactance of capacitors and inductors depends on the angular frequency (ω = 2πf). Capacitive reactance is X_C = -1/(ωC), and inductive reactance is X_L = ωL.
rules.check_logic: Verify the correct formula for X_C and X_L, ensuring that the angular frequency (ω) and the element values (C or L) are used appropriately. Confirm that the negative sign is applied for capacitive reactance and that the units of reactance are in ohms (Ω).
common_errors: Using linear frequency (f) instead of angular frequency (ω = 2πf).
Incorrectly applying the negative sign for capacitive reactance.
Swapping the formulas for X_C and X_L.

rules.title: Validate Impedance in Series and Parallel Combinations
rules.description: For series circuits, impedances add directly (Z_eq = Z_1 + Z_2 + ...). For parallel circuits, the reciprocal rule applies (1/Z_eq = 1/Z_1 + 1/Z_2 + ...).
rules.check_logic: Check if the correct formulas are used for combining impedances in series and parallel configurations. Ensure proper handling of complex arithmetic, including addition, reciprocals, and conversions between polar and rectangular forms.
common_errors: Incorrectly adding impedances in parallel circuits.
Forgetting to invert the result when calculating equivalent impedance for parallel circuits.
Neglecting the imaginary component when combining impedances.

rules.title: Verify Power Calculations in AC Circuits
rules.description: The real power (P), reactive power (Q), and apparent power (S) are related to the voltage, current, and impedance phase angle: P = VIcosθ, Q = VIsinθ, and S = VI.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that the correct trigonometric components of the phase angle are used to calculate P, Q, and S. Confirm that the power factor (cosθ) is consistent with the impedance angle. Verify that the units of power are consistent (watts for P, VAR for Q, and VA for S).
common_errors: Confusing real power (P) with apparent power (S).
Using incorrect trigonometric functions for P and Q.
Ignoring the phase angle in power factor calculations.

rules.title: Check Resonance Condition in RLC Circuits
rules.description: In an RLC circuit, resonance occurs when the inductive reactance equals the capacitive reactance (X_L = |X_C|). At resonance, the total impedance is purely resistive.
rules.check_logic: Verify that ω_res = 1/√(LC) is used to calculate the resonance angular frequency. Confirm that at resonance, Z = R (no imaginary component). Ensure that the phase angle of the impedance is zero at resonance.
common_errors: Forgetting to equalize X_L and X_C at resonance.
Misinterpreting resonance as a condition where Z = 0.
Incorrect calculation of resonance frequency using ω_res = 1/√(LC).

rules.title: Ensure Dimensional Consistency of Impedance and Reactance
rules.description: Impedance (Z) and reactance (X_L, X_C) must have the dimension of ohms (Ω). Impedance is a complex quantity, but its magnitude and components must be dimensionally consistent.
rules.check_logic: Verify that all calculations involving Z, X_L, and X_C result in units of ohms (Ω). Check the dimensional consistency of intermediate terms, such as ωL and 1/(ωC). Ensure that capacitance (C) and inductance (L) are expressed in standard units (farads and henries, respectively).
common_errors: Using inconsistent units for capacitance (C) or inductance (L).
Calculating Z or X without confirming units of intermediate terms.
Mixing incompatible units, such as radians and degrees, in calculations.

rules.title: Verify Use of RMS Values for AC Voltage and Current
rules.description: In AC circuits, root mean square (RMS) values are used for voltage and current in power and impedance calculations. RMS values relate to peak values as V_RMS = V_peak / √2 and I_RMS = I_peak / √2.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that RMS values are used in calculations unless specified otherwise. For peak values given, confirm conversion to RMS using the correct formula. Verify that RMS values are used consistently in power and impedance calculations.
common_errors: Using peak values instead of RMS values in power calculations.
Incorrect conversion between peak and RMS values.
Assuming equivalence of RMS and peak values.

rules.title: Verify Phase Angle Sign Convention
rules.description: The phase angle (θ) of impedance is positive for inductive circuits (current lags voltage) and negative for capacitive circuits (current leads voltage).
rules.check_logic: Check if the sign of the phase angle is consistent with the type of reactance (inductive or capacitive). Ensure that angles are measured in the correct unit (radians or degrees) and that conversions between units are accurate.
common_errors: Reversing the sign of the phase angle for inductive or capacitive circuits.
Using degrees and radians interchangeably without conversion.
Incorrectly interpreting the relationship between current and voltage phase.

rules.title: Verify Quality Factor in RLC Circuits
rules.description: The quality factor (Q) of an RLC circuit is a measure of its sharpness of resonance and is defined as Q = ω_resL/R for series circuits or Q = R/(ω_resL) for parallel circuits.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that the correct formula for Q is used based on the circuit configuration (series or parallel). Verify that ω_res is calculated correctly and that the units of Q are dimensionless.
common_errors: Using the wrong formula for Q based on circuit configuration.
Incorrect calculation of ω_res.
Confusing the quality factor with other parameters like power factor.

rules.title: 乘法器DC分量提取规则
rules.description:
触发条件：当题目涉及两个正弦信号相乘并提取DC（直流）分量时
检查逻辑：检查输出是否满足 (1/2)*A1*A2*cos(Δφ)，且频率必须相等（ω1=ω2）否则DC项为0
rules.check_logic: 检查输出是否满足 (1/2)*A1*A2*cos(Δφ)，且频率必须相等（ω1=ω2）否则DC项为0
rules.trigger: 当题目涉及两个正弦信号相乘并提取DC（直流）分量时

symbolic_hint.canonical: V_dc = 0.5 * V1 * V2 * cos(phi1 - phi2) if omega1 == omega2 else 0

rules.title: 区分有效值与平均值
rules.description:
触发条件：涉及交流电（AC）充电、电解或电镀等电量累积过程时
检查逻辑：检查是否错误地将有效值（RMS）直接用于电量计算。电量累积 Q=I_avg*t，必须先将有效值转换为峰值，再计算半波或全波整流后的平均值。
rules.check_logic: 检查是否错误地将有效值（RMS）直接用于电量计算。电量累积 Q=I_avg*t，必须先将有效值转换为峰值，再计算半波或全波整流后的平均值。
rules.trigger: 涉及交流电（AC）充电、电解或电镀等电量累积过程时

rules.title: Incorrect constant-velocity timing in accelerating fields
rules.description:
This rule flags solutions that compute the time spent in an accelerating field region as distance divided by a single velocity (e.g., t = D/v_f, t = D/v_0, or using s = v t with a constant v) instead of accounting for the changing speed under acceleration. In regions with nonzero electric field (acceleration gaps), the ion velocity varies along the path; the correct time must be obtained from kinematics with acceleration or by integrating dt = dx / v(x) using energy conservation. Detection criteria:
- The solution includes an accelerating region (keywords like: accelerating field, electric field E, acceleration gap, potential drop across length S, D, D1, etc.) and computes the traversal time as t = length / v where v is labeled as exit/final/post-acceleration speed, initial speed only, or an unsourced constant speed.
- Specific patterns to flag include: t = D1/v_f, t = D1/v_out, t = D/v0, t = D/√(2 q E D / m), or generic use of s = v t for a region explicitly under acceleration without an acceleration term, integral, or average-velocity justification.
- The total time-of-flight is formed as drift time only (e.g., T ≈ L/v_drift) plus constants, with no explicit time contributions for accelerating regions, in contexts where fields are present.
Acceptable (do not flag) formulations include:
- Using constant-acceleration kinematics for a uniform field: t_acc = (v_out − v_in)/a with a = qE/m, equivalently t_acc = D / v_avg where v_avg = (v_in + v_out)/2, or t_acc = √(2D/a) if starting from rest.
- Using an explicit integral over position or potential: t_acc = ∫_0^D dx / √(v_in^2 + 2 (qE/m) x), or any algebraically equivalent closed form.
Rationale: Treating the acceleration region with constant velocity underestimates the traversal time and leads to incorrect conditions (e.g., time-focusing/derivative dt/dS = 0 in dual-field TOF mass spectrometers). The correct approach must include the acceleration time in each field region via integration or constant-acceleration kinematics before adding the drift time.

rules.title: Time-varying magnetic field: do not conserve mechanical angular momentum; use magnetic moment μ as the adiabatic invariant
rules.description: Scope: Solutions involving a charged particle (e.g., electron) in a uniform magnetic field that changes slowly in time (adiabatically), typically phrased as B increasing/decreasing over a time scale much longer than the gyroperiod. Check: If the solution asserts or implicitly uses conservation of mechanical angular momentum (e.g., states L = m r v is conserved, uses angular momentum conservation to relate r and B, or infers r ∝ 1/B by holding v constant) in the presence of a time-varying B, flag as a conceptual error unless the solution explicitly accounts for the induced electric field from Faraday’s law. Rationale: For dB/dt ≠ 0, Faraday’s law (∇ × E = −∂B/∂t) implies an induced azimuthal electric field that exerts a tangential force and torque on the particle; mechanical angular momentum and kinetic energy are not conserved during the change. Correct invariant: The first adiabatic invariant (magnetic moment) μ = m v_perp^2/(2 B) remains constant when B varies slowly compared to the gyroperiod and the field is sufficiently uniform. Expected scaling: From μ = const, v_perp ∝ √B and r = m v_perp/(e B) ∝ 1/√B (not 1/B). Trigger phrases/structures to flag: 'angular momentum is conserved' for a time-varying B, 'L = m r v = const', derivations that assume v is constant while B changes, or conclusions r ∝ 1/B in this context, without mentioning induced electric field or adiabatic invariant μ. Acceptable indicators to pass: Explicit mention of Faraday-induced E and its torque/work, or use of μ as the adiabatic invariant to obtain the correct scaling relations (e.g., r ∝ 1/√B).

rules.title: Misuse of equivalent resistance to compute current through an ideal ammeter and inconsistent R_eq claims
rules.description: This rule flags solutions to circuit problems where an ideal ammeter (zero resistance) is connected between two nodes (e.g., A and B) and the solver attempts to compute the ammeter current using an 'equivalent resistance between A and B'. Specifically, it detects: (a) use of I = V/R (Ohm’s law) across the ammeter with a stated or implied equivalent resistance R_eq between the same nodes, which is invalid because the ammeter voltage V_AB must be zero; (b) statements that the voltage across an ideal ammeter is nonzero or that an equivalent resistance across the ammeter determines its current; (c) assertions that an ideal ammeter 'does not affect the circuit behavior' without justification, even though inserting a short can alter current distribution unless nodes are provably equipotential; (d) contradictory or unsupported multiple values for the same equivalent resistance (e.g., claiming R_eq = R, R/2, etc., without a consistent derivation) and then using these to compute the ammeter current. The correct approach is to determine the ammeter current via KCL/KVL (nodal or mesh analysis) on the modified topology with the short in place; any equivalent resistance used must refer to a sub-network with nonzero voltage and not be used as R_eq across the ammeter itself.

rules.title: Incorrect claim that an ideal ammeter does not affect circuit behavior
rules.description: Flag solutions that assert an ideal ammeter (zero resistance) 'will not affect' the circuit or 'won't change node voltages/currents' when connected between two distinct nodes (e.g., between A and B). An ideal ammeter acts as a short circuit; connecting it between nodes forces those nodes to the same potential and generally redistributes currents. Correct reasoning must acknowledge the shorting effect and its implications (e.g., the ammeter current equals the short-circuit current between the nodes). Accept only statements noting negligible loading when an ammeter is inserted in series with an existing branch (not creating a new parallel path between nodes). Trigger on presence of keywords such as 'ideal ammeter' and 'zero resistance' combined with conclusions like 'does not affect', 'no effect', or 'doesn't change currents/voltages' without acknowledging 'short circuit', 'equal potential', or 'redistribute currents'.

rules.title: Displacement flux and B-field scaling with capacitor plate area (no A^2)
rules.description:
This rule checks derivations that use Ampere–Maxwell law inside a parallel-plate capacitor (or similar uniform-field capacitors) to ensure correct area scaling in the electric flux and induced magnetic field. Specifically:
- If the solution defines the field between plates as E = Q/(ε0 A_plate), then the electric flux through a loop of area A_loop (e.g., A_loop = π r^2) must be Φ_E = E · A_loop = (A_loop/(ε0 A_plate)) · Q.
- Therefore, the time derivative must be dΦ_E/dt = (A_loop/(ε0 A_plate)) · dQ/dt.
- Flag an error if dΦ_E/dt (or intermediate steps like dE/dt) contain A_plate^2 or any power of A_plate other than one in the denominator, e.g., dΦ_E/dt ∝ 1/A_plate^2.
- When applying ∮ B · dl = μ0 ε0 dΦ_E/dt for a circular Amperian loop of radius r (inside the plate area), require B(r) to scale as B ∝ r/A_plate (for uniform E). Flag if B is derived with 1/A_plate^2 or any incorrect power of A_plate.
- Dimensional cross-check: Φ_E scales linearly with A_loop and inversely with A_plate; dΦ_E/dt must scale as (A_loop/(ε0 A_plate)) times a current-like term dQ/dt. Any extra factor of A_plate indicates a derivation error.

rules.title: Angular momentum in uniform magnetic field: substitution and dimensional consistency
rules.description: This rule verifies algebraic and dimensional correctness when deriving angular momentum L for a charged particle moving in a circular orbit in a uniform magnetic field perpendicular to its velocity. Context trigger: the solution uses the centripetal balance m v^2 / r = |q| v B and/or states v = |q| B r / m, and then computes angular momentum via L = m v r (non-relativistic). Check steps: (1) From m v^2 / r = |q| v B, infer v = |q| B r / m. (2) Substitute into L = m v r to obtain the canonical expression L_canon = |q| B r^2 (independent of mass m). (3) Compare the solution’s stated L expression to L_canon. Flag a violation if the solution includes any extra or missing factor of mass (e.g., L = (|q| B r^2)/m or L ∝ (|q| B r^2)·m), an incorrect power of radius (not r^2), or any dependence on m after correct substitution. (4) Dimensional check: ensure the written L has units of kg·m^2·s^-1; specifically, |q|·B·r^2 has these units, while (|q|·B·r^2)/m does not. The rule catches algebraic slips during substitution and unit inconsistencies in expressions for angular momentum under uniform B-field circular motion.

rules.title: Explicit derivation required for conserved J∥ in uniform magnetic field with modified momentum
rules.description:
This rule verifies claims of conservation of the angular momentum component along a uniform magnetic field for systems of charges (e.g., an electric dipole) by enforcing an explicit, correct derivation. It targets unsupported statements like dJ/dt = 0 and the use of incorrect linear/rotational quantities.

Checks performed:
- Trigger: The solution claims that the angular momentum component along B (e.g., J_z, J∥, (r_CM × P + L_rot)·b̂) is conserved or states dJ/dt = 0.
- Required definitions: The solution must explicitly define the conserved quantity as J∥ = [(r_CM × P_mod) + L_rot]·b̂, where b̂ = B/|B|, P_mod is the modified (pseudo/canonical) momentum appropriate for a uniform magnetic field, and L_rot is the rotational contribution (e.g., I ω or an equivalent expression derived from the body's rotation).
- Required derivation: The solution must compute dJ∥/dt explicitly using:
  - Vector identities: d/dt (r × p) = r × ṗ + v × p.
  - Equations of motion for the charges: m r̈_i = q_i (v_i × B) (plus any other specified forces), and the rotational equation of motion (torque balance) for L_rot.
  - Projection along B: The final step must evaluate the dot product with b̂ (or equivalently align axes so that b̂ = ẑ) and show term-by-term cancellation leading to dJ∥/dt = 0.
- Consistency requirements:
  - P_mod must be clearly defined and must be the appropriate modified (pseudo/canonical) momentum for a uniform B field, not merely the mechanical center-of-mass momentum. If the solution earlier defined P, that same definition must be used here; inconsistent reuse is flagged.
  - L_rot (e.g., I ω) must be consistent with the defined rotational dynamics of the dipole (correct I about the center of mass and correct torque from magnetic forces). If I or L_rot were incorrectly defined earlier, the conservation claim is invalid.
  - Units and dimensions of P_mod, L_rot, and J∥ must be consistent.
- Acceptance criteria:
  - The derivation includes d/dt of both r_CM × P_mod and L_rot, uses the Lorentz-force-based ṗ terms, includes v_CM × P_mod terms, and demonstrates explicit cancellation upon projection along b̂.
  - Alternatively, a Lagrangian/Hamiltonian derivation that constructs the correct gauge-invariant (pseudo/canonical) momentum and uses Noether’s theorem is accepted only if it explicitly identifies the symmetry and shows dJ∥/dt = 0 with the correct J∥ expression.

Flags as errors:
- Claim of conservation (e.g., dJ/dt = 0, J_z conserved) without an explicit time-derivative calculation and projection along B.
- Use of unmodified mechanical momentum for P in a magnetic field or omission of the required pseudo/canonical correction.
- Use of an incorrect or undefined moment of inertia/rotational term (e.g., arbitrary I ω) or omission of magnetic torque contributions.
- Inconsistency between definitions of P or I used in earlier parts and those used in the conservation proof.
- Reliance on qualitative symmetry/Noether arguments without constructing the correct conserved combination and showing d/dt = 0 explicitly.

rules.title: Annular/Toroidal Area Sign and Consistent Use in Enclosed Current/Flux
rules.description: This rule verifies the correctness and consistency of cross-sectional area definitions in annular or toroidal geometries used to compute enclosed current or magnetic flux. It flags: (1) negative or unphysical area expressions such as A = π (R_in^2 − R_out^2) when R_out > R_in; the correct annular area is A = π (R_out^2 − R_in^2) ≥ 0. (2) Inconsistent reuse of an area variable: if an area A is defined (e.g., annular area), subsequent steps must use the same expression when computing enclosed current I_enclosed = ∫ J · dA or flux Φ_B = ∫ B · dA; switching to a different area (e.g., π R_in^2 or π r^2) without explicit, justified change of region/geometry is flagged. (3) Misuse of A(r): if an area is defined as a constant (from fixed R_in, R_out), later steps must not treat it as a function of r; conversely, if A(r) is defined for a radius-dependent region (e.g., π r^2), it must remain radius-dependent consistently. The rule also checks dimensional consistency (area must be non-negative and have units of length^2) and raises an error if the sign or geometry of the area used in enclosed-current/flux derivations is inconsistent with earlier definitions.

rules.title: Area vector magnitude must be the geometric area (angle-independent)
rules.description: This rule checks definitions of the area vector and magnetic dipole moment in current-loop problems within magnetic fields. It flags solutions that make the area vector (or dipole moment magnitude) depend on the loop’s orientation angle (e.g., include sinθ or cosθ factors) instead of keeping the geometric area constant and placing the angular dependence in the torque or energy expressions. Specifically, it verifies that: (1) The area vector is defined as A⃗ = A n̂ with A equal to the geometric area of the loop (e.g., l^2 for a square, πR^2 for a circle), independent of any orientation angle. (2) The magnetic dipole moment is defined as m⃗ = I A n̂ without any angular factor multiplying A or I. (3) The torque and energy use the correct angular dependence: |τ| = I A B sinα and U = −I A B cosα, where α is the angle between the loop’s normal n̂ and the magnetic field B. The rule flags expressions such as: A = l^2 sinθ n̂, A(θ) = A0 cosθ, m⃗ = I (A sinθ) n̂, or any statement implying that the magnitude of A⃗ varies with orientation. It allows torque expressions like τ = I A B sinθ only if θ is explicitly the angle between n̂ and B. It also prompts a check that the defined angle is the correct one (if the given angle is between the loop’s plane and B, then α = 90° − given angle; if between the normal and B, then α equals the given angle), but it does not flag angle-definition issues unless the area vector magnitude is made angle-dependent. This rule is intended to catch the specific misconception where students write A = l^2 sinθ n̂ or similar, incorrectly attributing the sinθ factor to the area vector rather than to the torque (or energy) formula.

rules.title: Area vector and magnetic moment direction in charged-particle loops
rules.description: This rule checks statements about the direction of the area vector and the magnetic moment for a charge moving in a circular orbit or current loop. It flags the following errors: (1) Defining the area vector as aligned with the particle's velocity, tangent to the path, or 'in the direction of motion.' The correct area vector is perpendicular to the plane of the loop (orbit) and its orientation is set by the right-hand rule applied to the conventional current direction. (2) Using the right-hand rule based on electron motion rather than conventional current (positive charge flow). For a negatively charged particle (electron), conventional current is opposite the electron's motion; the right-hand rule must be applied to the conventional current, not to the electron trajectory. (3) Claiming that the magnetic moment vector is parallel to the electron's angular momentum. The correct relation is μ = (q/2m) L, so for an electron (q = −e) the magnetic moment is antiparallel to the angular momentum. The rule should pass statements that (a) define the area vector as the normal to the plane of the loop with orientation given by the right-hand rule using conventional current, and (b) explicitly note that for electrons μ is opposite to L.

rules.title: Low-loss approximation for EM attenuation coefficient α
rules.description: This rule verifies the small-conductivity (low-loss) approximation of the attenuation coefficient α for a plane EM wave in a weakly conducting dielectric. Given the exact form α = ω * sqrt( (μ ε / 2) * [ sqrt(1 + (σ/(ε ω))^2) − 1 ] ), with x = σ/(ε ω) and the condition x^2 ≪ 1, the correct leading-order approximation is α ≈ (σ/2) * sqrt(μ/ε). The verifier should: (1) Detect when the solution invokes the assumption (σ/(ε ω))^2 ≪ 1 (or equivalent). (2) Extract the student’s approximated expression for α and symbolically compare it to α_ref = (σ/2) * sqrt(μ/ε). (3) Flag as incorrect if the student’s α_lowloss contains: (a) ω-dependence at leading order, (b) sqrt(μ ε) in the denominator (e.g., α ≈ σ/(2√(μ ε))), or any form proportional to 1/√(μ ε) instead of √(μ/ε), (c) missing the factor of 1/ε inside the square root leading to dimensional mismatch. (4) Perform a dimensional check: α must have SI units of 1/m; α_ref yields 1/m because σ (S/m) * sqrt(μ/ε) (Ω) = 1/m. Any student expression not simplifying to 1/m should be flagged. (5) Accept equivalent correct forms that are algebraically identical to (σ/2) * sqrt(μ/ε) (e.g., using medium wave speed v = 1/√(μ ε), α ≈ (σ μ v)/2) but reject forms like α ≈ σ/(2√(μ ε)) or with residual ω factors. If the solution subsequently uses z_{1/e} = 1/α to infer depth, and α is incorrect per this rule, flag the depth result as propagated error.

rules.title: Check units and form of EM attenuation coefficient α in low-loss media
rules.description: This rule verifies that the attenuation coefficient α for a plane electromagnetic wave in a weakly conducting medium (σ/(ωε) << 1) has the correct dimensional form and magnitude. The expected low-loss approximation is α ≈ (σ/2)·sqrt(μ/ε), which yields units of 1/m because (S/m)·Ω = 1/m. The phase constant is β ≈ ω·sqrt(μ·ε) and has units of 1/m. The rule performs the following checks: 1) Dimensional analysis: Parse the user’s expression for α and evaluate its SI units using μ in H/m, ε in F/m, and σ in S/m. Flag an error if the units do not reduce to 1/m. In particular, expressions of the form α ∝ σ/(sqrt(μ·ε)) or α ∝ σ·sqrt(μ·ε) produce units S/s or S·s/m and must be rejected. 2) Pattern check for β/α swap: If α contains sqrt(μ·ε) (a signature factor of β) rather than sqrt(μ/ε), flag a likely swap between α and β. 3) Numerical sanity: When problem parameters are supplied (e.g., μ≈μ0, ε≈εr·ε0 with εr∈[3,15], σ∈[1e−5,1e−2] S/m), compute α. If |α| falls grossly outside a plausible range for GPR in soils (for these parameters typically 10^−3 to 10^1 m^−1), or if the implied penetration depth 1/α is microns to millimeters rather than meters, flag as unphysical. The rule provides corrective guidance: ensure α uses sqrt(μ/ε), not sqrt(μ·ε), and re-evaluate with α ≈ (σ/2)·sqrt(μ/ε).

rules.title: Opposite-charge superposition for axial dipole field (z > d)
rules.description: Checks that a dipole modeled as two equal-magnitude monopoles/charges separated by distance d uses opposite signs when superposing the axial field for z > d. Specifically: if the solution models two sources of magnitude q_m (or q) located on the z-axis at z = 0 and z = d, then for points with z > d the axial field must reflect opposite source signs (+q_m at z = d, −q_m at z = 0). The correct on-axis scalar expression must be proportional to [1/(z − d)^2 − 1/z^2], not [1/(z − d)^2 + 1/z^2]. For magnetic monopoles, an acceptable form is B(z) = (μ0 q_m / 4π)[1/(z − d)^2 − 1/z^2] along +z; for electric charges, the analogous E(z) uses (1/(4π ε0) q)[1/(z − d)^2 − 1/z^2]. Flag solutions that: (a) sum the two inverse-square contributions with a plus sign, (b) treat both sources as same sign (e.g., both +q_m) without introducing opposite signs in the superposition, or (c) assign the axial direction incorrectly by making both contributions point in +z for z > d. Do not apply this rule to solutions that do not explicitly use the two-point-source (monopole) dipole model or that provide the far-field dipole limit ∝ 1/z^3 without decomposing into two inverse-square terms. Equivalent algebraic rearrangements that simplify to a difference are acceptable and should not be flagged.

rules.title: Axion-induced field mis-modeled as standard toroidal field
rules.description: Checks solutions for modeling errors where the axion-induced effective current density J = g (da/dt) B in a toroidal magnet is treated as producing the standard toroidal solenoid field inside the core rather than the axial field in the pickup-loop region. The rule triggers if: (1) the solution uses or derives B = μ0 N I / (2π r) (or equivalent Ampère's law toroid expressions) to obtain the axion-driven magnetic field; (2) the induced field at the detector/pickup loop is described as azimuthal (φ-hat) or 'toroidal' rather than axial (z-hat); (3) the field is evaluated only inside the toroid core (at radius r along the winding) instead of in the central bore where the pickup loop resides; (4) an 'effective current' I_eff is substituted into the toroid formula (e.g., I_eff ≈ ∫ J·dA or I_eff ∝ g a0 ω B A) to compute Bφ in the core. Context cues include explicit use of μ0 N I/(2π r), Ampère's law around the toroid, references to the azimuthal unit vector φ̂ for the detected field, or language indicating the flux is taken from the toroidal core field. A compliant modeling should recognize that J_eff is azimuthal within the magnet volume and sources an oscillating axial (z-directed) magnetic field in the bore/pickup-loop region; the rule flags deviations from this geometry and orientation.

rules.title: Axis–plane orthogonality and angle-definition consistency
rules.description: Checks that solutions respect the stated geometry when an axis of rotation is perpendicular to a named plane (e.g., plane abcd). Specifically: (1) Any line segment lying entirely in that plane (edges, face diagonals such as bd) must have a 90° angle with the axis; any claim of a different angle (e.g., 45°) between such a segment and the axis is flagged as incorrect. (2) Verifies consistent use of the problem-defined angle θ: if θ is defined as the angle between the face diagonal bd and the magnetic field B, the solution must not reinterpret θ as an angle between any wire/segment and the rotation axis. (3) In induced-EMF or velocity projections, ensures the angle used is between v and B (e.g., in E = B l v sin φ), not between the wire and the axis or between the wire and B unless explicitly justified by geometry; misuse of θ or any angle to represent wire–axis inclination is flagged. This rule catches statements such as 'the diagonal bd makes a 45° angle with the axis' or 'the angle between the wire and the axis equals θ' when the axis is perpendicular to the plane containing the wire/diagonal.

rules.title: Nonzero azimuthal magnetic field requires z-acceleration term q v_r B_phi
rules.description: Checks for the common mistake of setting m*ddot{z} = 0 ("free motion along z") in cylindrical/toroidal geometries when the magnetic field has an azimuthal component B_phi != 0. Physics basis: In cylindrical (r, phi, z) coordinates, with B = B_phi e_phi, the Lorentz force contributes F_z = q v_r B_phi (since e_r × e_phi = e_z). Therefore, unless v_r is explicitly constrained to be identically zero for all time (e.g., by a stated hard constraint r = const), z-motion is coupled to radial motion and ddot{z} is generally nonzero. The verifier should: (1) Detect that the solution is using cylindrical/toroidal coordinates and identifies a nonzero B_phi component (or claims a toroidal field primarily in the phi-direction). (2) Extract the z-equation of motion: if the student sets m*ddot{z} = 0 or omits the magnetic term in z (e.g., writes m*ddot{z} = q E_z only) while B_phi != 0, then require an explicit statement that v_r ≡ 0 by constraint or boundary condition; initial v_r = 0 is not sufficient. (3) If no such constraint is provided, flag an error and suggest the minimally correct coupling term m*ddot{z} should include + q v_r B_phi (and, if present, + q E_z). Also cross-check radial equation: it should include a corresponding term - q v_z B_phi. This rule specifically catches incorrect v × B evaluations that miss the z-component from B_phi, leading to the incorrect conclusion of free motion along z.

rules.title: Require velocity-dependent back-EMF and piecewise powered-to-ballistic modeling in railgun motion
rules.description:
This rule verifies solutions to problems where a conducting bar slides on powered rails in a magnetic field (railgun/motional EMF contexts). It flags errors when the solution assumes a constant current or constant magnetic force/acceleration and ignores the velocity-dependent back-EMF and the transition from powered motion on the rails to ballistic flight. The rule checks for:
- Current modeled as a constant (e.g., I = V/R) without a velocity-dependent motional EMF term. Correct modeling requires I(v) = (V - ε(v)) / R_total with ε(v) = B·L·v opposing the motion.
- Magnetic force F = I·L·B or acceleration a taken as constant despite the presence of motional EMF; the acceleration during the powered phase must depend on v through I(v).
- Use of the full crossing distance (e.g., w = 1000 m) in powered kinematic relations (s = 0.5 a t^2, v^2 = v0^2 + 2 a s, etc.) instead of limiting the powered displacement to the rail length D. The powered motion must be constrained to D.
- Absence of piecewise modeling: (1) a powered phase along the ramp over length D with velocity-dependent dynamics to obtain the exit speed, followed by (2) a ballistic phase after leaving the rails where magnetic propulsion ceases and only gravity acts. Solutions that treat the entire crossing under the same constant acceleration or ignore the phase transition are flagged.
Detection heuristics: If the solution’s current I or force F lacks dependence on velocity v, or presents a numeric/angle-dependent constant acceleration applied across the entire crossing distance/time, or uses w in powered kinematics without separately computing exit speed at D and then projectile motion, trigger an error.

rules.title: Verify correct application of Biot-Savart Law equation
rules.description: The Biot-Savart Law states that the magnetic field dB at a point due to a current element I·dl is proportional to the cross product of the current element vector and the unit vector pointing from the current element to the observation point, divided by the square of the distance between them. This law is given as: dB = (μ₀ / 4π) * (I·dl × r̂) / r². It applies for steady currents.
rules.check_logic: Ensure the magnetic field contribution dB is calculated using the cross product (I·dl × r̂), and the denominator contains r² where r is the distance between the current element and the observation point. Verify that μ₀ / 4π is included as a constant multiplier.
common_errors: Forgetting to include the cross product in the equation
Incorrectly calculating the distance r or the unit vector r̂
Omitting the constant μ₀ / 4π
Using r instead of r² in the denominator
Using non-steady currents, which invalidates the law

rules.title: Verify correct application of Ampere's Law in integral form
rules.description: Ampere's Law relates the closed line integral of the magnetic field B around a closed loop to the current enclosed by the loop: ∮B·dl = μ₀I_enclosed. It is valid for steady currents and symmetric geometries where the magnetic field is uniform along the loop.
rules.check_logic: Check if the line integral of B·dl is properly calculated and equated to μ₀ times the total current enclosed by the loop. Ensure the loop is chosen to align with the symmetry of the problem.
common_errors: Failure to consider the direction of the magnetic field (sign convention in B·dl)
Forgetting to enclose the current completely within the loop
Applying Ampere's Law to non-steady currents
Incorrectly assuming symmetry in situations where it does not exist

rules.title: Ensure correct use of coordinate systems and sign conventions
rules.description: Both Biot-Savart Law and Ampere's Law require consistent application of coordinate systems (Cartesian, cylindrical, or spherical) to define vectors. The right-hand rule is used to determine the direction of the magnetic field.
rules.check_logic: Verify the coordinate system used is consistent throughout the problem, and the right-hand rule is applied correctly for cross products and determining field directions. Ensure proper transformations are applied when switching between coordinate systems.
common_errors: Switching between coordinate systems without proper transformations
Incorrect application of the right-hand rule for the cross product
Mislabeling components of vectors in the chosen system

rules.title: Verify geometric constraints for symmetry in Ampere's Law
rules.description: Ampere's Law in integral form is most effective for symmetric geometries like infinite wires, solenoids, or toroids, where the magnetic field is uniform and constant around the chosen loop.
rules.check_logic: Check if the geometry satisfies symmetry conditions. For instance, ensure the magnetic field is constant along the loop or the current enclosed is distributed uniformly. Verify that the chosen Amperian loop aligns with the geometry.
common_errors: Applying Ampere's Law to asymmetric geometries
Neglecting to account for non-uniformity in the magnetic field
Incorrectly selecting an Amperian loop that does not align with the geometry

rules.title: Verify dimensional and unit consistency in calculations
rules.description: The magnetic field B has units of teslas (T) in the SI system, and its dimensions are [M][T]⁻²[A]⁻¹. Ensure all terms in the Biot-Savart and Ampere's Law equations conform to these units.
rules.check_logic: Check each term in the equations for consistent units. For example, μ₀ has units of T·m/A, and r² should be in meters². Verify that the final magnetic field result has units of teslas.
common_errors: Omitting or miscalculating the μ₀ constant
Using incorrect units for distance (r) or current (I)
Mismatch in units between magnetic field B and other terms

rules.title: Verify magnetic field direction consistency
rules.description: The direction of the magnetic field calculated using Biot-Savart Law or Ampere's Law must conform to the right-hand rule or symmetry arguments.
rules.check_logic: Ensure the calculated field direction follows the right-hand rule for current-carrying wires or symmetry constraints for Ampere's Law. Verify that the direction is consistent with the problem's setup and assumptions.
common_errors: Incorrect use of the right-hand rule for field direction
Ignoring symmetry constraints for field direction in Ampere's Law
Reversing the field direction due to sign convention errors

rules.title: Verify boundary conditions at interfaces
rules.description: At the boundary between two media, the tangential component of the magnetic field B and the normal component of the magnetic flux density B·n must satisfy continuity conditions.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that the tangential component of B is continuous across the boundary, and the normal component of B·n accounts for any surface currents or discontinuities.
common_errors: Ignoring surface currents at boundaries
Incorrectly applying continuity conditions for B
Neglecting the effect of material properties on B

rules.title: 已知比例系数形式的反向约束
rules.description:
触发条件：题目明确给出结果正比于特定函数（如 tan(α/2)）时
检查逻辑：在积分或代数化简中，优先寻找能产生该特定半角函数的几何关系（如 (1-cosα)/sinα），避免陷入不相关的倍角变换。
rules.check_logic: 在积分或代数化简中，优先寻找能产生该特定半角函数的几何关系（如 (1-cosα)/sinα），避免陷入不相关的倍角变换。

rules.title: 复杂源磁通量积分校验
rules.description:

检查逻辑：必须先通过安培环路定理或毕奥-萨伐尔定律求出空间磁场分布 B(r,z)，再对回路面积进行积分 S B·dA，检查是否遗漏几何对数项或面积项。
rules.check_logic: 必须先通过安培环路定理或毕奥-萨伐尔定律求出空间磁场分布 B(r,z)，再对回路面积进行积分 S B·dA，检查是否遗漏几何对数项或面积项。

rules.title: 等效电流源磁场方向判定
rules.description:
触发条件：题目给出有效电流密度公式 J = k * B 且 B 为已知几何对称场时
检查逻辑：需识别 J 的流向。若 B 为环向场，则 J 为环向，其产生的感生磁场 B_eff 应类比螺线管（轴向），而非再次套用环向场公式。
rules.check_logic: 需识别 J 的流向。若 B 为环向场，则 J 为环向，其产生的感生磁场 B_eff 应类比螺线管（轴向），而非再次套用环向场公式。

rules.title: 有限长电流磁场角度定义校验
rules.description:
触发条件：计算直导线磁场 B = (μ0 i / 4π r) * (cos θ1 - cos θ2) 时
检查逻辑：检查 θ1 和 θ2 是否为从场点垂足向导线两端点连线与导线方向的夹角，注意半无限长导线的一个极限角通常为 0 或 π。
rules.check_logic: 检查 θ1 和 θ2 是否为从场点垂足向导线两端点连线与导线方向的夹角，注意半无限长导线的一个极限角通常为 0 或 π。
rules.trigger: 计算直导线磁场 B = (μ0 i / 4π r) * (cos θ1 - cos θ2) 时

rules.title: Misapplication of B_normal boundary condition at conductor surfaces
rules.description: Checks for incorrect claims that the normal component of the magnetic field (B_n) is zero at the surface of an electric conductor due to a 'perfect conductor' boundary condition. In magnetostatics, Gauss's law for magnetism (∇·B = 0) implies the normal component of B is continuous across any interface (n·(B2 − B1) = 0) in the absence of magnetic monopoles, regardless of conductivity. Therefore, asserting B_n = 0 at a metal or perfectly conducting (PEC) surface is generally incorrect unless the interior medium is explicitly modeled as a superconductor/perfect diamagnet (Meissner state, μ → 0) where B = 0 inside, or an equivalent magnetic boundary (e.g., imposed by specialized metamaterials). The rule flags statements such as: 'normal component of B vanishes at a conducting surface', 'B_n = 0 at a perfect conductor boundary', or 'B·n = 0 at z = 0 for a thin conducting film' without accompanying justification that the interior medium has B = 0 (superconductor/perfect diamagnet) or a derived condition from the specific induced-current response. It also requires that any use of image monopoles/dipoles to enforce boundary behavior be tied to the correct physical mechanism (e.g., induced surface currents satisfying Maxwell boundary conditions), not invoked as a universal PEC boundary condition for B. Acceptable justifications include: explicit mention of a superconducting Meissner state or μ = 0 medium inside the surface; or a derivation referencing Maxwell boundary conditions showing how induced currents in the actual geometry enforce the stated B_n at the boundary. Otherwise, the solution should instead use the correct boundary relations: continuity of B_n and possible discontinuity of tangential H via n × (H2 − H1) = K (surface current).

rules.title: Capacitance must scale with permittivity ε; Coulomb constant k cannot appear in the numerator
rules.description: This rule checks derivations of capacitance for electrostatic capacitors when the problem defines k as the electrostatic (Coulomb) constant (k = 1/(4π ε0), units N·m^2·C^-2). It flags a modeling error if the solution uses k in the numerator of a capacitance expression (e.g., C ∝ k A/s), or otherwise makes C directly proportional to k. Correct formulations require capacitance to scale with permittivity: C = ε A/d, or equivalently C = εr ε0 A/d = A/(4π k d) times any geometric factor. Detection criteria: (1) Identify any equation or proportionality involving capacitance (symbols like C, C_total, C_single, C_max). (2) Determine from the problem or the solution text that k is the electrostatic constant (look for phrases like "electrostatic constant k" or units N·m^2·C^-2). (3) If k appears multiplied in the numerator with area/geometry (e.g., k*A, k*geometry) or C ∝ k without an explicit inverse 1/k (or 1/(4π k)) relationship, flag an error. (4) Dimensional check: using k*A/d yields units incompatible with farads; this confirms the misuse. Exceptions: Do not trigger if k is explicitly defined as dielectric constant or relative permittivity (some texts use k for εr); in that case, C ∝ k is acceptable. Also do not trigger if k only appears inside ε0 = 1/(4π k) or as 1/(const·k). This rule is particularly relevant for parallel-plate, sector, or variable-overlap capacitors where the correct dependence is C ∝ ε and therefore C ∝ 1/k when expressed in terms of k.

rules.title: Apply Capacitance Formula for Parallel Plate Capacitors
rules.description: The capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor is given by C = ε * A / d, where ε is the permittivity of the material between the plates, A is the area of one plate, and d is the separation between the plates.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the area (A) and separation (d) are correctly used in the formula for parallel plate capacitors, and ensure the permittivity (ε) corresponds to the material between the plates.
common_errors: Using incorrect formula for parallel plate capacitors
Confusing the area with the separation distance
Ignoring the permittivity of the dielectric material

rules.title: Calculate Energy Stored in Capacitor Correctly
rules.description: The energy stored in a capacitor is given by U = 1/2 * C * V^2, where C is the capacitance and V is the voltage across the capacitor.
rules.check_logic: Ensure the energy is calculated using the correct formula, with accurate values for capacitance (C) and voltage (V). Verify that the 1/2 factor is included.
common_errors: Omitting the 1/2 factor in the formula
Using resistance instead of capacitance
Using an incorrect voltage value for the calculation

rules.title: Account for Dielectric Constant in Capacitance
rules.description: The introduction of a dielectric increases the capacitance by a factor of the dielectric constant k, modifying the equation to C = k * ε₀ * A / d, where ε₀ is the permittivity of free space.
rules.check_logic: Ensure the presence of a dielectric is accounted for in the capacitance calculation, and verify that the dielectric constant (k) is applied correctly.
common_errors: Ignoring the increase in capacitance due to the dielectric
Applying the dielectric constant to an incorrect variable
Confusing the dielectric constant (k) with the permittivity (ε)

rules.title: Maintain Correct Sign Conventions for Potential Differences
rules.description: Voltage is defined as the potential difference where the positive terminal is at a higher potential. Correct sign conventions are crucial for determining current flow direction and energy calculations.
rules.check_logic: Verify that potential differences are used with the correct sign conventions, and ensure polarity is assigned accurately based on the electric field direction.
common_errors: Reversing the potential difference sign
Incorrectly assigning polarity
Ignoring the direction of the electric field

rules.title: Ensure Unit Consistency in Capacitance Calculations
rules.description: Capacitance has units of farads (F), equivalent to coulomb/volt. Dimensional consistency ensures accurate calculations.
rules.check_logic: Verify that all terms in capacitance calculations use consistent units, such as meters for area dimensions, volts for voltage, and farads for capacitance.
common_errors: Mixing up area units (e.g., cm² vs m²)
Using incorrect units for the dielectric constant
Miscalculating due to voltage in incorrect units (e.g., V vs mV)

rules.title: Apply Correct Rules for Capacitors in Series or Parallel
rules.description: Capacitors in series have a reciprocal capacitance sum, while those in parallel directly add: 1/C_total = 1/C₁ + 1/C₂ + ... for series; C_total = C₁ + C₂ + ... for parallel.
rules.check_logic: Verify the configuration of capacitors (series or parallel) and ensure the correct formula is applied for the total capacitance calculation.
common_errors: Confusing series and parallel formulae
Incorrectly summing reciprocal quantities
Misidentifying circuit sections as series or parallel

rules.title: Verify Ideal Conditions for Capacitance Calculations
rules.description: Capacitance equations assume ideal conditions: perfectly conductive plates, uniform electric field, and negligible edge effects.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that physical assumptions hold true, such as ignoring fringing effects or non-uniform fields, and verify that the plates are assumed to be perfectly conductive.
common_errors: Considering edge effects without applying corrections
Assuming a uniform field in non-ideal cases
Incorrectly applying the perfect plate assumption

rules.title: Account for Temperature Effects on Capacitance
rules.description: Capacitance can vary with temperature due to changes in the dielectric material's properties. This is particularly important for materials with high temperature coefficients.
rules.check_logic: Verify whether temperature effects on the dielectric constant or material properties are significant and accounted for in calculations.
common_errors: Ignoring temperature dependence of the dielectric constant
Assuming constant capacitance in varying temperature conditions
Failing to use temperature-corrected material properties

rules.title: 临界平衡态能量转化判定

触发条件：题目提及“弹性膜/弹簧”、“电荷注入”及“临界力常数k”时

rules.check_logic: 检查是否将离子泵做的功（外力功）等效为系统总势能的变化（弹性势能+电场能）。在临界失稳点，外力功通常对应于系统达到该状态所需的最小输入能量。

检查逻辑：检查电容公式是否错误写为 C=kA/d。正确形式应为 C = A / (4πkd)。
rules.check_logic: 检查电容公式是否错误写为 C=kA/d。正确形式应为 C = A / (4πkd)。
