rules.title: Variable-capacitance coupling and order consistency in LC–mechanical linearization
rules.description: Checks electromechanical LC–capacitor systems where C depends on plate separation x (e.g., C(x) = ε0 S/(X1 + x)) for two common logical errors: (1) improper differentiation of a constant source and (2) omission of the linear coupling term arising from C(x). The rule triggers when the problem involves an inductor L in series with a voltage source U and a parallel-plate capacitor whose capacitance varies with x. Verification steps: (a) KVL for the electrical branch should be L q¨ + q/C(x) = U with U treated as constant; flag any derivation that differentiates this equation to produce q‴, U˙, or U¨ terms without an explicitly time-varying source. (b) Linearization about equilibrium (x = 0, q = q0, C0 = ε0 S/X1, q0 = U C0) must include the electromechanical coupling in the electrical equation: L δq¨ + (1/C0) δq + (U/X1) x = 0 (equivalently L q¨ + (X1/(ε0 S)) q + (q0/(ε0 S)) x = 0). Flag if the x-dependent coupling term is missing or if C is treated as constant throughout (e.g., yielding L q¨ + (1/C0) q = U with no x term). (c) Require explicit use of ∂C/∂x at equilibrium in at least one linearized equation; flag if no derivative of C with respect to x appears. This rule detects internal inconsistency where the coupling from C(x) is ignored and prevents incorrect elevation of the system’s differential order by differentiating a constant voltage source.

rules.title: Incorrect constant-voltage energy calculation for capacitor-like discharge
rules.description: This rule flags solutions that compute the energy released in a transient electrostatic discharge (e.g., capacitor discharge, cloud–ground lightning) by assuming a constant voltage and using U = I * V * t or U = P * t without time integration or a supply maintaining the voltage. The rule targets model inconsistencies where the system is described as a passive charge-storage element (capacitor or cloud–ground field) whose voltage necessarily collapses during discharge, yet the energy is evaluated as if V were fixed. Detection criteria (all must be met): (1) The solution models a passive electrostatic system using any of: capacitance C, Q = C * V, V = E * d (or E0 * h), parallel-plate approximations, or cloud–ground capacitor analogies. (2) The energy of the discharge is computed using a constant-voltage power formula: U = I * V * t, U = P * t, or equivalent (e.g., using an average current I_avg and a single V), with no integral over time (no ∫ V(t) I(t) dt) and no 1/2 factor associated with capacitor energy. (3) There is no explicit external source or regulation keeping the voltage constant (e.g., battery, mains, ideal source stated). (4) The solution does not use a physically consistent energy expression for passive discharge such as U = (1/2) C V^2 (initial), U = (1/2) V * Q, or an explicit time integral of power with V(t) decreasing. When these conditions are met, the rule flags an error: mixing a capacitor model with a constant-voltage energy calculation for a discharge. Acceptable cases that should not be flagged: energy from a source powering a resistive load at fixed V (with a stated source), or a correct discharge calculation using U = (1/2) C V^2 or ∫ V(t) I(t) dt.

rules.title: Parallel-plate capacitor energy/capacitance must include separation d
rules.description: Purpose: Detect the common modeling error where the separation d between parallel plates (or membrane thickness) is omitted from capacitor energy/capacitance expressions, leading to dimensionally incorrect results and wrong d-dependence of forces/work. Scope: Applies when a solution models two opposed uniformly charged surfaces as a parallel-plate capacitor with area A, permittivity ε, and separation/thickness d (e.g., biological membranes, parallel plates). Checks: 1) Capacitance form: Verify C = ε A / d. Flag as incorrect if C is written without 1/d (e.g., C = ε A). 2) Energy forms: Verify that the electric energy uses one of the equivalent, d-dependent identities: U = Q^2/(2C) with C = ε A/d, U = Q^2 d/(2 ε A), U = (1/2) ε A V^2 / d, or U = (1/2) Q V. Flag if U is written without d (e.g., U = (1/2) Q^2/(ε A) or U = (1/2) ε A V^2) or any expression dimensionally inconsistent with joules when only {Q, V, ε, A, d} are available. 3) Dimensional sanity: Ensure the final U carries units of energy; expressions like Q^2/(ε A) or ε A V^2 lack a factor of length and must be flagged. 4) Force/pressure dependence (if derived from U): For fixed V, expect F = (1/2) ε A (V/d)^2 and pressure p = (1/2) ε (V/d)^2 (i.e., ∝ 1/d^2). For fixed Q, expect F = Q^2/(2 ε A) (independent of d but nonzero). Flag if the derived force/pressure lacks the correct d-dependence, yields zero force at fixed Q, or otherwise follows from a d-independent U. Trigger examples: The solution includes phrases or equations such as U = 1/2·Q^2/(ε A), U = 1/2·ε A V^2, or C = ε A, or omits d entirely in energy/force expressions despite defining a plate separation/thickness. Correction reference: Remind that for parallel plates, C = ε A/d and U must include d via U = Q^2 d/(2 ε A) = (1/2) ε A V^2 / d = (1/2) Q V.

rules.title: Capacitor force under fixed charge must be independent of plate separation
rules.description: Purpose: Detect modeling errors where the electrostatic force/pressure between two oppositely charged, parallel surfaces with fixed charge is made to depend on separation d. Scope: Parallel-plate capacitor or membrane modeled as two facing charged surfaces (e.g., neuron membrane), especially when charges are placed by pumps/are isolated (fixed Q or fixed surface charge density σ). Physics reference: For a parallel-plate geometry at fixed charge Q (no battery), the attractive force is F = Q^2/(2 ε A), and the pressure is P = σ^2/(2 ε), both independent of separation d. At fixed voltage V (battery connected), F = (1/2) ε A V^2 / d^2 and P = (1/2) ε V^2 / d^2, which do depend on d. Trigger conditions: 1) The solution text indicates or implies fixed charge conditions: mentions of ions pumped onto surfaces, isolated capacitor, fixed Q, fixed σ, no external circuit/battery, or uses σ = Q/A as a constant. 2) Under such conditions, the submitted expressions for electrostatic force or pressure contain explicit d-dependence (e.g., proportional to 1/d, 1/d^2, or any non-constant function of d) when expressed in terms of Q or σ; or the solution uses voltage-based formulas (e.g., F = (1/2) ε A V^2 / d^2, P = (1/2) ε V^2 / d^2, E = V/d) without establishing a constant-V boundary condition. Pattern checks: - Flag any force/pressure formula of the form F ~ Q^2/(ε A d^n) or P ~ Q^2/(ε A^2 d^n) with n ≠ 0 under fixed-charge context. - Flag usage of U = (1/2) C V^2 or E = V/d to compute force/pressure when the narrative asserts or implies fixed Q (correct potential to use is U = Q^2/(2C) with derivative at fixed Q). - Flag mixing of Q- and V-based formulas indicating inconsistent constraints (e.g., deriving F with V/d while simultaneously treating Q or σ as the fixed parameter). Acceptance conditions: - Under fixed-charge context, accept expressions equivalent to F = Q^2/(2 ε A) or P = σ^2/(2 ε), independent of d; also accept derivations via U = Q^2/(2C) leading to d-independent force. - Under fixed-voltage context (explicitly states battery/constant V), allow d-dependent forms F ∝ 1/d^2 and P ∝ 1/d^2. Diagnostic message on violation: "Electrostatic force/pressure for a parallel-plate system with fixed charge must be independent of separation. Your expression introduces a d-dependence or applies constant-voltage formulas under fixed-charge conditions. Use U = Q^2/(2C) and differentiate at fixed Q, yielding F = Q^2/(2 ε A) and P = σ^2/(2 ε)."

rules.title: Torque in variable-capacitance geometries must come from energy derivative, not F=Q^2/(2kA) with a lever arm
rules.description: This rule verifies that torque (or force leading to torque) in problems with variable overlap/angle capacitors (e.g., sector plates on a rotor) is obtained via the energy method and the correct constraint (fixed Q after disconnection or fixed V while connected). A correct solution must use τ(θ) = -∂U/∂θ with U = Q^2 / (2 C(θ)) for fixed charge or U = (1/2) C(θ) V^2 for fixed voltage, and explicitly involve dC/dθ or d(1/C)/dθ. The rule flags as incorrect the following patterns: (a) invoking the parallel-plate force or pressure formula F = Q^2 / (2 k A), p = σ^2/(2ε), or equivalent, to obtain a net force and then multiplying by an assumed lever arm to get torque; (b) assuming a single effective lever arm such as R·sin((θ0−θ)/2) or using the centroid of overlap area without justifying a full pressure distribution integral; (c) omitting the determination of whether Q or V is constrained after (dis)connecting the source; (d) producing a torque expression that does not contain dC/dθ (or d(1/C)/dθ) in any form. The rule is triggered when a solution uses area-based force formulas (Q^2/(2kA), σ^2/(2ε), ‘pressure × area’) for curved/rotational capacitor geometries, introduces ad-hoc lever arms for torque, or fails to apply τ = -∂U/∂θ with the appropriate energy for the connection condition.

rules.title: Capacitor voltage must be derived from charge/current relation or proven parallel-node equality
rules.description: This rule flags steps that assign a capacitor voltage using Ohm's law from an unrelated resistor current (e.g., V_C(t*) = I_Rx(ti) * R_x) without proper justification. The checker requires one of the following to be explicitly demonstrated when determining V_C at a specific time: (1) Use of the capacitor constitutive relation V_C(t) = V_C(t0) + (1/C) ∫_{t0}^{t} i_C(τ) dτ (or Q = C·V with charge conservation), or (2) a clear topology argument that the capacitor is in parallel with the referenced resistor (same two nodes) and that the time indices match (t* = ti), so V_C(t) = V_Rx(t) follows from node voltage equality and KVL/KCL. The rule also enforces continuity of capacitor voltage (V_C cannot change instantaneously), so any assignment implying an instantaneous set by an external event (e.g., induced emf stopping) without integrating current is invalid. If a solution sets V_C at any time by multiplying a current through a different branch by a resistance, or uses current at one time to determine capacitor voltage at another time without the integral or parallel-node proof, it is flagged as a logic error.

rules.title: Misapplication of equipotential property to cavity interiors of conductors
rules.description: Flags solutions that incorrectly assert that the potential in a hollow cavity within a conductor is the same everywhere or equals the potential on the conductor’s inner/outer surface, especially when charges are present inside the cavity. The equipotential property applies only to the conducting material, not to the empty cavity region. Typical erroneous cues include statements such as: (a) 'the potential inside the conductor (including the cavity) is the same as on the inner surface,' (b) 'the cavity is equipotential,' (c) 'E inside the cavity is zero' (without conditions), or using 'E=0 inside a conductor' to conclude uniform potential throughout the cavity. The rule should trigger when an internal charge (e.g., a point charge +Q inside the cavity) is present and the solution equates the cavity potential to the conductor’s surface potential or to a constant without solving Poisson/Laplace equations, using image methods, or superposition with induced charges. Exception: If the solution explicitly states there are no charges within the cavity and the inner boundary is at a constant potential, concluding that the cavity potential is constant is acceptable (Laplace solution with constant boundary). Otherwise, the potential in the cavity generally varies with position due to the internal charge and induced surface charges, and only the metal is equipotential.

rules.title: Characteristic velocity must be material/geometry constant in quasi-static (small-v) regime
rules.description: This rule verifies that, in problems involving eddy-current interactions (e.g., a magnetic dipole moving near a conducting film), the characteristic velocity v0 used to form the dimensionless ratio v/v0 is independent of the object's velocity v in the quasi-static (small-v) limit. The check flags errors where the solution asserts or derives v0 ∝ v, v0 = k·v, or otherwise makes v0 an explicit function of v for the low-velocity regime. Detection steps: (1) Identify statements referring to the small-velocity/quasi-static regime (e.g., 'small-v', 'low velocity', 'slow motion', 'v << v0'). (2) If within this regime the solution writes v0 as a function of v (e.g., 'v0(v)', includes v symbol on the right-hand side of v0’s definition, or claims linear scaling 'v0 ∝ v'), flag as a conceptual error. (3) If the solution uses the ratio v/v0, verify v0 depends only on material/geometry parameters (e.g., conductivity σ, thickness t, permeability μ, characteristic lengths) and not on kinematic variables (v, a) in the small-v limit. Exceptions: do not flag if the solution explicitly and correctly justifies a v-dependence via material properties that themselves depend on v through a stated mechanism (e.g., temperature-dependent conductivity due to self-heating linked to v), and provides a consistent physical model for that dependence.

rules.title: Misapplied charge conservation in systems connected to an external reservoir/ground
rules.description: Flags solutions that impose conservation of net charge within a subset of conductors (e.g., small spheres) when the problem explicitly involves connections to an external conductor, ground, battery, or large charged sphere. In such setups, the connected subsystem can exchange charge with the external body, so statements like "q1 + q2 + q3 = 0", "the total charge on the small spheres remains zero", or "sum of charges equals the initial charge of the small spheres" are incorrect unless the solution includes the external conductor in the conserved system or demonstrates that no charge transfer is possible. The rule checks for: (1) context keywords indicating an external reservoir (e.g., "connected to ground", "connected to a large/distant conducting sphere", "battery/voltage source", "wire to external conductor", "reservoir", "successively connected"), and (2) assertions of internal charge conservation on the subset (e.g., "q_total_small = 0", "q1 + q2 + ... = constant because of charge conservation"). It does not trigger if the solution explicitly treats the entire closed system (including the external conductor) for conservation or if the problem states the connection is purely internal/isolated (no charge exchange). The correct constraint in these connection steps is potential equalization with the external conductor, not zero net charge of the subset.

rules.title: Apply charge conservation to the interacting subset, not the whole system
rules.description: Checks that conservation of charge is applied to the correct set of bodies in charge-redistribution scenarios. When the problem states that only a subset of conductors exchange charge (e.g., two plates that collide/contact and have time to redistribute charge) while other bodies remain isolated/fixed and do not exchange charge, the sum of charges after interaction for the exchanging subset must equal the sum of their initial charges. Equivalently, it can be written as the total initial system charge minus the charges of all non-interacting bodies. The verifier scans for conservation equations of the form: sum of charges after for the interacting subset equals the total initial charge of the entire system, without subtracting fixed/isolated bodies. If such an equation is found, the rule flags it. Example: with initial charges α = −Q (fixed, no contact), β = +q, γ = +Q, and only β and γ exchanging charge, the correct relation is Q_beta + Q_gamma (after) = q + Q = (−Q + q + Q) − (−Q). Any solution asserting Q_beta + Q_gamma = q (the total charge of the whole three-body system) misapplies charge conservation and should be flagged.

rules.title: Charge density from Gauss’s law must use field gradient (ΔE/Δz), not E/h
rules.description: This rule flags solutions that compute a volume or average charge density ρ (C/m^3) from Gauss’s law using a single electric field magnitude divided by a length (e.g., ρ = ε0·E/h). Gauss’s law relates enclosed charge to the net flux through a closed surface; for a planar/cylindrical slab of thickness h with a vertical field E(z), the correct relation is ρ = ε0∇·E, and the slab-averaged density is ρ_avg = ε0·[E_bottom − E_top]/h (equivalently ε0·ΔE/Δz with proper sign). The rule triggers if: (1) ρ or ρ_avg is computed as ε0 times a single E value divided by a geometric length (h, d, L) without using a difference of field values at the two boundaries or an explicit spatial derivative; (2) the derivation treats flux as E·A for one cap and then divides by volume A·h to get ρ, without subtracting the flux from both caps; (3) only one field value (e.g., E = 100 V/m) and one height (e.g., h = 100 m) are used to produce a non-zero ρ. Acceptable forms include ρ = ε0∇·E, ρ = ε0·dE/dz for one-dimensional vertical fields, or ρ_avg = ε0·[E(z1) − E(z2)]/|z2 − z1| with consistent sign conventions. Example of an incorrect pattern to flag: "ρ = ε0·E/h" yielding ≈ 8.85×10^-12 C/m^3 from E = 100 V/m and h = 100 m; correct approach uses boundary fields, e.g., ρ_avg ≈ ε0·(150 − 100)/100 m ≈ 4.4×10^-12 C/m^3.

rules.title: Improper assumption of equal charges in sequential connections
rules.description: Checks electrostatics solutions where identical conductors (e.g., small metal spheres) are connected successively to a large charged conductor/reservoir. Flags the unjustified assumption that charges acquired are equal (e.g., q1 = q2 or q1 = q2 = q3) merely because the conductors are identical or because their potentials must match the reservoir. In sequential processes, previously charged objects alter the potential at later objects; thus the charge required to reach the same reservoir potential generally differs between steps. Trigger conditions: (1) the problem statement or solution text indicates sequential or one-by-one connections (keywords like 'successively', 'in turn', 'first/second/third'); and (2) the solution asserts equality of charges without modeling or referencing superposition of potentials from previously charged objects, mutual influence/coupling, or a specific symmetry that guarantees equal potentials at each step (e.g., simultaneous connection or proven independence). The rule also flags potential-matching equations that omit contributions from already charged bodies when determining later charges.

rules.title: Charge Sign Consistency in Cyclotron Motion, Current, and Magnetic Moment
rules.description:
This rule verifies consistent handling of the charge sign in derivations involving cyclotron motion, electric current from orbital motion, and the magnetic moment. It flags solutions that mix q and |q| in a way that produces sign errors for direction-sensitive quantities. The rule checks for the following:

1) Cyclotron frequency and period: If the solution defines ω = |q|B/m or T = 2πm/|q|B (acceptable for magnitudes) but later treats ω or T as signed without reintroducing the sign of q, flag. Correct signed frequency is ω_signed = qB/m; magnitude-only forms must be explicitly treated as magnitudes.

2) Current from orbital motion: If current is computed using I = |q|/T or I = |q| ω/(2π) for a specific charged particle (e.g., electron) without addressing sign/direction (i.e., not using I = q/T or I = q ω/(2π)), flag. For an electron (q = −e), the conventional current should be negative relative to the electron’s motion direction.

3) Magnetic moment relation: If the magnetic moment is written with |q| as μ = (|q|/(2m)) L or its direction is stated incorrectly (e.g., μ parallel to L for an electron), flag. The correct signed relation is μ = (q/(2m)) L, implying μ is antiparallel to L for q = −e.

4) Lorentz force and direction statements: If direction-sensitive steps use |q| in q v × B or claim motion/rotation sense based on |q|, flag. Direction must come from the signed q.

5) Mixing q and |q| within the same derivation step: If a step uses |q| to derive a quantity and then uses that quantity as if it carried the sign of q without explicitly restoring the sign, flag.

The rule considers a derivation correct if absolute values are confined to scalar magnitudes (e.g., r = mv/(|q|B), |ω| = |q|B/m, T = 2πm/|q|B) and all direction-sensitive quantities (current sign, μ orientation, rotation sense) explicitly use the signed charge q, with special attention that for electrons (q = −e), μ is antiparallel to L and to B, and the conventional current is opposite the electron motion.

rules.title: Require use or explicit irrelevance of given circuit parameters (R, L) and motional EMF
rules.description: This rule checks solutions to electromechanical problems (moving current-carrying loops in magnetic fields) for proper treatment of given circuit parameters such as total resistance R and self-inductance L, and for acknowledgment of motional EMF. It flags solutions that: (1) are given R (and/or L) in the problem statement but never use R (or L) in any equations or reasoning, and do not explicitly justify why these parameters are irrelevant; (2) assume or use a fixed current I (e.g., in torque τ = IAB sinφ or magnetic moment M = IA) without stating the source type and why the current is unaffected by induced EMF; (3) ignore motional EMF (ε = ∮(v × B)·dl or dΦ/dt) when the loop is moving/rotating, unless an explicit assumption is made that an ideal current source enforces I(t) = constant and self-inductance is neglected, thereby making R and ε not alter I; (4) for a voltage source or unspecified source, fail to write or reference the governing circuit relation (e.g., I = (V − ε)/R or L dI/dt + R I = V − ε) or to discuss resistive dissipation/damping implications. The solution must either incorporate R/L into the electrical dynamics (Ohm’s law/Faraday’s law) or clearly state assumptions (ideal current source; L ≈ 0) that render R and ε irrelevant to I; otherwise, the rule triggers a modeling error.

rules.title: No energy threshold for circular motion in uniform magnetic field
rules.description: Flag any claim that a charged particle requires a minimum kinetic energy, speed, or momentum to execute circular motion in a uniform magnetic field when no other constraints or forces are introduced. In a uniform B field, the transverse motion is circular for any nonzero transverse velocity; the radius is r = p/(|q|B). Energy/momentum only set the radius; there is no intrinsic threshold for circularization. Acceptable threshold calculations must be explicitly tied to external constraints (e.g., detector geometry imposing r <= R to ensure repeated looping within the apparatus, presence of electric fields, radiation reaction, or collisions). If a solution states or derives a 'minimum' energy/momentum/speed for circular motion or for curving/looping without specifying such constraints, or implies that relativistic treatment introduces an energy threshold for circular motion, flag as a modeling error. Also flag formulations that assert circular motion requires v above/below a specific value in a uniform B field alone.

rules.title: Double-counting coil turns when using B or B_max
rules.description: This rule flags solutions that define a coil-generated magnetic field in terms of the number of turns N (e.g., B or B_max given by B = mu0 * N * I / (path length), or explicitly B_max = mu0 * N * I / (2*pi*R)), and then later present a final result that still includes an explicit multiplicative factor of the same N together with B or B_max. For a fixed magnetic field amplitude B (or B_max), measurable quantities driven by the field (e.g., axion-induced effective current J = g * dot(a) * B, induced voltage/flux in a pickup system, etc.) must not depend separately on the coil's turn count N used to generate B; N only enters through B when expressing B in terms of coil parameters. The rule checks for patterns such as 'answer ∝ N * B', 'answer ∝ N * B_max', or 'answer contains both B (or B_max) and an extra N factor' after B (or B_max) has already been defined using N. It also flags apparent double counting like 'answer ∝ N^2 I' resulting from keeping N outside B while B was set proportional to N*I. Exception: a distinct pickup coil turn count (e.g., N_pickup) may legitimately appear if it was not the N used to define the source field B; the rule attempts to match the same symbol N used in the B definition. Remediation: either (a) express the final result entirely in terms of I and N by substituting B = mu0 * N * I / (...) and remove B/B_max, or (b) keep the result in terms of B or B_max and remove the separate N factor so the scaling is not double counted.

rules.title: Conducting wire: Piecewise electric field domain (E=0 inside, 1/r outside)
rules.description: Checks derivations that use Gauss's law for a charged conducting wire in electrostatic equilibrium. Expected: a piecewise statement of the electric field with E(r<r0)=0 inside the metal and E(r>=r0)=lambda/(2*pi*epsilon*r) outside (using epsilon0 in vacuum or epsilon for a medium), and explicit mention of the boundary at the wire radius r0. Also expected: correct use of Gauss surfaces where Q_enc=0 for a cylindrical Gaussian surface with radius r<r0 (no enclosed surface charge) and Q_enc=lambda*L for r>=r0. Flags solutions that present E=lambda/(2*pi*epsilon*r) without specifying the domain r>=r0, that imply or state a nonzero field inside the conductor, that set Q_enc=lambda*L for a Gaussian surface with r<r0, or that omit the role of r0 entirely. If a sketch is provided, it should not show field lines inside the conductor and should reflect a constant potential inside. Do not trigger if the problem explicitly specifies a nonconducting (insulating) wire with a stated volume charge distribution or a non-electrostatic (time-varying) situation.

rules.title: Ampère–Maxwell usage must include/confront conduction current where applicable
rules.description: When a solution invokes Ampère–Maxwell law to find B-fields during capacitor charging/discharging, it must treat both terms: ∮B·dl = μ0 I_conduction(thru surface) + μ0 ε0 dΦ_E/dt. Flag an error if the solution simplifies to only the displacement-current term (μ0 ε0 dΦ_E/dt or ∇×B = μ0 ε0 ∂E/∂t) without explicitly justifying that I_conduction through the chosen surface is zero. Specifically check geometry/region: (a) If the Amperian loop/surface lies in the dielectric gap between plates and is bounded so as not to intersect any conducting paths (wires, plates, rings), neglecting I_conduction can be acceptable with a stated justification; (b) If the loop/surface is outside the gap, threads or intersects conducting elements (lead wires, current-carrying plate regions, external rings), or is chosen such that conduction current can pass through it, then μ0 I_conduction must be included or explicitly shown to be zero. Also verify current continuity: for a charging/discharging capacitor, I_conduction in the circuit equals the displacement current through the gap; choosing a surface that captures the wire requires accounting for I_conduction, while choosing the gap surface requires the displacement term. Trigger conditions: the text contains Ampère–Maxwell forms lacking the μ0 I term, phrases like 'displacement current is the dominant term so we can write ∇×B = μ0 ε0 ∂E/∂t' or '∮B·dl = μ0 ε0 dΦ_E/dt' without region-specific justification, and the described loop/surface is outside the capacitor gap or can enclose/ intersect conductors. In such cases, mark a conceptual error: neglect of conduction current leads to incorrect B-fields.

rules.title: Incorrect use of London/superconducting relations for normal conductors
rules.description: Flags solutions to eddy-current or magnetic response problems in normal (Ohmic) conductors that invoke superconducting (London) relations or an algebraic proportionality between the induced magnetic field and the applied field. Specifically: (a) If the problem context describes a conducting/Ohmic thin film, finite conductivity σ, or a normal metal (and does not mention superconductivity), the verifier checks for use of London-type equations or keywords (e.g., 'London equation', 'penetration depth', 'λ_L', 'supercurrent', 'Meissner'), or relations like ∇^2 B = B/λ_L^2, J ∝ A, or B_ind ∝ B with a frequency-dependent algebraic factor. (b) It flags expressions of the form B_ind = F(σ, ω) B, e.g., B_ind = (μ0 σ)/(1 + i ω μ0 σ) B, which treat the magnetic response of a normal conductor as an instantaneous/algebraic proportionality rather than a diffusion/skin-depth phenomenon. (c) It checks that normal-conductor modeling uses Ohm's law J = σE together with Maxwell-Faraday and Ampère laws to yield magnetic diffusion ∂B/∂t = (1/μσ) ∇^2 B and skin depth δ = √(2/(μσ ω)), or equivalent boundary-value treatments (e.g., k–ω space, eddy-current damping, or image-dipole with v-dependent image parameters). If superconducting relations or purely algebraic B_ind ∝ B are used in place of diffusion/skin-depth for a normal conductor, the step is marked as a modeling error.

rules.title: Incorrect conductor potential modeled as k*q divided by separation distance
rules.description: Checks for modeling errors where the potential of a conducting sphere (or conductor) is written as V = k*q/r with r taken as the distance to another object (e.g., separation to a large sphere) rather than the conductor’s own radius or capacitance. Trigger conditions: (1) The solution context involves conductors/spheres and potential equalization (e.g., connecting spheres by a wire). (2) An equation appears of the form V = k*q/r, V_i = k*q_i/r, or similar; and r is described/defined as center-to-center distance, separation, distance to another sphere/object, or any external distance parameter, not the sphere radius or a capacitance quantity. (3) The solution omits or replaces the correct formulations V = q/C (for an isolated conductor) or the multi-conductor relation V_i = Σ_j P_ij q_j + V_ext (capacitance/potential-coefficient matrix). The rule flags these patterns because using the separation distance in the denominator is dimensionally and physically incorrect for conductor self-potential; it confuses point-charge Coulomb potential with conductor self-potential and ignores influence/capacitance coefficients in the presence of other conductors.

rules.title: Verify Coulomb's Law formula usage
rules.description: Ensure that the formula F = k * (|q1 * q2|) / r^2 is used correctly. This equation calculates the magnitude of the force between two point charges, where k is Coulomb's constant, q1 and q2 are the charges, and r is the distance between the charges.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the force is calculated using F = k * |q1 * q2| / r^2 and that all variables are correctly substituted. Ensure that the absolute value of the product of charges is used, the distance is squared, and the correct value of Coulomb's constant is applied.
common_errors: Forgetting to square the distance (r^2)
Using q1 * q2 instead of |q1 * q2|, thus missing the absolute value
Using an incorrect value for Coulomb's constant (k)

rules.title: Verify Electric Field formula usage
rules.description: Ensure that the electric field is calculated using E = F / q or E = k * |q| / r^2, where E is the electric field, F is the force experienced by a test charge q, and r is the distance from the source charge.
rules.check_logic: Check if the electric field magnitude is calculated using E = k * |q| / r^2 or derived from E = F / q. Verify that the absolute value of the charge is used, the distance is squared, and the correct relationships between force, charge, and field are applied.
common_errors: Forgetting to divide by q when using E = F / q
Not using the absolute value of the charge in the formula
Forgetting to square the distance in E = k * |q| / r^2

rules.title: Verify consistency of coordinate system in vector representation
rules.description: Make sure all electric force and field vectors are expressed in a consistent coordinate system (Cartesian, spherical, etc.), with proper consideration of components and angles.
rules.check_logic: Verify that vector components (e.g., x, y, z) are consistent with the chosen coordinate system and that angles are measured correctly relative to the axes. Ensure that conversions between coordinate systems, if any, are performed accurately.
common_errors: Mixing coordinate systems (e.g., Cartesian with spherical)
Incorrect calculation of vector components
Using angles in degrees when radians are required or vice versa

rules.title: Ensure geometric constraints are satisfied
rules.description: Confirm that the distance r between charges is positive and matches the stated configuration. Verify that charges are treated as point charges unless specified otherwise.
rules.check_logic: Check if r > 0 and consistent with the given geometry. Ensure charges are sufficiently small to approximate as point charges if Coulomb's Law is applied. Verify that the physical arrangement of charges matches the problem's description.
common_errors: Using a zero or negative distance in calculations
Applying Coulomb's Law to extended charges without proper treatment
Incorrect interpretation of the charges' physical arrangement

rules.title: Verify validity conditions for Coulomb's Law application
rules.description: Ensure Coulomb's Law is applied only under the assumption of stationary point charges in a vacuum or sufficiently low-medium dielectric constant environment.
rules.check_logic: Check if charges are stationary and point-like, and that the medium is either vacuum or has a specified permittivity ε consistent with the problem. Ensure that magnetic effects are not ignored if charges are moving.
common_errors: Applying Coulomb's Law to moving charges without considering magnetic effects
Using Coulomb's Law in a medium without adjusting for permittivity
Using it for non-point charges without additional approximations

rules.title: Verify application of superposition principle
rules.description: Ensure that the net electric field or force is calculated by vector addition of individual contributions from multiple charges, using E_net = ΣE_i or F_net = ΣF_i.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the contributions from all charges are calculated separately and summed as vectors, considering both magnitude and direction. Ensure that vector addition is performed correctly, including handling angles and components.
common_errors: Adding magnitudes instead of vectors when determining net field or force
Omitting contributions from one or more charges
Incorrect vector addition due to sign or angle errors

rules.title: Verify boundary conditions for electric fields
rules.description: Ensure that boundary conditions, such as the behavior of electric fields at the surface of conductors or at infinity, are correctly applied.
rules.check_logic: Check if the electric field inside a conductor is zero and that the field at the surface is perpendicular to the surface. Verify that the field approaches zero at infinity unless specified otherwise.
common_errors: Incorrect assumption about the electric field inside a conductor
Forgetting that the electric field is perpendicular to the surface of a conductor
Incorrect treatment of the field at infinity

rules.title: 有限长带电线场强对称性校验
rules.description:
触发条件：计算带电线段在空间任意点的场强 E 时
检查逻辑：校验中垂线仅有径向分量，延长线仅有轴向分量。非对称点（如端点平面）必存在两个分量，需通过角度或分量合成表达。
rules.check_logic: 校验中垂线仅有径向分量，延长线仅有轴向分量。非对称点（如端点平面）必存在两个分量，需通过角度或分量合成表达。
rules.trigger: 计算带电线段在空间任意点的场强 E 时

rules.title: 积分限与物理域一致性检查
rules.description:
触发条件：在计算连续分布电荷产生的场强，设定积分变量 x 和场点距离 r 时
检查逻辑：检查积分区间 [a, b] 是否包含场点坐标 r。若 r > b 或 r < a，积分函数不应在区间内发散；若包含，需讨论主值或物理意义。
rules.check_logic: 检查积分区间 [a, b] 是否包含场点坐标 r。若 r > b 或 r < a，积分函数不应在区间内发散；若包含，需讨论主值或物理意义。
rules.trigger: 在计算连续分布电荷产生的场强，设定积分变量 x 和场点距离 r 时

rules.title: 多边形内心场强对称性判定
rules.description:
触发条件：均匀带电多边形边界，求解内心（Incenter）处的场强
检查逻辑：检查各边对内心张角的几何对称性。若各边电荷密度相同且到内心距离相等，其场强矢量和遵循多边形外法线矢量和为零的性质。
rules.check_logic: 检查各边对内心张角的几何对称性。若各边电荷密度相同且到内心距离相等，其场强矢量和遵循多边形外法线矢量和为零的性质。
rules.trigger: 均匀带电多边形边界，求解内心（Incenter）处的场强

rules.title: Coupled RL ring current/phase must depend on both R and L
rules.description: Checks solutions for a solenoid–metal ring system with mutual inductance M, ring resistance R, and ring self-inductance L. The correct ring-loop KVL is L di_ring/dt + R i_ring = - M dI_solenoid/dt. Under sinusoidal drive I_solenoid(t) with angular frequency ω, the phasor relation must be I_ring/I_solenoid = - j ω M / (R + j ω L). The rule flags modeling errors when: (a) the final ring current is given solely as i_ring(t) = (M/R) dI_solenoid/dt or otherwise lacks dependence on L; (b) the frequency-domain transfer function denominator omits the j ω L term (uses only R); (c) the stated amplitude |I_ring| equals ω M |I_solenoid| / R, missing the √(R^2 + (ω L)^2) factor; (d) the phase difference δ is asserted to be ±90° or tan δ is independent of L, R, or ω; the correct dependence is tan δ proportional to ω L / R (sign may vary with conventions). If any of these conditions are present, mark the solution as an incorrect modeling of self-inductance in steady state.

rules.title: Characteristic scale miscast as a hard threshold
rules.description: This rule detects when a characteristic parameter (e.g., v0, ω0, τc, ℓ0) is incorrectly described as a hard threshold or critical point rather than a crossover scale in linear-response physics problems. It flags language and reasoning that imply abrupt or qualitative changes at the parameter value without a derived non-analytic mechanism. Checks include: (1) Phrasing such as 'below v0 the motion is significantly affected', 'critical velocity v0', 'above v0 behavior changes abruptly', 'threshold v0', or claims that an effect turns on/off at v0. (2) Absence of justification for a genuine threshold (instability, phase transition, nonlinearity) demonstrated by a governing equation that changes form, a divergence, or non-analyticity. (3) In magnetoquasistatic eddy-current/levitation contexts, ensure v0 is introduced as a material/geometry-dependent crossover constructed from film properties (e.g., conductivity σ, thickness d, permeability μ) and used to compare regimes (v ≪ v0 and v ≫ v0) with smooth, continuous scaling (e.g., power-law or rational dependence), not step-like behavior. The rule expects: explicit identification of v0 as a crossover scale; presentation of limiting behaviors with continuous interpolation; avoidance of threshold/critical wording unless accompanied by a derived mechanism (e.g., superconducting transition, Landau criterion). Flag solutions that portray v0 (or analogous scales) as a threshold below which motion is 'significantly affected' or that imply discontinuous regime change without a physical mechanism.

rules.title: Reject unjustified symmetry-based equality of edge currents in rotating cube with in-plane magnetic field
rules.description: For a rigid cube made of twelve equal resistive wires rotating in a uniform magnetic field B perpendicular to the rotation axis (so B lies in the abcd face plane), the field orientation (angle θ between B and a face diagonal, e.g., bd) generally breaks equal-current symmetry among face edges. This rule flags a solution if it asserts I_ba = I_ad or I_bc = I_cd (possibly with opposite sign) based purely on symmetry without: (1) computing the motional EMF/potential drop along each edge via v×B (or an equivalent flux-rate method) and solving for nodal potentials; and (2) exhibiting explicit θ dependence that includes both sinθ and cosθ components arising from projecting B onto the two face diagonals. The rule also flags any claim of such equalities that is stated for all θ without restricting to special symmetry alignments of B (e.g., B parallel to a side or a diagonal; θ ∈ {0°, 90°, 45°}). Equality may be accepted only if the solution demonstrates that the induced EMFs on the compared edges are identical under a stated symmetry condition or derives distinct θ-dependent currents otherwise. This catches incorrect symmetry arguments that ignore anisotropic EMF distribution on the abcd face in a general orientation.

rules.title: θ-dependence and symmetry of currents in rotating cube face must include both sinθ and cosθ with correct coefficient
rules.description:
Applicable to problems where a rigid cube of 12 uniform resistive wires (each resistance R, side length l) rotates uniformly with angular speed ω in a uniform magnetic field B, with the rotation axis through the cube’s center and perpendicular to the abcd face, and the magnetic field perpendicular to the axis. At an orientation where the diagonal bd makes angle θ with B, the currents through the four edges of the abcd face must satisfy specific θ-dependence, symmetry, and scaling. The verifier checks: 
- Dimensional and scaling check: Each current I must scale as (B l^2 ω / R) times a dimensionless function of θ. Missing l^2, missing ω, or missing division by R is flagged. 
- Functional form check: The θ-dependence must be a linear combination of sinθ and cosθ. Expressions depending only on sinθ or only on cosθ (e.g., I ∝ sinθ alone) are flagged. 
- Symmetry check: Due to face symmetry, I_ba = I_cd and I_ad = I_bc. Violations are flagged. 
- Coefficient check: For this geometry (cube with uniform rods, negligible self-inductance), the correct magnitude coefficient is √2/8. Large deviations (e.g., 1/2, 1/4, or other inconsistent constants) are flagged. 
- Exact reference forms: The expected currents are I_ba = (√2/8)(B l^2 ω / R)(cosθ − sinθ), I_ad = (√2/8)(B l^2 ω / R)(cosθ + sinθ), I_bc = (√2/8)(B l^2 ω / R)(cosθ + sinθ), I_cd = (√2/8)(B l^2 ω / R)(cosθ − sinθ). Any solution lacking the cosθ contributions or with incorrect numerical coefficients/relative signs fails this rule.

rules.title: Enforce J = n_V q_e v, correct units, and proper current–velocity direction
rules.description:
Purpose: Detect conflation of electron velocity with current direction and dimensional errors when expressing current density in Hall/Drude-type problems.

Scope: Applies when a problem defines carrier density n_V (per volume), charge q_e, and references a carrier velocity v (e.g., "if the electrons have velocity v at steady state, what is J?").

Checks:
- Constitutive relation check:
  - If the prompt gives or assumes a carrier velocity v, the solution must use J = n_V q_e v (vector form). Flag if J is given without v or without an equivalent velocity derived from forces/transport parameters.
- Dimensional consistency check for J:
  - Verify the final expression for J has units of A/m^2.
  - Flag expressions of the form J ∝ n_V e E (or n_V q_e E) that do not include a factor with dimensions of mobility (m^2/(V·s)), time (τ), mass (m_e), or a B-dependent term that yields a velocity (e.g., E×B/B^2). Examples to flag: J = −n_V e E ŷ, J = n_V e E.
  - Acceptable alternatives include J = n_V q_e v_drift with v_drift derived consistently (e.g., v_drift = μE with μ = q_e τ/m_e; or v_drift = E×B/B^2 for an E×B drift context), or J = σE with σ defined and dimensionally correct.
- Direction/sign logic check:
  - For a single carrier species, the current density vector must be parallel to q_e v. For electrons (q_e < 0), J is antiparallel to their velocity. Flag statements equating current direction to electron velocity (J ∥ v) for q_e < 0, or choosing the electron velocity direction solely because q_e is negative without explicit force analysis.
  - Red-flag phrases/equations: "electrons move in −ŷ because q_e < 0", "current flows in the same direction as electron motion for electrons", or any assignment of velocity direction based only on charge sign without using F = q_e(E + v × B).

Pass conditions:
- The solution states J = n_V q_e v when v is given.
- If J is expressed via fields, it includes a velocity-producing factor (e.g., μ, τ/m_e, 1/B factors yielding m/s) and reduces to A/m^2.

Fail examples this rule will catch:
- J = −n_V e E ŷ (units C·V/m^4, not A/m^2; replaces v with E with no mobility/time; conflates sign with velocity/current direction).
- Any expression for J that lacks v or a dimensionally correct surrogate leading to m/s.

rules.title: Use direct definition for current density when velocity is given
rules.description: Checks that when a problem explicitly states the carrier velocity v is given (e.g., 'If the electrons have velocity v at steady state') and asks for the current density J, the solution uses the direct definition J = n_V q_e v without attempting to derive v from forces or fields. Trigger conditions: the prompt mentions carrier number density (n or n_V), charge (q or q_e), provides a velocity v, and requests current density. Pass criteria: the final expression for J is stated as J = n q v (vector form acceptable, with correct sign for q_e) and uses only {n (or n_V), q (or q_e), v}. Fail/flag conditions: (a) the solution attempts to solve for v via dynamics (e.g., includes F = q(E + v × B), m_e dv/dt, mentions 'force balance', 'Lorentz force', or uses v × B), (b) the final J depends on additional variables like E, B, m_e, or time derivatives despite v being provided, or (c) J is not expressed in terms of n, q, and v. Implementation hints: detect phrases like 'given velocity v' or 'has velocity v' in the prompt; then parse the answer for an explicit J = n q v relation. If the only provided expression for J contains symbols outside {n, q, v} (e.g., E, B, m_e), or if the solution includes derivation steps to compute v from fields, flag it. Unit sanity check: J should have units (C/m^3)*(m/s). Do not apply if the prompt explicitly asks to compute v from forces before determining J.

rules.title: Incorrect sign in current–velocity relation for electrons
rules.description: Checks that the mapping from carrier drift velocity to current density uses the correct charge sign for electrons. Verification logic: (1) Identify the carrier type mentioned (e.g., 'electrons', 'electron gas'). (2) When carriers are electrons, ensure the relation j = n q v is applied with q = -e (electron charge), i.e., j = -n e v. (3) Flag solutions that write j = n e v (or j_x = n e v_x, j_y = n e v_y) for electrons without an explicit negative sign or without defining q = -e and using j = n q v. (4) Cross-check consistency: for Drude steady state with E along +x and no magnetic field, v_x should be v_x = -(e τ/m) E; the corresponding current must be j_x = n e^2 τ/m E (positive along E). If the solution derives j_x ∝ v_x with the same sign (e.g., j_x = n e v_x) for electrons, flag a sign error. (5) In magnetotransport cases, verify that j components are opposite in sign to the corresponding electron velocity components; if j_x and v_x or j_y and v_y appear with the same sign linkage for electrons, flag. This rule targets the common mistake of using the charge magnitude e instead of the signed electron charge q = -e when converting velocities to current density.

rules.title: Verify Ohm's Law Application
rules.description: Ohm's Law defines the relationship between current (I), voltage (V), and resistance (R): V = IR. It applies only to materials or components with linear, ohmic behavior (constant resistance).
rules.check_logic: Check if V = I * R in the solution and ensure the material is specified as ohmic. If the resistance varies with current or temperature, Ohm's Law cannot be applied directly.
common_errors: Assuming Ohm's Law applies to non-ohmic materials (e.g., diodes, transistors)
Incorrect rearrangement of the equation (e.g., using R = V * I instead of R = V / I)

rules.title: Validate Use of Resistance Formula
rules.description: The resistance of a uniform conductor is R = ρ * (L/A), where ρ is resistivity, L is length, and A is cross-sectional area. This formula applies to uniform, isotropic materials.
rules.check_logic: Verify if R is calculated as R = ρ * (L/A), and check that all variables are properly defined and used. Ensure the conductor is uniform and isotropic.
common_errors: Forgetting to include the cross-sectional area (A) in the denominator
Using incorrect units for resistivity, length, or area
Applying this formula to non-uniform or anisotropic materials

rules.title: Check Sign Convention for Current Direction
rules.description: Current direction is conventionally defined as the flow of positive charge. It is opposite to the direction of electron flow. Ensure that the chosen current direction is consistent throughout the solution.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the current direction matches the problem setup or stated assumptions. If using electron flow, ensure it is explicitly noted.
common_errors: Confusing the direction of electron flow with conventional current
Inconsistently assigning current direction in circuit diagrams

rules.title: Verify Power Dissipation Equation
rules.description: The power dissipated in a resistor is given by P = IV, P = I^2R, or P = V^2/R, depending on the known quantities. These are derived from Ohm's Law.
rules.check_logic: Ensure the correct power formula is used based on the available variables (I, V, R). Verify the consistency of dimensional units in the power calculation.
common_errors: Using the wrong power formula for the given variables
Forgetting to square the current or voltage when using P = I^2R or P = V^2/R
Unit mismatch, such as not converting milliamps to amps

rules.title: Apply Kirchhoff's Voltage and Current Laws
rules.description: Kirchhoff's Current Law (KCL): The sum of currents entering a junction equals the sum leaving it. Kirchhoff's Voltage Law (KVL): The sum of voltage drops in a closed loop equals zero.
rules.check_logic: Verify that all currents at a junction satisfy KCL and all voltage drops around a loop satisfy KVL. Ensure consistent sign conventions for current and voltage.
common_errors: Missing terms in the summation for KCL or KVL
Incorrect sign convention for voltage drops or current directions
Failure to account for all branches in a circuit

rules.title: Verify Resistance Dependence on Temperature
rules.description: The resistance of a material changes with temperature, typically modeled as R(T) = R_0[1 + α(T - T_0)], where α is the temperature coefficient of resistance. This is crucial for non-room-temperature conditions.
rules.check_logic: Check if temperature dependence is accounted for when the problem involves significant temperature changes or explicitly mentions temperature effects.
common_errors: Ignoring the temperature dependence of resistance when significant
Using an incorrect value for the temperature coefficient (α)
Assuming resistance is constant without justification

rules.title: Check Circuit Boundary Conditions
rules.description: Ensure that all boundary conditions, such as total supplied voltage, current, or resistance, are satisfied for the entire circuit. Verify the sum of all branch currents matches the total current for parallel circuits, and total resistance is computed correctly.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the total voltage across a series circuit equals the sum of individual voltage drops, and the current splits correctly in parallel circuits.
common_errors: Incorrectly summing resistances for parallel or series configurations
Ignoring total supplied voltage or current constraints
Misapplying current or voltage division rules

rules.title: Apply Superposition Theorem
rules.description: The superposition theorem states that in a linear circuit with multiple sources, the current or voltage at any element is the algebraic sum of the currents or voltages produced by each source independently.
rules.check_logic: Verify that each independent current or voltage source is considered one at a time, with all other sources turned off (replacing voltage sources with short circuits and current sources with open circuits). Then, check that the results for each source are summed to find the total response.
common_errors: Forgetting to turn off sources aside from the one being considered
Incorrectly replacing sources (e.g., using open circuit for voltage source)
Failing to sum individual contributions correctly

rules.title: 连续介质电阻积分法
rules.description:
触发条件：计算具有特定几何对称性（球、柱）的非均匀或连续导电介质电阻
检查逻辑：验证是否通过微分电阻 dR = ρ * dl / A(r) 进行积分，并确认积分上下限与几何边界一致。
rules.check_logic: 验证是否通过微分电阻 dR = ρ * dl / A(r) 进行积分，并确认积分上下限与几何边界一致。
rules.trigger: 计算具有特定几何对称性（球、柱）的非均匀或连续导电介质电阻

rules.title: 区分结构间距与元件长度
rules.description:
触发条件：题目同时给出平行导轨间距（如h）和横向元件分布间距（如L）时
检查逻辑：核实电阻计算公式R=ρl/A中的l是否对应跨接导轨的物理长度，而非沿导轨方向的分布间距。
rules.check_logic: 核实电阻计算公式R=ρl/A中的l是否对应跨接导轨的物理长度，而非沿导轨方向的分布间距。
rules.trigger: 题目同时给出平行导轨间距（如h）和横向元件分布间距（如L）时

rules.title: 微观参数关联检查
rules.description:
触发条件：题目给出电子数密度n、质量m、电荷e等微观量用于宏观电阻估算时
检查逻辑：检查是否需通过经典电子导电模型（如德鲁德模型变体）将宏观电阻 R 或自感 L 与微观惯性质量关联，特别是涉及单匝线圈动能电感时。
rules.check_logic: 检查是否需通过经典电子导电模型（如德鲁德模型变体）将宏观电阻 R 或自感 L 与微观惯性质量关联，特别是涉及单匝线圈动能电感时。
rules.trigger: 题目给出电子数密度n、质量m、电荷e等微观量用于宏观电阻估算时

rules.title: 超导电流衰减建模
rules.description:
触发条件：涉及超导线圈电流长期保持、电阻上限估算或电流变化精度时
检查逻辑：必须使用自感衰减模型 I(t)=I0*exp(-Rt/L)，利用 ΔI/I ≈ Rt/L 建立电阻 R 与观测时间 t、电流精度 ΔI 的不等式关系。
rules.check_logic: 必须使用自感衰减模型 I(t)=I0*exp(-Rt/L)，利用 ΔI/I ≈ Rt/L 建立电阻 R 与观测时间 t、电流精度 ΔI 的不等式关系。
rules.trigger: 涉及超导线圈电流长期保持、电阻上限估算或电流变化精度时

rules.title: 无穷远边界电阻收敛性
rules.description:
触发条件：题目要求计算外径 b 趋于无穷大时的电阻值
检查逻辑：检查结果是否满足 1/b 项趋于 0，且最终表达式的量纲为 [电阻]（即 [电阻率]/[长度]）。
rules.check_logic: 检查结果是否满足 1/b 项趋于 0，且最终表达式的量纲为 [电阻]（即 [电阻率]/[长度]）。
rules.trigger: 题目要求计算外径 b 趋于无穷大时的电阻值

rules.title: Current from single charge in cyclotron motion must include q and scale as q^2 B/m
rules.description: Trigger when a solution derives the electric current from a single charged particle moving in a circular orbit in a uniform magnetic field (keywords: cyclotron motion, Larmor frequency, omega = |q|B/m, period T = 2πm/|q|B). Checks: 1) Require the base relation I = q/T = q·omega/(2π). Flag an error if I is set to 1/T or omega/(2π) without the factor q. 2) Upon substituting omega = |q|B/m, enforce |I| = |q|^2 B/(2π m); flag expressions proportional to |q| B/(2π m) or B/m as missing a factor of |q|. 3) Dimensional consistency: current must have units of charge per time; expressions like |q| B/(2π m) or B/m yield 1/s and are dimensionally incorrect for current. 4) If the particle is specified as an electron (q = −e) and a signed current is reported, require I = −(e^2 B)/(2π m); otherwise allow absolute value but still require q^2 dependence. This rule detects missing-charge-factor and unit errors in currents derived from cyclotron motion.

rules.title: Verify ω = eB/m substitutions and dimensional consistency
rules.description: This rule checks algebraic substitutions and unit consistency when the cyclotron frequency ω is introduced (ω = e B / m) in magnetotransport derivations (e.g., Drude model with Hall effect). It targets errors where ω, e, B, m, and τ are combined incorrectly, leading to wrong powers or dimensions. The verifier should: 1) Detect declarations or uses of ω = e B / m. 2) Validate common rewrites: - ω τ → (e B τ) / m (unitless). - (ω τ)^2 → (e^2 B^2 τ^2) / m^2 (unitless). - 1 / (ω^2 τ) → m^2 / (e^2 B^2 τ) (units of time). Any alternate forms must be algebraically equivalent and dimensionally identical. 3) Flag explicit incorrect substitutions, especially: - 1 / (ω^2 τ) = m / (e τ B^2) (incorrect; units C·s/kg vs s). - Replacing ω^2 with (e B / m) (missing square). - Multiplying numerator/denominator by e B (or m) in a way that changes powers of B or m (e.g., turning B into B^2 or altering m^±1 to m^±2) without corresponding factors elsewhere. 4) Perform dimensional checks for each substitution: - ω has units s^-1, τ is s, so 1/(ω^2 τ) must have units s. - m/(e τ B^2) has units C·s/kg, hence not equal to 1/(ω^2 τ). If an equality relates expressions with mismatched SI units, flag as dimensionally inconsistent. 5) Verify that factors in expressions like 1 + (ω τ)^2 become 1 + (e B τ / m)^2, preserving the square on the whole ratio. 6) In any factorization step intended to simplify denominators/numerators (e.g., multiplying by e B), confirm that the resulting dependence on B, m, and e remains algebraically consistent with ω = e B / m. If any of the above checks fail, mark the step as an algebraic/dimensional substitution error and provide diagnostics indicating the correct form (e.g., 1/(ω^2 τ) should be m^2/(e^2 B^2 τ), not m/(e τ B^2)).

rules.title: Lorentz force direction and cyclotron motion consistency
rules.description: Checks that solutions to charged-particle motion in a uniform magnetic field correctly state and use the direction of the Lorentz force and the resulting kinematics. The rule flags any of the following: (1) Asserting that the magnetic force has a fixed direction (e.g., 'vertical' or 'horizontal') without deriving it from F = q (v × B), which must be perpendicular to the instantaneous velocity and to B at all times. (2) Claiming 'centripetal acceleration in the vertical direction' or similar phrasing suggesting a constant-axis acceleration, rather than acceleration toward the center of circular motion in the plane perpendicular to B with a direction that rotates with the velocity. (3) Misidentifying which velocity components oscillate: in a uniform B, the component of velocity parallel to B is constant (no oscillation), while the components perpendicular to B undergo sinusoidal/circular motion at the cyclotron frequency ω_c = |q|B/m (period T = 2πm/|q|B). The rule also checks consistency between any stated oscillation of v_x or v_y and the orientation of B: only components lying in the plane perpendicular to B may oscillate at ω_c; a component parallel to B must not be described as oscillating. If any of these inconsistencies are present, the solution is flagged as conceptually incorrect.

rules.title: Cyclotron formula misuse in interacting multi-particle magnetic-field problems
rules.description: Flag solutions that apply single-particle cyclotron relations (e.g., r = m v/(|q| B), ω_c = |q| B/m, or mv^2/r = |q| v B) to each particle independently in a system with multiple charged particles when interactions or constraints are present (e.g., constant separation, mutual Coulomb forces, rigid linkage). The rule triggers if the solution: (a) assumes circular motion solely from the Lorentz force and equates mv^2/r = |q| v B for an individual particle; or (b) asserts identical angular velocities because q/m is the same; or (c) uses r = m v/(|q| B) or ω_c = |q| B/m to deduce speed/trajectory; without explicitly incorporating additional interaction/constraint forces into the radial force balance or justifying their neglect/cancellation. Acceptable justifications include: the problem explicitly states interactions are neglected; a quantitative argument showing interaction forces are negligible compared to |q| v B; or a correct decomposition into center-of-mass and relative motion demonstrating that internal forces do not alter the effective centripetal acceleration. If none of these are present, the use of single-particle cyclotron formulas is deemed a modeling error and should be flagged.

rules.title: Incorrect inversion of momentum–curvature relation in magnetic fields
rules.description: Checks that solutions preserve the correct monotonic relation r = p/(|q|B) for a charged particle in a uniform magnetic field. The cyclotron radius r increases with momentum p; higher p means less curvature (larger r). Flag solutions that: (1) assert or imply that minimum momentum corresponds to maximum radius, or that higher momentum curves more strongly (smaller r); (2) apply containment/looping criteria with reversed inequalities—for a detector of radius R, to loop repeatedly inside requires r ≤ R, i.e., p ≤ |q|BR, not p ≥ |q|BR; (3) label p = |q|BR as a 'minimum momentum to loop' rather than the maximum momentum that still loops; (4) equate 'avoid looping' with p ≤ |q|BR. Trigger if text contains phrases like 'minimum momentum corresponds to largest radius', 'greater momentum gives tighter curvature', or if computed thresholds use the wrong inequality direction relative to r = p/(|q|B) and r ≤ R.

rules.title: Gauss’s law: Correct flux computation for cylindrical Gaussian surfaces
rules.description: This rule verifies that, when Gauss’s law is applied using a cylindrical Gaussian surface, the electric flux is computed from the field component normal to each surface element. It flags solutions that erroneously take the flux through the cylinder’s lateral area as E*(2π r h) for a field aligned with the cylinder axis (e.g., a vertical atmospheric electric field). Checks: (1) If the field is described as vertical/axial or aligned with the cylinder axis, the lateral surface contribution must be zero because E · n_side = 0; any nonzero lateral term or Φ expressed as E*(2π r h) is incorrect. (2) The total flux must be through the end caps only, with Φ = A*(E_bottom − E_top) and A = π r^2, respecting outward normals (top cap normal upward, bottom cap normal downward). (3) Flag use of Φ = E*A with A taken as the total or lateral surface area without resolving E · n and surface orientation. (4) Allow lateral flux terms only if the solution explicitly justifies a non-axial field component (E has a radial component relative to the cylinder) or a tilted cylinder such that E · n_side ≠ 0. The rule targets modeling errors where symmetry and orientation in Gauss’s law are misapplied, especially in atmospheric charge density contexts.

rules.title: Ensure sum of voltages in a closed loop equals zero
rules.description: Kirchhoff's Voltage Law (KVL) states that the algebraic sum of all voltages around a closed loop in a circuit must equal zero. This is derived from the conservation of energy principle in electrical circuits.
rules.check_logic: Sum of voltage drops and gains across all components in a closed loop must equal zero: ΣV = 0.
common_errors: Forgetting to include the polarity of voltage sources or resistors
Incorrectly summing voltage drops (e.g., forgetting negative signs for voltage drops)
Omitting a component in the loop equation

rules.title: Ensure sum of currents at a junction is zero
rules.description: Kirchhoff's Current Law (KCL) states that the total current entering a junction must equal the total current leaving the junction. This follows from the conservation of electric charge.
rules.check_logic: Sum of currents entering and leaving a junction must be zero: ΣI_in = ΣI_out.
common_errors: Mislabeling the direction of currents at a junction
Neglecting to include all branches connected to a junction
Incorrect signs for current entering or leaving

rules.title: Verify Ohm's Law for resistive components
rules.description: Ohm's Law states that the voltage across a resistor is directly proportional to the current flowing through it: V = IR.
rules.check_logic: For each resistive component, check if V = IR holds true.
common_errors: Using incorrect resistance values from the problem statement
Forgetting to account for series or parallel combinations of resistors
Incorrect unit conversion (e.g., kilo-ohms to ohms)

rules.title: Ensure correct resistor combination rules are applied
rules.description: Resistors in series add directly (R_eq = R1 + R2 + ...), while resistors in parallel combine as reciprocals (1/R_eq = 1/R1 + 1/R2 + ...).
rules.check_logic: Check if equivalent resistance calculations for series or parallel combinations are correct.
common_errors: Using series formula for parallel resistors or vice versa
Forgetting to take the reciprocal when calculating equivalent resistance for parallel resistors
Misidentifying which resistors are in series or parallel

rules.title: Ensure power conservation in the circuit
rules.description: The total power supplied by voltage sources must equal the total power dissipated by resistors and other elements in the circuit.
rules.check_logic: Sum of power supplied (ΣP_supply = ΣV_source * I) must equal sum of power dissipated (ΣP_dissipated = ΣI^2 * R).
common_errors: Forgetting to square the current in power dissipation calculation
Misapplying the power formula for voltage sources
Ignoring power contributions from all elements in the circuit

rules.title: Verify proper sign convention usage for voltages and currents
rules.description: When applying KVL or Ohm's Law, the sign of the voltage drop or current must be consistent with the chosen direction of traversal or assumed current flow.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that voltage drops across resistors are consistent with the assumed current direction and that voltage gains are correctly identified.
common_errors: Incorrectly assigning signs to voltage drops or gains
Using inconsistent current directions for different components
Forgetting to reverse signs when changing the traversal direction in a loop

rules.title: 倍数增量语义解析
rules.description:
