rules.title: 感应磁矩与磁场变化率方向一致性
rules.description:
触发条件：计算由均匀磁场变化率 B_dot 产生的感应磁矩 μ
检查逻辑：根据楞次定律，非铁磁性球壳的感应磁矩 μ 应与 -B_dot 方向平行（或在其投影方向上），需检查分量符号是否符合阻碍磁通变化的物理本质。
rules.check_logic: 根据楞次定律，非铁磁性球壳的感应磁矩 μ 应与 -B_dot 方向平行（或在其投影方向上），需检查分量符号是否符合阻碍磁通变化的物理本质。
rules.trigger: 计算由均匀磁场变化率 B_dot 产生的感应磁矩 μ

rules.title: Require integration of provided discharge current curve for charge/energy estimates
rules.description: Checks that, when a problem provides an idealized current-time curve I(t) (or an explicit I(t) function) for a lightning/discharge scenario, the solution computes total charge via Q = ∫ I(t) dt (i.e., uses the area under the given curve) and derives energy using U ≈ ∫ V I dt ≈ V × Q with V taken from the provided field/geometry (e.g., V ≈ E0 × h). Flags modeling errors where the solver ignores the given curve and instead inserts ad hoc 'typical' constants such as an average current (e.g., ~30 kA) and a pulse duration (e.g., ~30 μs) that are not justified by the provided inputs, or computes Q as I × Δt without referencing the curve. Acceptable solutions must explicitly use or approximate the integral of the provided I(t) and tie V to given quantities; use of external nominal lightning parameters in place of the problem’s curve/inputs triggers this rule.

rules.title: Line-charge electric field magnitude consistency (power-of-ten check)
rules.description: Checks numerical evaluations of the electric field around a long straight charged wire computed via Gauss's law for large errors due to mishandled powers of ten. The expected magnitude outside the wire is E(r) = λ / (2π ε0 r), where λ is the linear charge density and ε0 ≈ 8.854×10^-12 C^2·N^-1·m^-2. The verifier should: (1) Detect that the solution uses a cylindrical Gaussian surface and a line charge model. (2) Extract λ from the problem/solution (e.g., λ = 4.4×10^-11 C·m^-1) and use ε0 unless the solution specifies a different value. (3) Compute the coefficient k = λ / (2π ε0); for λ = 4.4×10^-11 C·m^-1, k ≈ 0.79. (4) For any stated radii r (e.g., r0 = 1×10^-6 m, b_max = 1×10^-4 m) at which the solution reports numerical E values, compute E_expected = k / r. (5) Compare reported E_reported to E_expected via ratio R = E_reported / E_expected. (6) If R is outside [1/3, 3], flag a magnitude inconsistency; if R ≤ 0.1 or R ≥ 10, flag as likely power-of-ten error. Example target values for λ = 4.4×10^-11: E(1×10^-6 m) ≈ 7.9×10^5 N/C; E(1×10^-4 m) ≈ 7.9×10^3 N/C. Reported values like 8.0×10^4 N/C or 8.0 N/C would be flagged. This rule specifically catches errors where the analytic form is correct (E ∝ 1/r) but numerical substitutions produce wrong orders of magnitude due to exponent mishandling.

rules.title: Loop field direction and vector/time-averaging in rotating ring + Earth field
rules.description: This rule verifies correct handling of the direction and time dependence of the magnetic field produced by a conducting loop at its center when the loop is in a vertical plane and rotates about a vertical axis in Earth's magnetic field. The checker should enforce the following: (1) Direction of loop field: The magnetic field at the center of a current loop must be stated as along the loop’s normal (perpendicular to the loop’s plane). For a vertically oriented ring, this field is horizontal. Flag an error if the solution claims the loop’s field at the center is vertical or otherwise misaligned with the loop’s normal. (2) Rotation of the loop field: If the ring rotates about the vertical axis, the loop normal (and thus the loop’s field direction at the center) rotates in the horizontal plane with the same angular velocity. Flag an error if the solution treats the loop’s field direction as fixed while the ring rotates. (3) Relation to Earth’s horizontal field: The loop’s horizontal field is not generically perpendicular to Earth’s horizontal field; their relative angle changes with time as the loop rotates. Flag an error if the solution assumes orthogonality (e.g., combines fields using sqrt(B_E^2 + B_loop^2) or states B_loop ⟂ B_E,H without justification). (4) Proper vector and time averaging: The deviation angle must be based on the time-averaged horizontal vector sum of Earth’s fixed horizontal field and the loop’s rotating horizontal field over a rotation period. Flag an error if the solution averages magnitudes instead of vectors, ignores time averaging, or computes the angle from a static scalar ratio (e.g., tan(alpha) = B_loop/B_E) without accounting for the rotating, possibly sign-changing loop contribution. Detection cues for violations include phrases like “perpendicular to Earth’s field,” “vertical field at the center of the loop” for a vertical ring, using Pythagorean addition of magnitudes, or omission of any mention of the rotating loop normal and time-averaged vector sum.

rules.title: Validate inductance model for a single-turn circular loop
rules.description: This rule checks the modeling of the self-inductance L of a single-turn circular wire loop (ring) of radius r made from thin wire of radius a (diameter d). It flags solutions that set L to μ0 r / 2 or otherwise model L ∝ μ0 r with an O(1) coefficient that lacks the required π or logarithmic dependence. Specifically: (1) If the solution derives L directly from the center-field expression B_center = μ0 I/(2r) and either (a) omits flux integration (Φ = ∫ B dA) or (b) computes L = Φ/I as μ0 r/2 (missing at least a factor of π), flag a modeling error. A crude but acceptable area-flux estimate yields L ≈ (μ0 π r)/2. (2) For thin loops (r/a ≳ 10), a more accurate expression is L ≈ μ0 r [ln(8r/a) − 2]; using an L value that is much smaller than this (e.g., by a factor > 2) indicates a significant modeling error. (3) Implementation guidance: compute c = L/(μ0 r). If c < π/2 × 0.9 ≈ 1.41, flag "undervalued inductance". When r/a ≥ 10, also compute L_thin = μ0 r [ln(8r/a) − 2]; if L < 0.5 × L_thin, flag the error. This rule is designed to catch the specific mistake of taking L = μ0 r / 2 from B_center, which misses at least a factor of π and leads to an underestimated inductance and an incorrect resistivity bound.

rules.title: Magnetic Lorentz force must include B factor and correct components
rules.description: This rule verifies the magnetic part of the Lorentz force in solutions that involve charges moving in a uniform magnetic field. It checks that the force is written as F_m = q (v × B), not q (v × 6B̂) or similar forms that drop the scalar field magnitude. For fields specified as B ẑ, it expects component relations F_x = q B v_y, F_y = - q B v_x, and F_z = 0. The rule flags: (a) any expression for the magnetic force or its components that lacks the multiplicative factor B; (b) force expressions that are independent of B or fail the dimensional consistency check (force must scale as q·v·B); (c) limiting-case violations where B → 0 does not yield F_m → 0; and (d) incorrect orientation/sign in the x–y components relative to v × B. This catches errors such as writing F_m = q (v × ẑ) or producing component equations without B, which lead to dimensional inconsistency and incorrect dynamics.

rules.title: Sign consistency in steady-state Lorentz + drag for electrons (E along x, B along z)
rules.description: For a 2D electron gas with E = E i, B = B k, and linear drag Fs = -m v / τ, steady-state force balance FE + FB + Fs = 0 must yield component equations: x: -e E - e v_y B - (m/τ) v_x = 0; y: +e v_x B - (m/τ) v_y = 0. This rule verifies that: (1) the drag terms in both components carry a negative sign (−(m/τ) v_x, −(m/τ) v_y); (2) the magnetic terms follow from q(v × B) with q = −e, i × k = −j and j × k = i, giving −e v_y B in the x-equation and +e v_x B in the y-equation; (3) the electric term in x is −e E and there is no electric term in y. If the student’s component equations include sign flips such as +(m/τ) v_x in the x-equation or −e v_x B in the y-equation, the rule flags a logic/sign error in the force-balance setup, which will propagate to the computed current densities.

rules.title: Lorentz force must use vector form and perpendicular velocity component
rules.description:
This rule checks for conceptual misuse of the Lorentz force where a solution replaces the vector expression F = q (v × B) with a scalar component such as F = q v_x B (or F = q v_y B, etc.) without explicitly identifying the velocity component perpendicular to the magnetic field. The rule flags solutions that: 
- Write the magnetic force as F = q v_x B, F = q B v_x, F_x = q v_x B, a = (q v_x B)/m, or similar, unless there is a clear, justified mapping that v_x is the perpendicular component v_perp relative to B.
- Use the scalar form F = q v B without mentioning the geometric dependence (sin φ) or explicitly defining v_perp, when the velocity is not stated to be strictly perpendicular to B.
- State or imply that the magnetic force depends on a specific Cartesian component (e.g., “B is perpendicular to v_x” or “force depends on v_x”) instead of the component of velocity perpendicular to B.
- Derive cyclotron relations (ω_c = qB/m, T = 2πm/(qB), radius r = m v_perp/(qB)) using an incorrect component (e.g., substituting v_x for v_perp) without geometric justification.
The rule passes when the solution uses the full vector form q (v × B) and, for magnitudes, correctly identifies v_perp (e.g., v_perp = v sin φ, or notes φ = 90° so v_perp = v), with clear reasoning about the orientation of v and B.

rules.title: Incorrect v×B components for azimuthal-only magnetic field
rules.description: This rule verifies the magnetic part of the Lorentz force components when the magnetic field is stated or implicitly used as purely azimuthal in cylindrical/toroidal coordinates (B = B_phi e_phi, with B_r = 0 and B_z = 0). The cross product v×B must be evaluated using the standard orthonormal basis relations e_r×e_phi = e_z, e_phi×e_z = e_r, e_z×e_r = e_phi. Under these conditions, the magnetic force components must be: F_r = -q v_z B_phi, F_phi = 0, F_z = +q v_r B_phi. The rule flags the following issues: (1) Any nonzero phi component attributed to the magnetic force (e.g., terms proportional to v_r B_phi, v_z B_phi, v_phi B_phi, or curvature factors like B_phi/R0) when B_r = B_z = 0; (2) Incorrect r or z components, including sign errors, missing terms, or inclusion of v_phi in F_r or F_z; (3) Use of a 'dominant term' or curvature-based approximation to justify a nonzero magnetic F_phi when B has only an azimuthal component; (4) Introduction of coordinate-basis derivative or scale-factor terms into the cross product itself (the cross product is algebraic in the instantaneous orthonormal basis and does not generate connection terms). This rule only constrains the magnetic contribution q v×B; it permits additional phi components arising from an explicitly present electric field E (which must be clearly separated from the magnetic term). It also accepts equivalent notation for the azimuthal direction (e.g., e_phi, phi-hat, azimuthal). The check should trigger whenever the solution states or uses B_r = B_z = 0 and yields F_phi ≠ 0 from the magnetic term, or produces F_r/F_z inconsistent with F_r = -q v_z B_phi and F_z = +q v_r B_phi.

rules.title: Flux continuity in high-μ magnetic circuits (Gauss's law / Kirchhoff’s flux law)
rules.description: Checks that solutions to magnetostatic circuit problems with high magnetic permeability and negligible external field (B ≈ 0 outside) enforce magnetic-flux continuity. Specifically: (1) Apply Gauss’s law for magnetism (∇·B = 0) so that flux is conserved: the total flux through any series cross-section of a closed ferromagnetic path is the same. (2) At junctions (nodes) in ferromagnetic networks, use the magnetic-circuit analogue of Kirchhoff’s current law: sum of fluxes entering a node equals the sum leaving (no flux is created or destroyed). (3) For comparisons of total flux carried by permanent magnets versus ferromagnetic pieces along the same closed circuit, require Φ_F / Φ_C = 1 (independent of geometry, symmetry, or number of elements). Flag solutions that: - assert or compute Φ_F / Φ_C ≠ 1 or make it depend on the number/arrangement of blocks; - treat flux as being created/annihilated at spheres/nodes (violating ∇·B = 0); - sum per-magnet fluxes without enforcing continuity through connected ferromagnetic elements; - rely only on symmetry arguments for flux distribution without invoking flux conservation. This rule detects conceptual errors where flux continuity is not respected in high-μ, leakage-free magnetic circuits.

rules.title: Unit flux ratio in closed, non-leaky magnetic circuits
rules.description: Check that in problems explicitly stating a closed ferromagnetic contour with all magnetic field lines confined inside the material (e.g., high magnetic permeability and B=0 outside), the magnetic flux is continuous and identical through series-connected components along the same path. Therefore, any ratio of flux between a permanent magnet segment and an adjacent ferromagnetic segment in the same closed loop must equal 1. Flag solutions that compute Φ_F / Φ_C (or analogous flux ratios between series parts) as values ≠ 1 (e.g., 1/2, 1/3) unless the solution explicitly identifies and correctly analyzes parallel branching paths in the magnetic circuit. This rule targets errors where flux is incorrectly 'split' among multiple symmetric edges without actual branching, as in tetrahedral assemblies, where the correct result is Φ_F / Φ_C = 1.

rules.title: Nonrelativistic moving dipole: source B-field must be velocity-independent
rules.description: Checks that, in problems describing a permanent magnetic dipole with fixed moment m moving at constant nonrelativistic velocity (v << c), the magnetic field of the dipole used as the source field does not contain explicit velocity dependence. The correct source field in the lab frame is the static dipole field evaluated at the instantaneous position R(t)=R0+vt: B(r,t)=μ0/(4π)[(3(m·r̂)r̂ − m)/r^3] with r = r_obs − R(t), and no factors of v appear in its amplitude or tensor structure. The rule flags solutions that insert v directly into the source B expression, e.g., B ∝ v, Bz ∝ v/h^3, or terms like m × (r × v)/r^3 in B. Allowed velocity dependence pertains only to kinematics (time argument via R(t)) and to the conductor’s response (induced E, eddy currents, forces/drag), not to the static form of the source B. Exceptions: explicitly relativistic treatments that state v is comparable to c and use Lorentz-transformed fields; accelerated motion (radiation) or time-varying dipole moment m(t); and electric-field expressions containing v × B. Trigger indicators for flagging include explicit v appearing in the magnetic dipole field formula, claims that the dipole’s B scales linearly with v, or attributions of Lorentz enhancement of B with v in nonrelativistic, constant-velocity contexts.

rules.title: Verify magnetic dipole moment calculation
rules.description: The magnetic dipole moment of a current loop is given by the equation μ = I × A, where I is the current and A is the area vector (A = area × normal unit vector). Ensure the direction of the dipole moment follows the right-hand rule.
rules.check_logic: Check if μ = I × A is used, ensuring current magnitude and area are consistent with their respective units (Amperes, square meters). Verify that the direction of μ is perpendicular to the plane of the loop and follows the right-hand rule.
common_errors: Using incorrect magnitude for current or area
Not applying the right-hand rule for the direction of μ
Forgetting to include the normal vector direction in the area calculation

rules.title: Check magnetic field from a dipole formula
rules.description: The magnetic field due to a dipole at a point in space is derived from B = (μ₀ / 4π) × [(3(μ·r̂)r̂ - μ) / r³], where μ is the magnetic dipole moment, r̂ is the unit vector pointing from the dipole to the observation point, and r is the distance. This applies only for r >> dipole size.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the formula for B is used correctly, with proper vector operations, and ensure r is much larger than the size of the dipole. Confirm that the unit vector r̂ is correctly normalized.
common_errors: Forgetting the r³ factor in the denominator
Incorrectly calculating dot and cross products between vectors
Using the formula for distances comparable to the dipole size
Not normalizing the unit vector r̂

rules.title: Validate sign conventions for coordinate systems
rules.description: The direction of the magnetic dipole moment μ and magnetic field B is determined by standard sign conventions, typically using the right-hand rule for current loops or coordinate systems like Cartesian or spherical coordinates.
rules.check_logic: Check that all directions of vectors (μ, B) are consistent with the right-hand rule. Ensure the chosen coordinate system (Cartesian, spherical, or cylindrical) is explicitly stated and consistently applied throughout the problem.
common_errors: Using left-hand rule instead of the right-hand rule
Mixing Cartesian and spherical coordinate systems without proper transformation
Incorrectly defining unit vectors in spherical or cylindrical systems

rules.title: Ensure boundary conditions for magnetic materials
rules.description: At the boundary between two magnetic materials, the tangential components of H (magnetic field intensity) are continuous, and the normal components of B (magnetic flux density) follow the relation B₁n/μ₁ = B₂n/μ₂.
rules.check_logic: Verify continuity conditions for the tangential component of H and the normal component of B. Ensure proper use of material permeabilities and confirm that the boundary is clearly defined.
common_errors: Neglecting the continuity of H's tangential components
Not accounting for the ratio of B₁n and B₂n based on material permeability
Confusing the roles of H and B in the boundary conditions

rules.title: Validate energy stored in a magnetic dipole in an external field
rules.description: The potential energy of a magnetic dipole μ in an external magnetic field B is given by U = -μ·B. This is a scalar product, and the energy depends on the relative orientation of μ and B.
rules.check_logic: Verify that U = -μ·B is used, with the correct scalar product and orientation between μ and B. Ensure the angle between μ and B is correctly calculated.
common_errors: Forgetting the negative sign in U = -μ·B
Using vector multiplication instead of scalar multiplication
Incorrectly calculating the angle between μ and B

rules.title: Verify hysteresis loop characteristics
rules.description: The hysteresis loop of a magnetic material shows the relationship between B and H during magnetization and demagnetization. Key values like coercivity, retentivity, and saturation magnetization should be correctly identified.
rules.check_logic: Check if the hysteresis loop is correctly plotted and interpreted. Ensure values for coercivity, retentivity, and saturation are appropriately labeled and measured. Confirm that the loop shape matches the expected behavior for the material type.
common_errors: Mislabeling or misinterpreting coercivity and retentivity
Incorrectly plotting the hysteresis loop
Neglecting the saturation magnetization value
Failing to account for material-specific loop characteristics

rules.title: Check validity conditions for magnetic dipole approximation
rules.description: The magnetic dipole approximation assumes the observation point is far from the dipole compared to the size of the dipole. This condition is essential for the formulas to hold.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that the distance r from the dipole to the observation point satisfies r >> size of the dipole. Confirm that the dipole size is explicitly stated or estimated.
common_errors: Applying the dipole approximation to points too close to the dipole
Ignoring the spatial extent of the dipole in the approximation
Using dipole formulas without verifying the far-field condition

rules.title: Verify nonlinearity in magnetic materials
rules.description: Magnetic materials often exhibit nonlinear behavior, where B is not proportional to H. This is especially true near saturation or in ferromagnetic materials.
rules.check_logic: Check if the nonlinearity of the B-H curve is accounted for, particularly near saturation. Ensure that any approximations assume linearity only in the appropriate range.
common_errors: Assuming linearity in the B-H relationship near saturation
Neglecting hysteresis effects in ferromagnetic materials
Using linear approximations without specifying the valid range

rules.title: 磁源模型极性校验
rules.description:
触发条件：题目涉及两个磁单极子（magnetic monopoles）或磁偶极子计算时
检查逻辑：检查是否默认磁荷为等量异号（q_m 与 -q_m）。若无明确说明为同号，应按偶极子模型处理，磁场贡献应为矢量相减而非绝对值相加。
rules.check_logic: 检查是否默认磁荷为等量异号（q_m 与 -q_m）。若无明确说明为同号，应按偶极子模型处理，磁场贡献应为矢量相减而非绝对值相加。
rules.trigger: 题目涉及两个磁单极子（magnetic monopoles）或磁偶极子计算时

rules.title: Sign consistency of external force vs magnetic drag in sliding-rod circuits
rules.description: Checks that, in problems with a conducting rod sliding on parallel rails in a uniform (possibly time-varying) magnetic field, the external force required for uniform motion is assigned the correct direction and magnitude. Specifically: (1) If the solution states the rod moves uniformly at constant speed in a fixed direction (e.g., to the right), the net force along the rail must be zero, so the external force must oppose the magnetic drag and have magnitude |I(t)|·L·|B(t)|. Equivalently, F_ext + F_mag = 0 with F_mag = I·(L × B) pointing opposite the motion by Lenz’s law. (2) Flag solutions that set F_ext = I·L·B(t) (or any scalar variant using the signed current without absolute values or explicit vector/sign handling) and thereby infer the external force direction from the sign of I, which can produce an external force opposite to the stated motion. (3) Implementation checks: detect the uniform motion condition and the motion direction; extract I(t) and F_ext(t); if F_ext(t) is proportional to I(t)·L·B(t) without absolute value or an explicit negation indicating opposition to F_mag, mark as sign-inconsistent. Evaluate sign consistency with representative positive parameters (B0>0, k>0, L>0, v>0, R>0, x0≥0) at t=0: if sign(F_ext(0)) is opposite to the motion direction, flag an error. Also flag if F_ext(t) changes sign within an interval where the motion direction is fixed, unless the solution explicitly justifies this with a clear sign convention and shows F_ext is along the motion direction. (4) Accept solutions that either express the external force as a magnitude with a separately stated direction (e.g., F_ext = |I|·L·|B| to the right) or use F_ext = −F_mag with a consistent sign convention that yields F_ext along the stated motion direction for the given parameters.

rules.title: Unjustified use of F = I B L with perimeter/effective-length heuristic for magnetic drag
rules.description: Checks solutions modeling magnetic drag in moving conductors (e.g., satellites in Earth's magnetic field) for the improper use of the lumped formula F = I B L (or |F| = I B L) with an arbitrary choice of L such as the body perimeter or L ≈ 2√S. The Lorentz force on distributed currents must be computed from F = ∫ J × B dV or ∮ I dl × B along a specified current path with known orientation relative to B. The rule flags a modeling error when all of the following are true: (1) The context mentions induced current/EMF, magnetic drag, or motion through Earth's magnetic field; (2) The force is written as F_drag = I B L (or equivalent scalar magnitude I*B*L); (3) L is assigned using a perimeter-based or area-derived heuristic (e.g., L = perimeter, L ≈ 2√S, L ≈ 4√S, or similar) without defining a specific conductor segment or loop geometry; and (4) No explicit current path, loop orientation, or integral expression (∮ I dl × B or ∫ J × B dV) is provided to justify the chosen L. The verifier should require either a clearly specified loop/segment with its orientation and resistance path or a distributed-current integral; otherwise, flag the use of perimeter/effective-length heuristics as incorrect scaling and unjustified modeling.

rules.title: Magnetic field direction for a straight wire in the plane of motion
rules.description:
Flag solutions that misstate or ambiguously state the direction of the magnetic field produced by a long straight current-carrying wire when the wire lies in the plane of a particle’s circular motion. The correct geometry is: (a) For an infinite straight wire, B at a point is tangent to a circle centered on the wire; equivalently, B is perpendicular to the wire and to the displacement vector from the wire to the point; (b) When the wire lies in the plane of motion, B at the particle is normal to that plane (out of the plane), so v ⟂ B and the Lorentz force q v × B lies in-plane and can be radial. Trigger this rule if any of the following is detected:
- The solution claims “B is perpendicular to the wire and the radius” without specifying that the radius is from the wire to the particle (i.e., appears to mean the radius of the circular trajectory about the circle’s center).
- The solution asserts or implies that B is perpendicular to the radius of the circular motion (center-to-particle line) as a general property of the wire’s field.
- The solution places B in the plane of motion or otherwise misorients B (e.g., not recognizing that with the wire in-plane, B is out of plane at the particle).
- The solution concludes the magnetic force is radial based on an incorrect or unstated orientation of B (e.g., stating v ⟂ B without establishing that B is normal to the plane in this geometry).
This rule ensures that the field direction is tied to the radial line from the wire (not from the circle’s center) or, equivalently, that B is identified as out of the plane when the wire lies in the plane, before using v × B to argue the force direction.

rules.title: Verify Lorentz Force Equation Application
rules.description: The Lorentz force equation, F = q(E + v × B), applies to a charged particle moving in electric and magnetic fields. It calculates the force on the particle due to these fields.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that the force is calculated as the vector sum of qE (electric force) and q(v × B) (magnetic force). Verify that the cross product is calculated correctly and that the electric and magnetic contributions are combined as vectors.
common_errors: Omitting one of the terms (qE or q(v × B)).
Using scalar multiplication instead of the vector cross product for v × B.
Incorrectly calculating the direction of the cross product using the right-hand rule.

rules.title: Check Dimensional Consistency for Magnetic Field Units
rules.description: The magnetic field (B) is measured in Tesla (T), which is equivalent to N/(A·m). Ensure calculations respect these units and are dimensionally consistent.
rules.check_logic: Verify that B is derived or expressed in consistent units, and that related physical quantities (force, velocity, charge, etc.) align dimensionally. Ensure that derived units are converted correctly when necessary.
common_errors: Using incorrect units for B, e.g., treating it as a scalar without units.
Failure to include the current (A) factor when converting derived units.
Mixing up units for related quantities like force or velocity.

rules.title: Ensure Use of Right-Hand Rule for Cross Products
rules.description: The direction of the magnetic force (q(v × B)) is determined using the right-hand rule: point fingers along v, curl toward B, and thumb gives the force direction for a positive charge.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the cross product direction is determined correctly using the right-hand rule for the given vectors. Ensure the rule is reversed for negative charges.
common_errors: Using the left-hand rule instead of the right-hand rule.
Incorrectly swapping the order of v and B in the cross product (v × B ≠ B × v).
Forgetting to reverse the direction for negative charges.

rules.title: Check Magnetic Force Does No Work
rules.description: The magnetic force is always perpendicular to the velocity of the charged particle, meaning it does no work (W = F · d = 0).
rules.check_logic: Verify that the magnetic force is perpendicular to the velocity vector (v · F = 0), and ensure no work is calculated for it. Confirm that any work done is attributed to other forces, such as the electric force.
common_errors: Incorrectly assuming the magnetic force does work on the particle.
Failing to check the orthogonality of v and F.
Misattributing work done by other forces to the magnetic force.

rules.title: Verify Consistency in Coordinate System Orientation
rules.description: Magnetic fields and forces often involve three-dimensional vector calculations. Ensure the coordinate system used follows a right-handed convention.
rules.check_logic: Check that the coordinate axes follow the right-hand rule (x × y = z). Verify that all vector calculations are consistent with this orientation.
common_errors: Using a left-handed coordinate system.
Mixing up coordinate axes when calculating cross products.
Failing to verify the orientation of the coordinate system in complex setups.

rules.title: Ensure Correct Radius for Circular Motion in Magnetic Fields
rules.description: For a charged particle moving in a uniform magnetic field, the magnetic force provides centripetal acceleration. The radius is r = mv/(qB).
rules.check_logic: Confirm that the radius is calculated using r = mv/(qB), with the direction of the motion forming a circle perpendicular to the magnetic field. Verify that the velocity is perpendicular to the magnetic field for circular motion.
common_errors: Using incorrect formulas for radius.
Forgetting velocity must be perpendicular to the magnetic field for circular motion.
Ignoring the charge sign when determining motion direction.

rules.title: Check Validity for Static Charges
rules.description: The Lorentz force equation does not apply to static charges since v = 0 eliminates the magnetic force (q(v × B) = 0).
rules.check_logic: Ensure that the velocity is non-zero if applying the magnetic force component of the Lorentz force equation. Verify that only the electric force qE acts on a stationary charge.
common_errors: Applying q(v × B) to static charges.
Failing to recognize that only the electric force qE acts on a stationary charge.

rules.title: Verify Conditions for Biot-Savart Law Application
rules.description: The Biot-Savart law calculates the magnetic field B due to a current element. It applies to steady currents and must integrate over the entire current distribution.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that the current is steady and the law is applied to infinitesimal current elements (dL) before integrating. Verify that the contributions from all current elements are summed correctly.
common_errors: Applying the Biot-Savart law to time-varying currents.
Failing to integrate over the entire current distribution.
Incorrectly calculating the vector contributions (direction or magnitude) from each current element.

rules.title: Verify Application of Ampere's Circuital Law
rules.description: Ampere's circuital law relates the line integral of the magnetic field around a closed loop to the current passing through the loop (∮B·dl = μ₀I).
rules.check_logic: Ensure the law is applied to closed loops and that the current enclosed by the loop is correctly calculated. Verify that the magnetic field is tangential to the loop at every point.
common_errors: Applying the law to open loops.
Incorrectly calculating the enclosed current.
Failing to account for symmetry when simplifying the integral.

rules.title: Verify Faraday's Law and Lenz's Law Application
rules.description: Faraday's law states that a changing magnetic flux induces an electromotive force (EMF), and Lenz's law determines the direction of the induced current (EMF = -dΦ/dt).
rules.check_logic: Ensure that the EMF is calculated as the negative rate of change of magnetic flux. Verify that the induced current opposes the change in flux, consistent with Lenz's law.
common_errors: Ignoring the negative sign in Faraday's law.
Incorrectly determining the direction of the induced current.
Failing to account for all contributions to the changing flux.

rules.title: 等质量弹性碰撞速度交换律
rules.description:
触发条件：出现“absolutely elastic”、“mass m”且为“central collision”时
检查逻辑：检查是否直接应用速度交换结论（v1'=v2, v2'=v1），除非存在持续作用的非冲量性质外力干扰碰撞瞬间。
rules.check_logic: 检查是否直接应用速度交换结论（v1'=v2, v2'=v1），除非存在持续作用的非冲量性质外力干扰碰撞瞬间。
rules.trigger: 出现“absolutely elastic”、“mass m”且为“central collision”时

rules.title: 多级电场运动顺序校验
rules.description:
触发条件：题目描述包含“dual acceleration field”及“drift region”
检查逻辑：核实漂移区 L 的物理位置。通常质谱仪结构为：离子源 -> 加速区1 -> 加速区2 -> 自由漂移区 -> 检测器。需检查公式中各段位移的时间累加顺序是否与物理结构一致。
rules.check_logic: 核实漂移区 L 的物理位置。通常质谱仪结构为：离子源 -> 加速区1 -> 加速区2 -> 自由漂移区 -> 检测器。需检查公式中各段位移的时间累加顺序是否与物理结构一致。
rules.trigger: 题目描述包含“dual acceleration field”及“drift region”

rules.title: 线性阻力位移矢量关系
rules.description:
触发条件：受线性阻力 f = -kv 且初速度为 v0 的粒子运动
检查逻辑：利用速度变化量 Δv 与位移 Δr 的线性关系：mΔv = -kΔr + ∫F_other dt。若 F_other 为洛伦兹力，则 Δr 满足复数或矢量代数方程。
rules.check_logic: 利用速度变化量 Δv 与位移 Δr 的线性关系：mΔv = -kΔr + ∫F_other dt。若 F_other 为洛伦兹力，则 Δr 满足复数或矢量代数方程。
rules.trigger: 受线性阻力 f = -kv 且初速度为 v0 的粒子运动

rules.title: 镜像法矢量叠加一致性
rules.description:
触发条件：涉及点电荷/单极子在无限大平面边界附近的场强计算
检查逻辑：验证场强表达式是否为源点矢量与镜像点矢量的线性叠加，且分母幂次（如3/2次）与距离定义一致。
rules.check_logic: 验证场强表达式是否为源点矢量与镜像点矢量的线性叠加，且分母幂次（如3/2次）与距离定义一致。
rules.trigger: 涉及点电荷/单极子在无限大平面边界附近的场强计算

symbolic_hint.canonical: B = k * ( (r - r_source)/|r - r_source|^3 + (r - r_image)/|r - r_image|^3 )

rules.title: 绝热不变性半径关联
rules.description:
触发条件：磁场缓慢变化（时间远大于旋转周期）且电荷做圆周运动
检查逻辑：利用磁矩不变性（M=IA）或角动量守恒推导，验证半径r与磁感应强度B的关系是否满足r²B=const
rules.check_logic: 利用磁矩不变性（M=IA）或角动量守恒推导，验证半径r与磁感应强度B的关系是否满足r²B=const
rules.trigger: 磁场缓慢变化（时间远大于旋转周期）且电荷做圆周运动

rules.title: 相对论动量单位转换
rules.description:
触发条件：高能物理背景且涉及 MeV/c 或 GeV/c 单位时
检查逻辑：验证是否使用了 p = E/c 的量纲处理方式，直接利用 p(eV/c) = B(T) * r(m) * c 的简化数值关系。
rules.check_logic: 验证是否使用了 p = E/c 的量纲处理方式，直接利用 p(eV/c) = B(T) * r(m) * c 的简化数值关系。
rules.trigger: 高能物理背景且涉及 MeV/c 或 GeV/c 单位时

rules.title: 广义动量守恒项量纲检查

rules.title: Do not infer B ⟂ loop from 'loop parallel to straight wire' without geometric justification
rules.description: This rule checks solutions involving magnetic flux near a long straight current-carrying wire for incorrect or ambiguous directional reasoning. Specifically, it flags statements that conclude the magnetic field B is perpendicular (normal) to the loop's plane solely because the loop is 'parallel to the wire'. The magnetic field produced by a straight wire is azimuthal (circulating around the wire axis), so its direction varies with position. B is perpendicular to a given planar surface only under specific geometric conditions (e.g., the loop's plane contains the wire's axis and the plane normal coincides with the azimuthal direction across the entire area). The rule triggers if the solution contains cues such as: mentions of a long straight wire with B = μ0 I /(2π r), assertions that the loop is parallel to the wire, and claims that 'the magnetic field is perpendicular/normal to the plane of the loop' without explicitly stating and justifying the necessary geometric conditions (plane contains the wire axis and the azimuthal direction aligns with the plane normal across the loop). When triggered, the verifier should require the solver to: (1) identify the loop plane and its normal vector, (2) state the B direction as azimuthal around the wire, and (3) compute the flux using Φ = ∫ B · n dA, showing that B · n is nonzero and appropriately oriented, or explicitly justify the special geometry under which B is everywhere perpendicular to the loop's plane.

rules.title: Magnetic flux angle reference: plane vs normal consistency
rules.description: Checks that the magnetic flux through a planar loop in a uniform magnetic field is computed with the correct angle reference and special-case orientations. The physically correct relation is Φ = B A cos(α), where α is the angle between the magnetic field vector B and the loop’s area vector (normal to the plane). Equivalently, if β is defined as the angle between B and the plane itself, then Φ = B A sin(β). The rule flags the following inconsistencies and common errors: (1) Using Φ = B A cos(θ) while defining θ as the angle between B and the plane (instead of the normal), without converting to the complementary angle. (2) Claiming that when the loop’s plane is perpendicular to B (normal ∥ B), the flux is zero or setting θ = 90° in Φ = B A cos(θ). Correct outcome: Φ = B A (maximum). (3) Claiming that when the loop’s plane is parallel to B (normal ⟂ B), the flux is Φ = B A or setting θ = 0° in Φ = B A cos(θ). Correct outcome: Φ = 0. (4) Switching between sin and cos forms without adjusting the angle definition (e.g., using Φ = B A sin(θ) while θ is defined as between B and the normal). (5) For problems explicitly stating geometries like “plane horizontal; B vertical,” the rule expects initial flux Φ0 = B A (e.g., A = l^2 for a square) and will flag derivations that set Φ0 = 0 or use cos(90°) under those conditions. This rule is triggered by textual/derivational cues such as: references to the angle being between B and the plane while using cos, statements like “plane ⟂ B ⇒ Φ = 0” or “plane ∥ B ⇒ Φ = B A,” or assigning θ = 90° when the normal is parallel to B. The rule is tolerant of either cos- or sin-based expressions provided the angle is consistently and correctly defined.

rules.title: Require normal-field component or image-cancellation when claiming zero flux through a plane
rules.description: This rule checks claims that the magnetic flux Φ_B through a horizontal plane (z = z0) due to a magnetic monopole (or an equivalent source) is zero. The verifier will flag an error if the solution justifies Φ_B = 0 by stating that the monopole field is 'radial', 'spherically symmetric', or 'tangent to the plane', without explicitly evaluating the normal component B_n = B · n̂ on the plane or invoking a correct image-source cancellation argument. Specifically: (1) If a monopole is at z = h, the pointwise normal component on a plane is generally nonzero, e.g., B_z(ρ, z0) ∝ (z0 − h)/[ρ^2 + (z0 − h)^2]^{3/2}. Therefore, asserting B · dA = 0 everywhere on the plane is incorrect unless z0 = h or a boundary condition enforces B_n = 0. (2) In setups using the method of images (e.g., conducting or superconducting films), zero flux at a plane must be justified by explicit cancellation of B_z from the real source and its image(s); the solution must specify the image location and sign consistent with the boundary conditions and show that B_z(real) + B_z(image) = 0 on the plane. (3) The rule triggers when a solution sets Φ_B = 0 through a plane without: computing B_z or B · n̂, performing the surface integral, or providing a correct image-cancellation reasoning. It also triggers if the stated reason for zero flux is solely the 'radial' nature of the monopole field. The verifier should require either: an explicit expression for B_z on the plane and its integral, or a correct and complete image-source argument demonstrating pointwise cancellation of the normal field component on that plane.

rules.title: Incorrect flux integral: integrating along wire or using wrong area element
rules.description: Checks magnetic flux computations through a loop/ring to ensure the integral is taken over the surface bounded by the loop (B·n dA) with correct area element and limits. Flags solutions that: (1) describe the ring as lying in the 'ρ = a plane' (a cylinder) instead of a plane z = constant; (2) use an area element like a dφ dz or integrate only over φ with a prefactor a (no radial integral), indicating integration along the wire or over a cylindrical surface; (3) include dz in dA when the surface is at fixed z; (4) omit the radial integration from 0 to a for a circular loop. For a circular loop of radius a at z = z0, the correct flux setup is Φ = ∫_0^{2π} ∫_0^a B_z(ρ, z0) ρ dρ dφ. Additionally warns when an explicit flux calculation is unnecessary for a requested circuit relation (e.g., expressing emf via L, R, and i using Faraday’s law and Kirchhoff’s loop equation).

rules.title: Flux through a circular loop: correct plane and area element
rules.description: For a circular conducting ring of radius a centered on the z-axis and lying in a plane perpendicular to the axis, the magnetic flux must be computed over the disk enclosed by the ring in the plane z = z0. The surface element in cylindrical coordinates is dA = ρ dρ dφ with ρ ∈ [0, a] and φ ∈ [0, 2π], and the relevant field component is the component normal to the disk (typically B_z for a horizontal disk). The verifier should flag solutions that: (1) identify the ring's surface as the 'ρ = a plane' (note: ρ = a defines a cylindrical surface, not a plane); (2) express the flux using an area element like 'a dφ' or 'a dφ dz' (missing the ρ dρ factor); (3) reduce the flux to a line integral over the circumference, e.g., Φ = ∫₀^{2π} B_z(a, φ, z0) a dφ, without integrating over ρ; or (4) include integration over z for a fixed ring at z = z0. A correct setup should be Φ = ∫₀^{a} ∫₀^{2π} B_normal(ρ, z0) ρ dρ dφ, and if B_normal is φ-independent, Φ = 2π ∫₀^{a} B_normal(ρ, z0) ρ dρ, not 2π a B_normal(a, z0).

rules.title: Net magnetic force must use relative velocity (v1−v2), not center-of-mass velocity
rules.description: This rule checks solutions for a two-particle electric dipole (charges +q and −q, equal masses m) in a constant uniform magnetic field B to ensure the net Lorentz force and center-of-mass (CM) dynamics are derived from the relative motion, not the CM velocity. Specifically: (1) Expected force sum: F_net = q v1 × B + (−q) v2 × B = q (v1 − v2) × B. Any expression that replaces (v1 − v2) with v_CM or asserts F_net ∝ q v_CM × B is incorrect. (2) Kinematic identities to enforce: v_CM = (v1 + v2)/2 and v_rel = v1 − v2. For a rigid rod of length ℓ, v_rel = dℓ/dt = ω × ℓ. (3) Expected CM equation of motion: M dv_CM/dt = q (dℓ/dt) × B = q (ω × ℓ) × B (with M = 2m). The rule flags as a logic error any of the following patterns: (a) F_net = q v_CM × B or M dv_CM/dt = q v_CM × B; (b) an explicit or implicit substitution v1 − v2 = v_CM; (c) equating dℓ/dt to v_CM. The rule accepts solutions that correctly keep v_rel (or ω × ℓ) in the net force and CM acceleration, demonstrating the coupling between translation and rotation. Context trigger: problems describing a neutral dipole (±q) connected by a rigid rod in a uniform magnetic field without external electric fields.

rules.title: Magnetic moment of a single charged particle in circular motion: correct dependence on q, B, and L
rules.description:
Scope: Applies when a solution derives the magnetic moment μ of a single point charge q moving in a circular (cyclotron) orbit in a uniform magnetic field B.
Checks:
- From μ = I A with I = q/T, A = π r^2, and T = 2π/ω, verify equivalence to μ = (q ω r^2)/2 and μ = (q v r)/2. Flag if factors (1/2) or π are missing or incorrectly placed.
- If the derivation uses the centripetal/Lorentz relation m v_perp = |q| B r (or r = m v_perp/(|q| B)), the final magnitude must reduce to |μ| = m v_perp^2/(2 B) and be independent of |q|. Flag any expression that retains |q| after this substitution (e.g., m v_perp^2/(2 |q| B)).
- Verify the angular momentum relation: μ = (q/(2m)) L (vector). Flag forms missing the factor q/(2m) or with incorrect factors, such as μ = L/2 or μ = (m v × r)/2.
- Functional dependence on B: For fixed m and v_perp, μ must scale as 1/B, not proportional to B. Flag statements like μ ∝ B or explicit forms such as μ = m B/2.
- Dimensional consistency: μ must have units of A·m^2 (J/T). Flag expressions with units inconsistent with magnetic moment (e.g., kg·T, kg·m^2/s without the q/(2m) factor).
- Allowed correct final forms include any of: μ = (q ω r^2)/2, μ = (q v r)/2, μ = (q/(2m)) L, and |μ| = m v_perp^2/(2 B). If the final expression contains both q and B simultaneously but is not one of the allowed forms (i.e., it attempts to eliminate r yet retains q), flag as algebraic inconsistency.

rules.title: Dimensional consistency for induced magnetic moment (μ) in eddy-current solutions
rules.description: This rule verifies that any final expression provided for the magnetic dipole moment μ has the correct SI units (A·m^2). It is triggered when the target quantity is μ and the expression involves a time-varying magnetic field (dot{B}) and material resistivity ρ or conductivity σ = 1/ρ. The verifier will: - Map known variable units: μ [A·m^2], B [T], dot{B} [T/s], ρ [Ω·m], σ [S/m], R [m], D (thickness) [m], μ0 [N/A^2]. - Compute the resultant units of the provided μ expression. - Flag an error if the units do not reduce to A·m^2 (e.g., if they reduce to A or A·m). - Apply a heuristic specific to thin conducting shells and similar eddy-current problems: if μ depends on dot{B} and σ (or 1/ρ) but lacks sufficient geometric length factors (e.g., area or thickness) to supply at least length squared, the expression is likely missing geometry terms. Typical correct scalings require additional powers of length and/or thickness (e.g., factors involving R and D) to reach A·m^2, whereas forms like (const)·R^2·σ·dot{B} yield units of amperes. - Example of a common failure pattern to flag: μ expressed as (const)·R^n·σ·dot{B} with n ≤ 2 and no thickness D term; this combination cannot produce A·m^2. The rule is general and will catch similar dimensional inconsistencies in future solutions where μ is derived from induced currents.

rules.title: Disallow magnetic potential energy for free charges in uniform magnetic fields
rules.description: Flag solutions that introduce a magnetic potential energy term for free charges in a spatially uniform, static magnetic field. Specifically, if the system consists of point charges (e.g., an electric dipole made of ±q connected by an insulating rod) with no specified intrinsic magnetic dipole or current loop, the verifier should: (1) detect inclusion of a term labeled as magnetic potential energy (e.g., U = −μ·B, −p·B, or any analogous scalar magnetic energy) in the total energy, Hamiltonian, or Lagrangian; (2) detect use of U = −μ·B where μ is defined ad hoc from charges, separation, and center-of-mass motion (e.g., μ ∝ q (ℓ × v_CM)), particularly when μ depends on v_CM or omits the relativistic factor 1/c^2; (3) detect any claim that a uniform magnetic field does work or that energy conservation includes a magnetic-field contribution for free charges; (4) detect substitution of such a U term to couple translational and rotational motion in place of using the vector potential/canonical momentum. Rationale: In a uniform B field, the Lorentz force on free charges does no work and there is no scalar magnetic potential energy; −μ·B applies to systems with a bona fide magnetic dipole (e.g., a current loop or intrinsic moment), not to free charges constrained by an insulating rod. The correct coupling appears via the vector potential in the Lagrangian and the modified/canonical momentum, not via a magnetic potential energy.

rules.title: Torque must not be directly proportional to dΦ/dt (emf) without current or magnetic moment
rules.description: This rule verifies that the magnetic torque on a conducting loop in a magnetic field is not modeled as directly proportional to the rate of change of magnetic flux (dΦ/dt) or emf ε without involving the loop current I (or resistance R via I = ε/R) or the magnetic moment μ = I·A. The physically correct torque on a rigid current loop in a uniform field is τ = μ × B with μ = I·A·n̂, equivalently |τ| = I·A·B·sinθ. For a resistive loop with negligible self-inductance, I = ε/R = -(1/R) dΦ/dt when the circuit is closed. Therefore, any torque expression that depends on dΦ/dt or ε must include the circuit response (e.g., factors of 1/R and A·B·sinθ) or explicitly use I. The verifier should flag solutions that: (1) write torque as τ ∝ dΦ/dt, τ = k·(dΦ/dt), or τ = ε times a length/geometric factor (e.g., τ = -(dΦ/dt)·(l/2), τ = ε·l) without I, μ, R, or A·B; (2) omit the B-field in the torque expression when deriving torque from induction; (3) are dimensionally inconsistent, e.g., torque expressed as voltage times length(s) without converting voltage to current via resistance; (4) in open-circuit conditions (I = 0), predict a nonzero magnetic torque due solely to changing flux. Acceptable forms include τ = I·A·B·sinθ or τ = -(A·B·sinθ/R)·(dΦ/dt) for a closed loop. Flag any direct use of dΦ/dt (or ε) to compute torque that lacks current/magnetic moment dependence or yields incorrect units.

rules.title: Incorrectly summing isolated magnet flux by counting elements in a connected magnetic circuit
rules.description:
Checks for modeling errors where a solution treats the total flux in an assembled magnetic circuit as an integer multiple of the isolated flux of one magnet by simply counting magnets, edges, or vertices. Trigger this rule when any of the following are observed:
- The solution defines Φ (or Phi) as the flux produced by a single magnet in isolation (e.g., in a U-shaped core), and later sets Φ_C, Φ_F, or any "total flux" equal to k × Φ with k equal to the number of magnets/spheres/edges/vertices, without computing the circuit's reluctances or using magnetic circuit equations (MMF/reluctance, flux continuity).
- Statements like "each magnet contributes Φ" or "total flux is nΦ" justified only by symmetry or by counting elements, with no analysis of the assembled magnetic circuit.
- Introduction of a per-sphere flux (e.g., Φ_sphere) and summation over spheres, treating ferromagnetic spheres as independent flux sources.
- Addition of flux across series-connected components (e.g., summing flux along edges of a closed path) instead of recognizing that flux is continuous and equal through series elements.
Do not flag if the solution explicitly models the magnetic circuit using MMF and reluctance (Ampere’s law/Ohm’s law analog), enforces flux continuity at nodes, and only sums flux across well-justified parallel branches after computing branch fluxes from the common MMF and branch reluctances. This rule targets answers that infer Φ_C or Φ_F via element counting rather than magnetic circuit analysis.

rules.title: Incorrect use of ε0/Coulomb constant in magnetic-field prefactors
rules.description: This rule checks expressions that represent magnetic field quantities (e.g., B, Bz, Br, Bφ, B_mp, B′) for the improper use of the electric permittivity ε0 (or Coulomb’s constant k_e = 1/(4π ε0)) as the leading prefactor. Detection criteria: (1) If an expression for a magnetic field includes factors like 1/(4π ε0) or k_e multiplied by a magnetic source (e.g., q_m, m, M) and 1/r^n (typically n = 2 for a monopole, n = 3 for a dipole), flag it. (2) If ε0 appears anywhere in the magnetic field prefactor without μ0, or the field is written as q_m/(4π ε0 r^2) r̂ for a monopole or similarly for a dipole, flag it. (3) If both ε0 and μ0 appear but the effective prefactor for the magnetic field follows the electric-field form (Coulomb prefactor), flag it. Rationale: In SI units, magnetic fields due to monopoles/dipoles must use μ0 (e.g., B_mp = μ0 q_m/(4π r^2) r̂, and B_dipole ∝ μ0 m/(4π r^3)), whereas electric fields use ε0. Using ε0 in a magnetic-field expression indicates a conceptual mix-up and yields dimensional inconsistency (not in tesla).

rules.title: Verify Gauss's Law for Electric Fields
rules.description: Gauss's Law states that the total electric flux through a closed surface equals the total charge enclosed divided by the permittivity of free space (ε_0). This law applies in both static and dynamic scenarios involving electric fields.
rules.check_logic: Ensure the integral of the electric field dot product with the normal surface area vector equals the enclosed charge divided by ε_0.
common_errors: Failing to account for all enclosed charges.
Using incorrect surface normals for the flux calculation.
Omitting the permittivity constant (ε_0).
Misinterpreting open surfaces as closed surfaces.

rules.title: Verify Gauss's Law for Magnetism
rules.description: Gauss's Law for magnetism states that the total magnetic flux through any closed surface is always zero, indicating the non-existence of magnetic monopoles.
rules.check_logic: Check that the integral of the magnetic field dot product with the normal surface area vector equals zero for any closed surface.
common_errors: Assuming non-zero flux for magnetic fields through closed surfaces.
Incorrectly applying this law to open surfaces.
Improperly handling vector directions for normal components.

rules.title: Verify Faraday's Law of Induction
rules.description: Faraday's Law states that the electromotive force (EMF) around a closed loop equals the negative rate of change of the magnetic flux through the loop. This law is relevant for time-varying magnetic fields.
rules.check_logic: Ensure the line integral of the electric field around the loop equals the negative time derivative of the magnetic flux through the loop.
common_errors: Neglecting the negative sign (Lenz's Law).
Mixing up integration limits for the loop.
Forgetting to calculate the rate of change of magnetic flux.
Omitting contributions from time-varying magnetic fields.

rules.title: Verify Ampere-Maxwell's Law
rules.description: Ampere-Maxwell's Law states that the line integral of the magnetic field around a closed loop equals the permeability of free space (μ_0) times the sum of conduction current and displacement current through the loop.
rules.check_logic: Ensure the line integral of the magnetic field equals μ_0 times the sum of conduction current and the time derivative of the electric flux density through the loop.
common_errors: Failing to include displacement current in time-varying cases.
Omitting the permeability constant (μ_0).
Using incorrect integration paths for the loop.
Ignoring contributions from non-uniform current densities.

rules.title: Check Sign Conventions in Maxwell's Equations
rules.description: The signs in Maxwell's equations depend on orientation rules, mainly the right-hand rule for vector cross products. Incorrect sign conventions lead to errors in calculations.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the surface normals, loop directions, and vector cross products adhere to the right-hand rule and match the chosen coordinate system.
common_errors: Using left-hand rule instead of right-hand rule.
Reversing the orientation of surface normals.
Flipping the direction of closed loop integration.

rules.title: Validate Boundary Conditions for Fields
rules.description: At the boundary between two media, tangential components of the electric and magnetic fields must be continuous, while normal components depend on surface charge and surface current densities.
rules.check_logic: Ensure boundary conditions are satisfied for both electric and magnetic fields across the interface between two media.
common_errors: Assuming continuity of normal electric fields when surface charges are present.
Neglecting surface currents when analyzing magnetic field boundaries.
Failing to consider dielectric properties of the media.

rules.title: Check Dimensional and Unit Consistency
rules.description: Each term in Maxwell's equations must exhibit consistent dimensions and units, including flux, fields, charge density, and current density.
rules.check_logic: Ensure all terms in the equations have consistent units (e.g., electric field in V/m, magnetic field in T, charge density in C/m³, etc.).
common_errors: Incorrectly converting between units (e.g., from Gauss to Tesla).
Omitting unit conversions when using derived quantities.
Using incompatible units across terms in the equations.

rules.title: Verify Validity Conditions for Maxwell's Equations
rules.description: Maxwell's equations assume classical conditions like non-relativistic speeds and neglect quantum effects. They also assume continuous media without abrupt discontinuities unless explicitly accounted for.
rules.check_logic: Ensure the problem context is within the classical regime and that media are continuous unless specified otherwise.
common_errors: Applying Maxwell's equations to quantum-scale systems.
Neglecting relativistic corrections at high speeds.
Using Maxwell's equations without considering boundary conditions in discontinuous media.

rules.title: Nonideal meter loading must be modeled when readings depend on external resistance
rules.description: This rule flags solutions to circuit problems involving a voltmeter or ammeter where the reading changes by a finite factor as another resistance is varied, but the solution neglects the instrument's finite resistance or models the topology incorrectly. The rule applies when: (1) the problem statement includes a voltmeter/ammeter without explicitly declaring it ideal, and (2) the solution either (a) asserts or implies an ideal meter (e.g., "R_V >> R, r", "neglect R_V", "ideal voltmeter", or sets R_V → ∞ / R_A → 0), (b) omits the meter resistance from the governing expressions for current/voltage (e.g., uses I = E/(R + r) and V_meter = I·R while a voltmeter is present), or (c) uses dimensionally or topologically inconsistent total resistance such as R_total = R + r + 1/R_V (adding a reciprocal of resistance or treating a parallel meter as series). Rationale: When the reading changes with the external resistor, the dependence typically arises from meter loading; a finite meter resistance must appear explicitly in the equations. Neglecting it leads to incorrect factor-change predictions and can yield contradictions (e.g., negative or infinite inferred resistances). The rule checks for explicit phrases like "neglect R_V", "R_V >> R", the absence of R_V or R_A in the derived expression for the meter reading, and misuse of series vs parallel modeling. It does not trigger if the problem explicitly states an ideal meter or if the final equations include the instrument resistance consistently with circuit topology.

rules.title: Method-of-Images Sign Consistency for Conducting Plane
rules.description: Checks that image charge/monopole signs and removal/addition terms are correctly implemented when using the method of images near a planar conducting boundary (e.g., z=0). The verifier triggers when a solution constructs a scalar potential or field as a sum/integral of image sources. It enforces: (a) for Dirichlet (grounded conductor) boundary conditions on the potential, the first image across the plane must have opposite sign to the source and subsequent reflections must alternate sign; (b) for Neumann (zero-normal-derivative) boundary conditions, the image has the same sign; (c) for magnetostatic analogs (e.g., magnetic monopole near a perfectly conducting or superconducting film imposing B_n=0), the image monopole must have opposite sign across the plane. Detection criteria: 1) Identify summations/integrals of the form sum_n c_n * G(r - r_n) where c_n corresponds to image strengths. If all c_n share the same sign as the source for a Dirichlet or B_n=0 boundary, flag an error; absence of an explicit alternating sign factor (e.g., (-1)^n) in multi-reflection ladders also flags. 2) Evaluate the constructed boundary value by substituting z=0: if Phi(x, z=0) (or the required normal field component) fails to meet the stated boundary condition within tolerance, flag. 3) For moving sources modeled by time-discretized image creation, verify that removal-creation pairs are present (net contribution includes subtraction of the prior state); if the series includes only additive +q_m terms without corresponding negative or removal terms, flag. 4) Reject configurations that place an 'image' on the same side of the boundary with the same sign as the source unless explicitly justified by non-conducting or Neumann boundary conditions. This rule catches solutions that keep +q_m for all image terms or omit the alternating sign pattern required to satisfy the conducting boundary conditions.

rules.title: Numeric minimum momentum in uniform magnetic field using p = qBR
rules.description:
Triggers for problems asking the minimum momentum of a charged particle to loop/track in a uniform solenoidal magnetic field (e.g., LHC detector scenarios). The verifier checks the following:

1) Final numeric result: The solution must provide a numerical value for the momentum threshold with proper momentum units (e.g., GeV/c, MeV/c, kg·m/s). If no numerical momentum is given, flag the solution.

2) Correct relation and geometry: The solution should use the cyclotron radius relation r = p/(qB) and set r equal to the relevant detector/tracking radius R provided or inferable from context. If r is not linked to the detector geometry (R) to determine the threshold, flag the solution.

3) Expected value consistency: When B (in Tesla) and a characteristic radius R (in meters) are present, the threshold must satisfy p_min = |q| B R. In high-energy physics units, require p[GeV/c] ≈ 0.3 × B[T] × R[m] for |q| = e. Compare the reported momentum to this value (after unit conversion) and flag if the relative error exceeds 20%.

4) Units check: Flag if the reported quantity is not momentum (e.g., energy without conversion), lacks units, or uses incompatible units for momentum.

5) Overuse of relativistic expressions without result: Discussions of γ, m, v are acceptable, but the computation must conclude with the geometric threshold p = qBR and a numeric result. If the solution introduces relativistic formulas yet omits the final numeric momentum, flag.

Example context-specific expectation: For ATLAS inner detector with B ≈ 2.0 T and R ≈ 0.55 m, p_min ≈ 0.3 × 2.0 × 0.55 ≈ 0.33 GeV/c. Solutions failing to produce a comparable numeric value or not applying p = qBR are flagged.

rules.title: EM momentum density must be S/c^2 (not S/c)
rules.description:
Checks that the linear momentum density of an electromagnetic wave in vacuum is expressed with the correct power of c. The correct vector relation is p_V = S/c^2, which is equivalent to p_V = (E × B)/(μ0 c^2) = ε0 (E × B). The rule flags solutions that:
- Express momentum density as p_V = S/c (missing one factor of c), or equivalently p_V = (E × B)/(μ0 c).
- Omit the c^2 in any expression proportional to the Poynting vector (e.g., p_V ∝ S) without the 1/c^2 factor.
- Fail a dimensional check: momentum density has units kg/(s·m^2); S/c has units kg/(s^2·m) and is inconsistent, while S/c^2 is consistent.
Accepted correct forms include any of the following (vacuum only):
- p_V = S/c^2
- p_V = (E × B)/(μ0 c^2)
- p_V = ε0 (E × B)
The rule should recognize common notations for momentum density (p_V, g) and for the Poynting vector (S), and verify algebraic equivalence under c^2 = 1/(μ0 ε0). It triggers a warning/error when the found expression is proportional to S/c rather than S/c^2.

rules.title: EM momentum density must be S/c^2 = ε0 (E × B), not along E or B alone
rules.description: Checks student expressions for the electromagnetic linear momentum density (p_V, g, or similar). The correct vector form in vacuum is g = p_V = S/c^2 = (1/μ0 c^2)(E × B) = ε0 (E × B), i.e., parallel to E × B (the propagation direction). The rule flags solutions that: (1) give a momentum density vector proportional to E or B alone (e.g., ε0 E E⃗, ε0 E^2 Ê, k E⃗, k B⃗), or explicitly state it is along E or B; (2) omit the cross product between E and B in the final vector expression for momentum density; (3) use B = E/c to eliminate B and produce an expression in terms of E only for momentum density; (4) equate momentum density to u/c or u/c^2 without tying it to S or the propagation direction (i.e., missing E × B); (5) use an incorrect prefactor when a cross product is present (prefactor must be ε0 or 1/(μ0 c^2)); (6) present a magnitude depending only on E^2 or B^2 (e.g., ε0 E^2) with direction Ê or B̂ instead of the vector E × B. Unit sanity check heuristic: flag if the proposed result has units of energy density (J/m^3, e.g., ε0 E^2) or field magnitude times permittivity (ε0 E) rather than N·s/m^3 (same as S/c^2). Acceptable forms that should pass: g = S/c^2, g = (1/μ0 c^2)(E × B), g = ε0 (E × B), and textual statements that the momentum density is parallel to E × B and proportional to S with factor 1/c^2.

rules.title: Incorrect use of relativistic E–p relation and failure to apply r = p/(qB) = R for momentum thresholds
rules.description: This rule flags logic errors in solutions that seek the minimum/threshold momentum for a charged particle to loop or be (un)measured in a uniform magnetic field with a known detector/aperture radius. The correct criterion is the geometric curvature constraint r = p/(qB) and the threshold occurs at the boundary r = R_det, giving p_threshold = q B R_det. The rule triggers when: (a) the problem context includes a uniform magnetic field (B) and a detector/aperture/field region radius (R) or mentions looping/trapping/curvature-limited detection; AND (b) the solution introduces or relies on the relativistic energy–momentum relation E^2 = (pc)^2 + (mc^2)^2 or extensive gamma manipulations to determine p without first or explicitly using r = p/(qB) and equating r to R; OR (c) the solution uses contradictory phrasing such as 'assuming r is minimized, set r = R' or 'minimize the radius' to define the threshold. The rule also flags if the final threshold expression for p omits R, B, or q, or includes unnecessary dependence on m or c (beyond p = γ m v) when the immediate threshold is p = q B R. Correct solutions may use relativistic relations only to convert the momentum threshold to an energy threshold after establishing p_threshold = q B R.

rules.title: Point-source magnetic field must use full 3D displacement with single |r−r0|^3 denominator
rules.description: Checks expressions for the magnetic field of a magnetic monopole (or analogous electric point charge) to ensure proper 3D Coulomb-form modeling. The expected field for a monopole at r0 is B(r) = (μ0 q_m / 4π) (r − r0) / |r − r0|^3. In cylindrical coordinates with r0 = h ẑ, this is B(ρ, z) ∝ [ρ ρ̂ + (z − h) ẑ] / (ρ^2 + (z − h)^2)^{3/2}. The rule flags errors when any of the following are detected: (a) different denominators are used for different vector components; (b) the denominator depends only on the transverse distance |ρ| or otherwise omits the axial offset (z − h) for sources at z ≠ 0; (c) the displacement vector is written as (ρ − ρ_mp) − z ẑ, or similar splits that treat radial and axial parts with separate denominators; (d) a nonzero transverse source location ρ_mp is introduced when the source is specified at r0 = h ẑ (i.e., ρ_mp must be 0); (e) any component lacks the consistent single distance-cubed factor |r − r0|^3. The rule accepts algebraically equivalent forms in Cartesian coordinates: numerator (x − x0, y − y0, z − z0) with denominator [(x − x0)^2 + (y − y0)^2 + (z − z0)^2]^{3/2}. For image sources, it verifies the same structure with the correct image location z0 (e.g., z_im = −h), requiring B ∝ [ρ ρ̂ + (z − z_im) ẑ] / (ρ^2 + (z − z_im)^2)^{3/2}. Apply this rule whenever a solution models the field of a point monopole/source; it should not be applied to extended or distributed sources.

rules.title: Avoid area-based EMF for rigidly translating loops; use segment vBL and plasma-limited current for satellite magnetic drag
rules.description:
This rule flags misapplication of Faraday’s law and current modeling in magnetic-drag problems for spacecraft. It detects when a solution (a) computes a nonzero EMF around a rigid, closed conductive loop translating in a uniform, steady magnetic field using an area term (e.g., ε ∝ v·B·S), and/or (b) derives current via I = ε/R using only the satellite’s internal resistance without accounting for plasma current closure and particle-flux limits.

Checks:
- EMF modeling in uniform, static B:
  - If the solution models a rigid, closed loop translating at constant velocity through a uniform, time-invariant magnetic field and uses an area-based EMF (e.g., ε = v·B·S, ε ∝ area, or treats Φ = B·S with dΦ/dt ≠ 0 purely due to translation) → flag.
  - If loop EMF is obtained by ∮(v × B)·dl with v treated as uniform along the loop but reported nonzero → flag.
  - Absence of length-based motional EMF (ε_segment ≈ v·B·L for an open conductor segment) in such contexts → flag.
- Current modeling for satellite magnetic drag:
  - If the solution computes current as I = ε/R using only an internal/structural resistance for a free-flying satellite (no electrodynamic tether/contactors) and does not model current closure through the ambient plasma or particle collection → flag.
  - If no mention is made of plasma/ionosphere parameters (e.g., electron/ion density n, collection area A, relative velocity v_rel or thermal speeds, sheath/collection limits) and current is set solely by an internal circuit → flag.

Why this is incorrect:
- For a rigid closed loop in uniform, steady B undergoing pure translation, the net EMF around the loop is zero: dΦ/dt = 0 and ∮(v × B)·dl = 0 because v is the same along the entire loop. Motional EMF applies across an open segment and scales with length (ε ≈ v·B·L), not with area.
- In LEO magnetic-drag scenarios without a defined external circuit, induced potentials lead to charge collection from the ambient plasma; the attainable current is limited by particle flux and sheath physics (order-of-magnitude I ~ e·n·A·v_rel for the collected species), not by the satellite’s ohmic resistance.

Allowed exceptions (do not flag):
- The loop rotates/deforms so that velocities differ along the loop, or B is time-varying/non-uniform such that dΦ/dt ≠ 0 (then loop EMF can be nonzero).
- The solution explicitly models a closed current path through the ionosphere/plasma (e.g., electrodynamic tether with contactors) and includes plasma/contact resistances in R_total.

Detection heuristics (text/math patterns):
- Presence of formulas like ε = v B S, ε ∝ area, or treating Φ = B S with nonzero dΦ/dt for pure translation in uniform B.
- Use of I = ε/R based solely on spacecraft internal resistance without mention of: ionosphere/plasma, particle density n, collection area, sheath, contactors/tether, or non-uniform/Time-varying B.
- Absence of length L in EMF expressions and absence of particle-flux terms (e.g., e n A v) in current estimates.

Corrective guidance (for feedback systems):
- For rigid translation in uniform B, set loop EMF to zero; if needed, compute motional EMF across a conductor segment: ε ≈ v·B·L.
- For magnetic drag in plasma, bound current by collection limits (I ≲ e·n·A·v_rel with appropriate species and sheath considerations) unless a valid external circuit through the plasma is modeled.

rules.title: Motional EMF in rotating rigid conductors must use ∫(v×B)·dl and correct geometry
rules.description: This rule verifies modeling of motional EMF in rotating rigid circuits. It flags solutions that: (a) compute EMF along a rotating wire using the shortcut E = B l v sin(φ) or an 'effective length' without performing or justifying the line integral of (v × B) · dl along the actual conductor; (b) fail to use the velocity field v(r) = ω × r and to account for its spatial variation along each segment; and (c) assign nonzero EMF to segments whose geometry makes it zero. Specifically: for a rotation axis perpendicular to a plane containing a conductor segment and a uniform magnetic field B perpendicular to the axis (i.e., B lies in that plane), v lies in the plane and v × B is parallel to the axis. Therefore (v × B) has no component along any segment that lies entirely in that plane, and the motional EMF along such in‑plane edges must be zero. The driving EMFs reside on segments parallel to the rotation axis (where dl is parallel to v × B); only there may a simplified constant integrand be justified when r is constant along the segment. The rule requires that the solution: (1) explicitly formulates EMF as ∫(v × B) · dl with v = ω × r or provides a clear justification for constancy of (v × B) · dl along the segment; (2) checks the directionality of (v × B) relative to each conductor’s dl to determine where EMF is nonzero; and (3) assigns sources and computes currents accordingly. Any use of a single, uniform v or an unqualified E = B l v sin(φ) on non-axial segments, or any nonzero EMF claimed on in‑plane edges under the stated geometry, is flagged as a modeling error.

rules.title: Sliding conductor in B-field: require motional EMF (ε = B L v) in current/force model
rules.description: Scope: Problems involving a sliding conducting bar or railgun accelerated by a DC source in a magnetic field (keywords: railgun, sliding bar, rails, magnetic field B, bar length L). Check for the following modeling consistency: 1) If the solution sets the circuit current as I = V/R (or I = V/R_total) constant while the bar is moving in a magnetic field, flag an error. In such systems the motional/back EMF ε_m = B L v must be included and the correct relation is I(v) = (V − B L v)/R_total. 2) If the magnetic force is modeled as F_B = I L B with I replaced by V/R (no velocity dependence) or F_B is stated to be constant, flag an error. Correctly, F_B(v) = L B I(v) = (B L V)/R_total − (B^2 L^2/R_total) v. 3) If the derived acceleration a is constant (independent of v) in a moving-conductor railgun setup, flag an error; a should depend on v via the BLv term (e.g., m dv/dt includes a term proportional to −v). 4) Also flag if the solution omits any mention of induced/motional EMF, back EMF, or a term proportional to B L v in the circuit or force equations despite using B and L and describing motion of the bar. Rationale: Ignoring ε_m = B L v violates Faraday’s/Lenz’s law and yields incorrect constant-current/constant-acceleration results. Expected correction: Use V − ε_m = I R_total with ε_m = B L v, then compute F_B = L B I(v) and a(v) accordingly.

rules.title: Motional EMF dot-product geometry consistency
rules.description: Detects misuse of the motional-emf formula dℰ = (v × B) · dl by checking geometric consistency of vector directions. The rule triggers when a solution: (1) explicitly sets the conductor element dl parallel to the local velocity v (e.g., dl = R dθ θ̂ with v = ωR θ̂), yet proceeds to compute a nonzero (v × B) · dl; (2) claims a nonzero ∮(v × B) · dl for a circular ring rotating about its symmetry (vertical) axis in a uniform magnetic field lying in the ring’s plane, where v × B is along the axis and perpendicular to the wire tangent everywhere, making the integrand identically zero. The verifier extracts stated directions for v, B, and dl; if dl ∥ v anywhere, it asserts that (v × B) ⟂ dl at that location, so the local contribution must vanish. Any nonzero emf or current derived from such a setup via the (v × B) · dl integral is flagged as a logic error.

rules.title: Static mirror-image used instead of moving-image formalism for finite-conductivity thin film
rules.description: Flags solutions that incorrectly model the field of a moving magnetic monopole near a thin conducting film by using a static perfect-conductor mirror image at z = −h (or a fixed ±q_m at z = ±h), instead of the required moving image-monopole formalism. Trigger when: (1) The problem context specifies a thin film with finite conductivity/slow response or explicitly instructs use of the 'moving image-monopole concept' (e.g., A.7). (2) The solution places image monopoles at fixed positions z = −h (and/or z = +h) with constant magnitudes equal to the source (±q_m), independent of time and velocity v, or recreates identical static images at discrete x-steps. (3) The boundary is treated as a perfect conductor or instantaneous mirror with no dependence on film parameters (e.g., σ, thickness) or relaxation time τ. (4) The potential/field is expressed purely as a static sum over image terms and lacks any time-dependent convolution/integral over the source trajectory (e.g., no ∫_0^∞ dt kernel of the form (a+pt)/[(a+pt)^2+(b+qt)^2]^{3/2}, and no explicit dependence on v, σ, or τ in image strengths/positions). If these conditions are met, report a modeling error: inappropriate static image construction in a regime requiring time-dependent moving images tied to the film’s finite conductivity and the monopole’s motion.

rules.title: Thin-film induced field must show moving image monopole (advective z–t dependence)
rules.description: This rule verifies the modeling of the induced magnetic field near a thin conducting film when a magnetic monopole/dipole is introduced above the film under the h ≫ d approximation and neglected radial derivatives. Expected behavior: Near z ≈ 0 for t > 0, the induced field satisfies an advection-type boundary condition at the film, leading to a moving image monopole that recedes with constant speed v0 = 2/(μ0 σ d). Equivalently, the induced z-component should obey ∂B′z/∂t + v0 ∂B′z/∂z = 0 and have the functional dependence B′z(ρ, z; t) = F(ρ, z + v0 t). The rule flags solutions that: (a) omit the moving image monopole description or the advective z–t coupling; (b) propose purely separable exponential decay in time and/or space (e.g., B′z ∼ e^{−γ t} G(ρ, z) or G(ρ, z) with e^{−k z}) without the z + v0 t dependence; (c) use an incorrect speed expression for the receding image (v0 not equal to 2/(μ0 σ d) in the thin-film limit); or (d) introduce spurious dependence of v0 on ρ, h, or other variables inconsistent with h ≫ d and neglected radial derivatives. Passing solutions may either state the moving image monopole with the correct v0 or present the correct advection PDE or its characteristic solution form.

rules.title: Missing removal-creation (hop) difference in time-stepped image-source sums
rules.description: This rule flags solutions that model a moving point source (charge/monopole/dipole) near a boundary (e.g., conducting film) using discrete time steps or hops, yet build the potential/field as a plain sum over contributions from all step positions with the same sign, without subtracting the previous position’s contribution. Physics requirement: in a hop/removal-creation picture, the net source at step n is the change in source distribution, q δ(r − r_n) − q δ(r − r_{n−1}), so the corresponding potential/field must be expressed as a difference of Green-function terms, G(r − r_n) − G(r − r_{n−1}); this produces a telescoping sum that reduces to endpoint contributions. Detection criteria: (a) The solution references a moving source and discretized time/hops (terms like “time step,” “hop,” “at t = 0 sum over previous positions,” “positions x = n Δx”). (b) The presented superposition is Σ_n w_n G(r − r_n) (or equivalent image contributions) with uniform-sign weights w_n and no explicit subtraction referencing the prior position r_{n−1}. (c) There is no use of a difference operator, time derivative of the Green’s function, or pairing of terms that ensures telescoping (e.g., G(r − r_n) − G(r − r_{n−1})). (d) In image-method contexts, the solution “adds image sources at each time step” but does not represent the removal from the previous location or alternate signs across steps associated with the change in source position. If criteria (a) and (b) are met and neither (c) nor (d) is satisfied, flag the solution for missing the essential removal-creation difference structure.

rules.title: Coupled coils with ramp current: require resistive drop in U1 and induced U2 (including constant-i2 case)
rules.description:
