The rule flags as inconsistent if any of the following occur after a positive-for-descent convention is declared or implied:
- A reported value for the same variable (Δh, Δr, H, ‘descent’, ‘drop’, ‘loss’) is negative while still being described as the descent amount (e.g., “H = −120 m of descent”).
- The variable is used as a magnitude in subsequent equations or comparisons but retains a negative sign (e.g., plugging a negative H into magnitude-based inequalities or summations without absolute value or redefinition).
- The text interprets a negative value as a physical decrease without converting to magnitude or updating the convention (e.g., “Δh = −30 m, therefore the satellite drops 30 m per orbit,” with no statement that the reported value is signed and the magnitude is used).
- The solution mixes conventions midstream (e.g., starts with Δh = r − r′, later uses Δh = h′ − h implicitly, or sets H = −Δh without stating a redefinition) leading to sign flips that are not explicitly justified.

The rule does not flag if:
- The variable is explicitly defined as signed (e.g., Δh = h_f − h_i) and a negative result is correctly interpreted as a descent, while the reported descent magnitude is given as |Δh| or −Δh.
- The author clearly redefines variables (e.g., “we now use H := −Δh as the descent magnitude”) and uses them consistently thereafter.

Keywords/phrases monitored include: Δh, Δr, H, descent, drop, loss, decrease, altitude change, radius change, ‘positive for descent’, ‘downward positive’, ‘amount of descent’, ‘per orbit drop’. The rule targets cases where internal sign conventions for descent are contradicted by the sign of reported results or by their interpretation, as in reporting H negative after defining it as positive for a drop.

rules.title: Linear amplitude decrement with Coulomb friction in mass–spring oscillations
rules.description: Applies to a horizontal mass–spring system with constant kinetic friction (force magnitude F_f = μ m g) and initial release from x = d. Under sliding conditions (μ_s > μ), the turning-point amplitudes decrease linearly by 2 μ m g / k per half-cycle. The correct first return maximum displacement to the right is x_max = d − 4 μ m g / k. The verifier checks: (1) Energy accounting per half-cycle uses W_f = μ m g × (path length), with friction opposing motion in each leg; (2) The left turning amplitude satisfies 1/2 k A_left^2 = 1/2 k d^2 − μ m g (d + A_left) and simplifies to A_left = d − 2 μ m g / k; (3) The right turning amplitude follows A_right = A_left − 2 μ m g / k, giving x_max = d − 4 μ m g / k; (4) The derived x_max is linear in d and μ m g / k (equivalently d − 4 F_f / k) and has correct monotonicity: decreases with μ, m, g and increases with k, with x_max < d; (5) Dimensional consistency: 4 μ m g / k has units of length. Flag a calculation/modeling/sign error if the solution produces a quadratic or square-root expression for x_max that does not reduce to the linear relation above, if x_max ≥ d, if friction work is not equal to μ m g times total travel, or if the amplitude decrement per half-cycle is not 2 μ m g / k.

rules.title: Angle condition must depend on inter-contact friction μ_C and given angle θ
rules.description: Checks statics solutions for multi-body contact systems (e.g., two rods) where an inter-body friction coefficient (μ_C) is specified and a reference angle for one body (θ) is given. When the problem asks for an equilibrium condition on another angle α, the final equation/inequality for α must include dependence on both μ_C and θ. The verifier will: (1) detect from the problem statement that μ_C (rod-rod contact friction) and θ (angle of rod AB) are given; (2) extract the student's final condition for α; (3) verify that the final expression contains μ_C and θ as parameters. If either μ_C or θ is missing without an explicit, correct justification (e.g., a demonstrated cancellation from properly written equilibrium equations or a declared special case consistent with the problem), the solution is flagged. The rule also scans the derivation for inclusion of the inter-contact friction force in force/torque balances; if the rod-rod contact friction is never used, it is flagged as a conceptual omission. Typical violations include conclusions such as tan(α) ≥ 1/(2 μ_A), or any α-condition depending only on ground friction μ_A while omitting μ_C and θ. This rule helps catch oversimplifications that ignore required parameter dependencies arising from inter-contact friction and the given geometry.

rules.title: Unjustified Complementary Angle Assumptions Between Independent Bodies
rules.description: Checks for logically unsupported angle relations (e.g., θ + α = 90°, α = 90° − θ, sin α = cos θ, cos α = sin θ, cot α = tan θ) asserted between orientation angles that belong to different rigid bodies or contacts. Trigger: The solution introduces a complementary-angle identity linking two angles that reference distinct objects (e.g., two rods or two separate contacts with wall/floor). Validation: Search for explicit prior geometric constraints that mandate complementarity or perpendicularity, such as (a) the angles are acute angles of the same triangle with a stated right angle, (b) the bodies are declared perpendicular or share a rigid right-angle bracket or hinge, or (c) both angles are defined at the same vertex with a known right angle. If none of these justifications are present, flag a logic error. Rationale: In statics problems with multiple rods contacting a wall/floor, each rod’s angle with the wall is independently determined by equilibrium; wall smoothness, friction coefficients, or mere contact do not impose α + θ = 90°. This rule prevents incorrect simplifications like α = 90° − θ or cot α = tan θ without geometric basis.

rules.title: Torque-free radial mass ejection implies constant angular velocity
rules.description: This rule checks for misuse of angular momentum conservation on a rotating body that is losing (or gaining) mass radially with no tangential interaction. Applicability: problems where mass exits/enters through holes radially and flight time is ignored (i.e., no tangential impulse/torque on the source body during detachment). Verification checks: (1) If the solution asserts or derives a time-varying angular velocity for the source cylinder (e.g., cylinder A) solely because its moment of inertia decreases (uses d(I_A*omega_A)/dt = 0 for the source, or sets omega_A proportional to 1/I_A(t), or states "omega_A decreases as sand is ejected"), flag as a conceptual error. (2) Under the stated assumptions, the tangential torque on the source is zero, so the correct condition is d(omega_A)/dt = 0 and omega_A(t) = omega_A(0) throughout the ejection phase; the loss of angular momentum from the source is carried away by the mass flux (omega_A * dI_A/dt), not by a change in omega_A. (3) Ensure the initial condition omega_A(0) equals the given initial angular velocity (e.g., omega_0). (4) Only allow omega_A(t) to change if the solution explicitly models a tangential interaction (e.g., friction, inelastic sticking with tangential impulse) that exerts a torque on the source body. Example patterns to flag: "omega_A(t) = omega_0 * I_A(0)/I_A(t)", "d(I_A*omega_A)/dt = 0 for cylinder A", "omega_A decreases due to decreasing I_A" without introducing a tangential torque.

rules.title: Misuse of angular momentum conservation in planar sliding without rotation
rules.description: Flags solutions that invoke conservation of angular momentum as a necessary step in problems where bodies are constrained to slide without rotation and the interaction is along the line of centers. Detection criteria: (1) Problem context includes keywords such as "frictionless sliding", "can only slide", "no rotation", or describes symmetric setups with a push from the center (e.g., frog at the center of a circular leaf). (2) The solution states or uses "conservation of angular momentum" (e.g., "L is conserved", "sum of external torque is zero implies angular momentum conservation") to derive velocities or work, rather than recognizing that the relevant conserved quantity is linear momentum in the horizontal direction. (3) There is no explicit rotational degree of freedom or off-center impulse/force causing a torque; initial angular momentum is zero by symmetry (e.g., push from the center of a symmetric platform). The rule should not trigger if angular momentum is mentioned only to note it is zero and irrelevant or if the problem explicitly includes rotation (e.g., off-center push, spinning, rolling, or nonzero external torque). When triggered, the verifier should prompt: "Angular momentum conservation is unnecessary/misleading here; use linear momentum conservation in the horizontal direction to relate the bodies' velocities and determine work."

rules.title: Energy-only determination of velocity component when angular momentum is not conserved
rules.description:
This rule detects solutions that attempt to compute a specific velocity component (normal/tangential) using only mechanical energy conservation in problems where angular momentum is not conserved. Rationale: With planar motion in a non-central field (nonzero torque), energy conservation provides only one scalar relation, E = T + U, which constrains v^2 = ṙ^2 + (r θ̇)^2 but does not uniquely determine the decomposition into ṙ and θ̇. A second independent relation (e.g., the angular-momentum balance dL/dt = τ, an explicit θ̇(r) relation, a geometric/curvature constraint, or boundary/initial conditions used to eliminate ṙ) is required to solve for v_n or v_t.
The rule flags a solution if all of the following hold:
- The context indicates angular momentum is not conserved (explicitly stated or implied by a force with nonzero torque or a potential depending on angle).
- The solution invokes conservation of mechanical energy to determine v_n or v_t and does not introduce any additional independent dynamical or geometric relation (no use of dL/dt = τ, no derived θ̇(r) relation, no curvature/path constraint, no equivalent constraint from initial/boundary data).
- The obtained expression for the desired component either (a) is taken directly from v = sqrt(2/m (E − U)) without resolving the radial/tangential split, or (b) still contains ṙ or θ̇ (or both) that are not eliminated by a justified relation.
The rule does not trigger if the solution shows angular momentum is conserved, or derives and uses sopporting equations (e.g., dL/dt = τ integrated to relate θ̇ and r) or correct geometric constraints to eliminate the extra degree of freedom before isolating the velocity component.

rules.title: Include correct sin(angle) in translational angular momentum about a new contact point
rules.description: This rule checks computations of the translational contribution to angular momentum about a point that is not the instantaneous center of rotation. It targets impact/pivot-change scenarios (e.g., a rolling polygonal prism transitioning contact from one edge to the next) where students often assume the center-of-mass velocity v_CM is perpendicular to the position vector r_new from the center of mass to the new contact point. Checks performed: (1) When angular momentum about a point P is evaluated just before impact, verify that the translational term is written as L_trans = M |r_CM→P| |v_CM| sin(phi), where phi is the angle between r_CM→P and v_CM. Flag an error if the expression is simplified to M v R (i.e., sin(phi) implicitly set to 1) without justification that r_CM→P ⟂ v_CM. (2) If the body was rolling without slipping about an old contact point O_old prior to impact, infer that v_CM ⟂ r_CM→O_old, not necessarily r_CM→O_new. Require the solver to account for the geometry relating r_CM→O_old and r_CM→O_new. (3) For a regular N-gon transitioning to the next supporting edge, enforce phi = 90° − Δ with Δ = 2π/N, so sin(phi) = cos(Δ). For a hexagon (N = 6), this yields phi = 30° and sin(phi) = 1/2. Flag if the solution omits this factor or uses sin(phi) = 1. (4) Accept equivalent correct treatments (e.g., component-wise cross product or explicit dot/cross evaluation) that produce the same sin(phi) factor. (5) Also flag if the perpendicular assumption is justified using the old contact geometry for the new contact (i.e., conflating r_new with r_old). This rule is triggered whenever an impact/pivot-change angular momentum balance about the new contact point is used and the translational term lacks or mis-evaluates the required sin(angle) factor.

rules.title: Improper conservation of angular momentum about COM during impulsive collision
rules.description: This rule checks the use of angular momentum conservation in problems involving an impact/collision (keywords: collision, impact, impulsive, inelastic, perfectly inelastic, contact with ground/wall/floor). It flags solutions that: (1) claim angular momentum is conserved about the center of mass during the impulsive interval without explicitly justifying that the net external impulsive torque about the COM is zero (e.g., the impulse acts through the COM or all impulsive torques cancel). In typical ground/wall contacts, the contact impulse does not pass through the COM, so conservation about the COM is invalid. (2) compute angular momentum about the COM and incorrectly include a translational term like r_cm × m v_cm (e.g., using m v (l/2) or adding m v r terms) alongside I_cm ω; about the COM, H_COM must be I_COM ω only. (3) equate pre- and post-impact angular momentum using L = I ω with ω tied to v_CM during the collision while external impulses at a contact point exist; this is incorrect unless the chosen origin is one where the net external impulsive moment is zero. The rule expects that any conservation of angular momentum during an impulsive collision be performed about a point/axis with zero net external impulsive moment (commonly the instantaneous point of contact), with gravity treated as negligible over the short collision duration. If the solution uses COM as the reference or mixes translational and rotational terms incorrectly for COM, or omits justification for zero impulsive torque about the chosen origin, the rule should flag it as a logic error.

rules.title: Verify angular momentum conservation equation
rules.description: Angular momentum is conserved if no external torque acts on a system. Mathematically, L_initial = L_final, where L = Iω for rigid bodies (moment of inertia times angular velocity).
rules.check_logic: Check if the net external torque on the system is zero. If torque = 0, ensure L_initial = L_final. Verify that the moment of inertia and angular velocity are correctly calculated for all components of the system.
common_errors: Forgetting to check for external torques on the system.
Using incorrect moments of inertia for the system components.
Not accounting for changes in rotational inertia when the system configuration changes.

rules.title: Ensure consistent sign convention for angular momentum
rules.description: Angular momentum is a vector quantity. Its sign depends on the direction of rotation, usually determined using the right-hand rule.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the chosen direction (e.g., clockwise or counterclockwise) is consistently applied for all angular momentum and torque calculations. Ensure the right-hand rule is correctly applied to determine the direction of angular momentum vectors.
common_errors: Mixing up clockwise and counterclockwise directions in the same problem.
Applying the right-hand rule incorrectly for angular momentum directions.
Ignoring the vector nature of angular momentum and treating it as a scalar.

rules.title: Check validity of angular momentum conservation
rules.description: Angular momentum conservation only applies if the system is isolated with no external torques. Ensure this condition is satisfied before applying the conservation law.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the sum of external torques acting on the system is zero before applying angular momentum conservation. Explicitly check for frictional or other non-conservative forces that might introduce external torques.
common_errors: Applying angular momentum conservation when external torques are present.
Ignoring frictional or other non-conservative torques that act on the system.

rules.title: Verify dimensional consistency of angular momentum equations
rules.description: Angular momentum (L) has SI units of kg·m²/s. Ensure that all terms in the equations are dimensionally consistent.
rules.check_logic: Confirm that angular momentum, torque, and angular velocity terms respect their respective units (kg·m²/s, N·m, rad/s). Check that all derived quantities are dimensionally consistent.
common_errors: Using incorrect units for moment of inertia or angular velocity.
Adding or equating terms with incompatible dimensions (e.g., torque and angular momentum).

rules.title: Verify kinematic constraints in angular momentum systems
rules.description: For systems with geometric constraints (e.g., a pulley or rotating bar), ensure the angular velocity and radius relationships are correctly applied.
rules.check_logic: Check if v = rω is satisfied for linear and angular velocities, or if other constraints (e.g., rope length conservation) are respected. Verify that the radius used in torque or angular momentum calculations corresponds to the correct point of application.
common_errors: Incorrectly relating linear velocity to angular velocity.
Ignoring constraints imposed by fixed pivots or hinges.
Misinterpreting radius in the torque or angular momentum calculations.

rules.title: Verify torque-angular momentum relationship
rules.description: The rate of change of angular momentum equals the net external torque acting on the system: τ = dL/dt. Ensure this relationship holds when external torques are present.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the derivative of angular momentum matches the calculated torque for non-conservation cases. Ensure that the torque is calculated using the correct lever arm and force direction.
common_errors: Neglecting time-dependence of angular momentum in non-conservation cases.
Calculating torque incorrectly (e.g., using incorrect lever arm or force).
Confusing internal forces/torques with external ones.

rules.title: Account for system redefinition during motion
rules.description: If the system's boundaries change (e.g., a person moving inward on a rotating platform), ensure the change in moment of inertia is properly accounted for.
rules.check_logic: Check for changes in system configuration and verify that the moment of inertia and angular velocity are updated accordingly. Ensure that the conservation of angular momentum is applied correctly to the redefined system.
common_errors: Failing to adjust the moment of inertia for changing system boundaries.
Assuming angular velocity remains constant when the moment of inertia changes.
Incorrectly summing or redistributing masses in composite systems.

rules.title: Relate conservation of angular momentum to kinetic energy
rules.description: In systems where angular momentum is conserved, rotational kinetic energy may change if the moment of inertia changes. Verify the relationship between rotational kinetic energy (1/2 Iω²) and angular momentum.
rules.check_logic: Check if changes in rotational kinetic energy are consistent with conservation of angular momentum and changes in moment of inertia. Verify that the correct formulas for rotational kinetic energy and angular momentum are used.
common_errors: Incorrectly assuming rotational kinetic energy is conserved when angular momentum is conserved.
Failing to account for changes in angular velocity when moment of inertia changes.
Using incorrect formulas for rotational kinetic energy.

rules.title: Account for external forces affecting angular momentum
rules.description: External forces can create torques that affect angular momentum. Ensure all external forces and their lever arms are accounted for in torque calculations.
rules.check_logic: Verify that all external forces acting on the system are identified and their torques are calculated correctly. Ensure that the net torque is consistent with the observed changes in angular momentum.
common_errors: Ignoring external forces that create torques.
Incorrectly calculating lever arms for external forces.
Failing to distinguish between internal and external forces.

rules.title: Angular momentum non-conservation must be attributed to torques, not dissipation
rules.description:
This rule verifies explanations of angular momentum non-conservation in atmospheric or geophysical flows (e.g., Hadley circulation). It flags solutions that misattribute the loss of angular momentum to 'dissipation' by turbulence or to intrinsic properties (density/inertia, moisture) instead of external torques. The check consists of:

- Trigger conditions:
  - The text states or implies that turbulence, viscosity, or mixing 'dissipates', 'destroys', 'consumes', or 'loses' angular momentum (e.g., phrases like 'turbulence dissipates angular momentum', 'angular momentum is dissipated', 'momentum loss due to turbulence'), without concurrently framing turbulence as momentum transport/exchange that produces torques via stresses.
  - The explanation for non-conservation fails to mention external torques or stresses (surface friction/drag, turbulent/eddy stresses, pressure/stress torques) when discussing the lower branches/boundary layer.
  - The explanation attributes non-conservation to air density/inertia ('air is denser lower down so inertia slows rotation') or moisture content, with no reference to torques or momentum exchange.

- Required elements for a correct explanation:
  - Explicit recognition that angular momentum changes only under external torques; in the lower atmosphere these arise from surface friction (boundary layer drag) and turbulent/eddy stresses that exchange momentum between layers and with the surface.
  - Turbulence described as momentum transport/mixing producing effective (Reynolds) stresses and torques, not as a mechanism that intrinsically dissipates angular momentum (contrast with energy dissipation).

- Detection method (text-based):
  - Search for dissipation-related keywords in proximity to 'angular momentum' (dissipate/dissipation/destroy/consume/loss) and flag unless nearby terms include 'torque', 'stress', 'friction', 'drag', 'eddy', 'momentum exchange', or 'transport'.
  - Search for claims blaming 'density', 'inertia', or 'moisture/humidity' for angular momentum non-conservation without any mention of torque/stress; flag as concept error.
  - Validate that at least one correct torque source is named when explaining non-conservation along lower branches (e.g., surface friction/drag, turbulent/eddy stresses).

The rule aims to catch the common conceptual error of treating angular momentum like a dissipative quantity and to ensure explanations correctly attribute non-conservation to torques from frictional and turbulent stresses.

rules.title: No tangential speed from instantaneous radial change at turning point
rules.description: This rule checks for misuse of energy conservation and violation of angular-momentum constraints when a pendulum/swing length is changed instantaneously at an extreme point. Trigger conditions: (a) The solution identifies a highest/lowest point (turning point) where tangential speed is zero (v = 0, ω = 0) and thus angular momentum about the pivot is zero; (b) An instantaneous change of the radial distance (e.g., standing/squatting changing the COM distance r → r + Δr) is performed at that same angle with no external torque about the pivot (force along the radius only); (c) The solution then derives a nonzero tangential speed immediately after the change (v' > 0, ω' ≠ 0), typically by equating total mechanical energy before and after the instantaneous change (E_before = E_after) or by writing mgΔh = (1/2) m v'^2 at the same angular position. The rule flags: (1) Any claim that kinetic energy remains the same (or zero) at the turning point while also computing a nonzero tangential speed right after the radial change; (2) Any derivation that produces nonzero tangential velocity immediately after a purely radial, torque-free, instantaneous length change when the initial angular momentum is zero; (3) Application of energy conservation across the instantaneous internal actuation step to create tangential kinetic energy at the same angle. Rationale: With zero angular momentum and no external torque about the pivot, angular momentum must remain zero during an instantaneous radial change, so tangential speed cannot be created (ω' = 0). Mechanical energy may change due to work by the radial force, but it cannot instantaneously produce tangential kinetic energy when L = 0. Exceptions: Do not flag if the solution explicitly includes an external torque during the change (off-radial impulse, applied moment) or treats a finite-time process with nonzero torque that can change angular momentum.

rules.title: 复合系统角动量叠加
rules.description:
触发条件：计算包含自转和公转的系统总角动量
检查逻辑：验证是否正确区分并加总了刚体自转角动量 (Iω) 与质点/轨道公转角动量 (mr²ω)
rules.check_logic: 验证是否正确区分并加总了刚体自转角动量 (Iω) 与质点/轨道公转角动量 (mr²ω)
