rules.title: Correct indexing of spring constants in linear-chain normal-mode equations
rules.description: This rule verifies the equations of motion/normal-mode eigenvalue equations for a 1D linear molecule (N masses m_i connected by N−1 springs with constants k_1,…,k_{N−1}). It flags the common mistake of using the same spring constant k_i for both the left and right springs of atom i and of replacing the diagonal spring coefficient by 2·k_i instead of the sum of the neighboring spring constants. Checks performed: (1) Interior atoms (2 ≤ i ≤ N−1): The correct force balance is m_i x_i'' = k_{i−1}(x_{i−1} − x_i) + k_i(x_{i+1} − x_i). Under the normal-mode ansatz x_i(t) = A_i e^{iωt}, the algebraically equivalent forms are k_{i−1} x_{i−1} + k_i x_{i+1} − (k_{i−1} + k_i) x_i = −m_i ω^2 x_i or [(k_{i−1}+k_i) − m_i ω^2] x_i − k_{i−1} x_{i−1} − k_i x_{i+1} = 0. Flag an error if the interior equation uses k_i on both neighbor terms (x_{i−1} and x_{i+1}) and a diagonal coefficient 2·k_i (e.g., k_i x_{i−1} + (2 k_i − m_i ω^2) x_i + k_i x_{i+1} = 0), unless the solution explicitly and correctly assumes a uniform chain k_j ≡ k for all j. (2) Boundary atoms: i = 1 must use only k_1: m_1 x_1'' = k_1 (x_2 − x_1) ⇒ k_1 x_2 − k_1 x_1 = −m_1 ω^2 x_1. i = N must use only k_{N−1}: m_N x_N'' = k_{N−1} (x_{N−1} − x_N) ⇒ k_{N−1} x_{N−1} − k_{N−1} x_N = −m_N ω^2 x_N. Flag an error if boundary equations contain −2 k_1 x_1 or −2 k_{N−1} x_N or use mismatched spring indices. (3) Mass/frequency term placement: Ensure the inertial term appears as −m_i ω^2 x_i (or equivalently moved to the LHS) and is not mixed into neighbor coefficients. The rule triggers when the problem statement provides distinct spring constants k_1,…,k_{N−1} (nonuniform chain) and the solution’s coefficients do not map to k_{i−1} for x_{i−1}, k_i for x_{i+1}, and (k_{i−1}+k_i) for x_i for interior atoms, or when boundary equations include spurious duplicate spring contributions.

rules.title: Correct MOI for an oblate spheroid about its spin (polar) axis
rules.description: Checks the moment of inertia used for a uniformly dense oblate spheroid (axisymmetric ellipsoid) rotating about its symmetry/polar (spin) axis. For an ellipsoid with equatorial radius r_e (a = b = r_e) and polar radius r_p (c = r_p), the correct moment of inertia about the spin/polar (z) axis is I_z = (1/5) M (a^2 + b^2) = (2/5) M r_e^2. The polar radius r_p must not appear in I_z. The rule flags formulas that include r_p (e.g., I = (2/5) M * ((r_e^2 + r_p^2)/2), I = (1/5) M (r_e^2 + r_p^2), or any averaging/mixture of r_e and r_p in the spin-axis MOI). It also flags use of an average radius R_avg or combinations like (r_e + r_p)/2 within I_z. Conditions: apply when the body is explicitly modeled as a uniform oblate spheroid (a = b ≠ c) and the rotation axis is the symmetry/polar axis. Do not apply when the solution explicitly states a different physical model (e.g., thin shell, non-uniform density, rotation about an equatorial axis). The verifier should parse expressions for I, identify axis labels ("spin", "polar", "z-axis"), and confirm that I_z depends only on M and r_e^2 with the coefficient 2/5 (or algebraic equivalents of (1/5)(a^2+b^2) with a = b), and does not include r_p in any form.

rules.title: Correct sign and coefficient for drag-induced change in orbital radius
rules.description:
Checks the sign and numeric coefficient when converting drag work into a change in orbital radius (or semimajor axis) via orbital energy balance.

Scope:
- Applicable when a solution models orbital decay in a central gravitational field using the circular/near-circular energy relation E = -μ M/(2r) or the general semimajor-axis form E = -μ M/(2a), where μ = G M_E, M is the spacecraft mass, r (or a) is orbital radius (semimajor axis).
- Applicable when energy loss due to atmospheric drag per revolution is represented as W_drag = ∮ F_t ds, often approximated as W_drag ≈ F_drag · 2π r for a circular orbit with tangential drag F_drag ≥ 0 (magnitude).

Required physics relations:
1) Energy balance under dissipative drag: E' = E - W_drag.
2) From E = -μ M/(2a), the correct mapping is: 1/a' - 1/a = (2 W_drag)/(μ M) > 0.
   - For circular orbit a = r, per revolution: 1/r' - 1/r = (4π r F_drag)/(μ M) > 0.
3) In specific-energy form (per unit mass): ε = -μ/(2a), W_spec = W_drag/M, so 1/a' - 1/a = (2 W_spec)/μ.

What to flag:
- Wrong sign in energy update (e.g., E' = E + W_drag) for dissipative drag.
- Derived expressions where Δ(1/a) or Δ(1/r) has the wrong sign (≤ 0) when W_drag > 0, implying an increase in radius under drag.
- Missing factor of 2 when converting from ΔE to Δ(1/a): student uses Δ(1/a) = W_drag/(μ M) instead of (2 W_drag)/(μ M).
- Missing orbit-length factor when using force over a full revolution: student uses 1/r' - 1/r = (2π r F_drag)/(μ M) or with a negative sign; the correct coefficient per revolution is +4π.
- Dimensional inconsistency: the derived Δ(1/a) term must have units of 1/length; e.g., (F_drag·r)/(μ M) has correct units, sign must be positive.

Acceptance of equivalent correct forms:
- Using semimajor axis a instead of r.
- Using path integral W_drag = ∮ F_t ds with variable F_t; coefficient should be +2 times the integral divided by μ M.
- Using specific energy per unit mass and W_spec = ∮ a_t ds; then Δ(1/a) = (2 W_spec)/μ.

Implementation guidance:
- If the solution contains an equation matching pattern 1/a' = 1/a + k · (F_drag · r)/(μ M), require k = 4π (per revolution). If k ≠ 4π or sign is negative, flag.
- If the solution contains 1/a' = 1/a + c · W_drag/(μ M), require c = 2 and sign positive.
- Additionally, if the narrative asserts that drag increases orbital radius or makes energy less negative, flag for physical inconsistency.

rules.title: Per-orbit drag-induced radius change must include 4π coefficient
rules.description:
This rule checks the consistency of per-revolution orbital radius (or altitude) decrease derived from atmospheric drag for a near-circular orbit under small-change assumptions. For a circular orbit with orbital energy E(r) = -μ M_S/(2 r) (μ = G M_E), tangential drag force F_drag approximately constant over one orbit, and work per revolution W_drag = F_drag · 2π r, energy balance gives ΔE = -W_drag and dE/dr = +μ M_S/(2 r^2). Therefore the correct small-change result is Δr = -(4π F_drag r^3)/(μ M_S). The rule flags solutions that:
- Present Δr (or H, Δa) with a prefactor of 2π instead of 4π in the form Δr ∝ -C · F_drag · r^3/(μ M_S), where the expected coefficient C = 4π; or the numerical coefficient is off by a factor ≈2 (e.g., ratio of reported to expected coefficient in [0.45, 0.55] or [1.8, 2.2]).
- Compute dE/dr for a circular orbit as μ M_S/r^2 (missing the 1/2 factor), which leads to the same 2× underestimate in |Δr|.
- Use drag power P = F_drag v and period T = 2π√(r^3/μ) but still arrive at a coefficient equivalent to 2π rather than 4π.
Synonyms/notations recognized: μ = GM_E, M_S = satellite mass, r = orbital radius (R_E + h), Δa ≈ Δr for nearly circular orbits, H as per-orbit descent, F_drag may be given as D or F_t. Applicability: near-circular orbit, small per-orbit change, drag modeled as purely tangential and approximately constant over the orbit. The rule does not apply to strongly elliptical orbits or models with significant drag variation along the path without appropriate averaging. The verifier should parse the derived Δr expression (symbolic or numeric), compute the effective coefficient multiplying F_drag r^3/(μ M_S), and flag when it deviates by about a factor of two from the correct 4π value.

rules.title: Do not equate tangential deceleration dv/dt with radial descent rate dr/dt
rules.description: This rule flags solutions to orbital drag problems that conflate tangential speed change with orbital radius/altitude change. Specifically, it checks for any instance where a descent speed/rate (identified via symbols or phrases such as dh/dt, dr/dt, altitude loss rate, u_desc, u_ind) is set equal to dv/dt, a_t, or F_drag/m, or where altitude loss per revolution is computed by integrating dv/dt over an orbital period without converting to changes in orbital energy/semi-major axis. The rule also performs a dimensional sanity check: dv/dt has units of m/s^2 while dh/dt or dr/dt must be m/s; equating them is dimensionally inconsistent. For circular (or near-circular) orbits under drag, the correct approach must use the orbital energy–semi-major axis relation (E = -μ m/(2 a) or per-unit-mass ε = -μ/(2 a)) and drag power (dE/dt = -F_drag v or dε/dt = -(F_drag/m) v) to derive da/dt (and hence dr/dt for circular orbits), e.g., da/dt = -(2 a^2/μ) v a_t. A solution passes this rule if it explicitly transforms tangential deceleration into semi-major axis/radius change via energy balance or Gauss’s planetary equations, and fails if it directly identifies dv/dt with dh/dt/dr/dt or uses tangential deceleration alone to compute altitude change.

rules.title: Use total mechanical energy in orbital decay power balance
rules.description: Detects solutions for orbital decay under a dissipative force (e.g., drag, electromagnetic induction) that equate drag power solely to the time derivative of kinetic energy. In bound Keplerian motion, energy loss from drag reduces the total mechanical energy E = K + U, not just kinetic energy. For circular or near-circular orbits, the correct energy relation is E = -GM m/(2 r) (or E = -GM m/(2 a) for general elliptic orbits). The correct power balance is dE/dt = -F_drag · v_tan, and the radius/semi-major axis change must follow from dE/dt via dE/dr (or dE/da), e.g., for circular orbits: dE/dr = GM m/(2 r^2) ⇒ dr/dt = -(2 r^2/(GM m)) F_drag v. Flag the solution if it uses any of the following kinetic-only balances in an orbital context: m v dv/dt = -F_drag v, d/dt(1/2 m v^2) = -F_drag v, or dv/dt = -F_drag/m, without introducing the gravitational potential energy term or the total energy E = -GM m/(2 r or 2 a). Also flag if the derived decay rate lacks the required r- (or a-) dependence from dE/dr (or dE/da). The rule applies when the problem involves satellites/spacecraft in Earth's (or a central body's) gravitational field and discusses descent/decay due to drag or induced electromagnetic effects.

rules.title: Do not assume immediate circular orbit after impulsive tangential speed change
rules.description:
Scope: Orbital mechanics problems where a body on a circular orbit receives an instantaneous, tangential velocity change at a fixed radius (e.g., due to an inelastic collision from behind). The central gravitational field is Keplerian (parameter mu = GM_planet).

What to check:
- If a solution treats the post-impulse motion as a new circular orbit determined by v' = sqrt(mu/R') or by equating centripetal force to gravity (m v'^2 / R' = mu m / R'^2) to solve for a new radius R' immediately after the impulse, flag this as a modeling error unless an explicit circularization mechanism (e.g., a second impulse or dissipation) is provided.
- The correct post-impulse orbit is generally elliptical, with the collision point at pericenter if the tangential speed increases (v' > v0) and at apocenter if the tangential speed decreases (v' < v0). The radius at the instant of impulse remains the same (r = R); it does not jump to R'.
- A correct method must use the vis-viva equation at the collision radius r = R: v'^2 = mu (2/R − 1/a), along with angular momentum conservation for the instantaneous state h' = R v'_t (for purely tangential impulses) to determine the ellipse parameters (semimajor axis a and eccentricity e). Then pericenter/apocenter distances are r_p = a(1 − e), r_a = a(1 + e). For v' > v0 on an initial circular orbit, r_p = R and r_a = 2a − R.
- For requests about “maximum deviation” from the original orbit radius, the solution must compare the apoapsis or periapsis radius to R as appropriate. Any approach that outputs a single new circular radius R' or a percentage change derived from circular-orbit formulas (e.g., R' ∝ 1/v'^2) without ellipse analysis should be flagged.

Heuristics for auto-detection:
- Presence of phrases/formulas like “new circular orbit”, “set centripetal force equal to gravity after collision”, “v'^2 = mu/R'”, or “R' = mu/v'^2” used immediately after an impulse/collision at radius R, with no mention of ellipse/vis-viva/angular momentum, is indicative of the error.
- Absence of vis-viva usage and ellipse parameters (a, e, r_p, r_a) in the post-impulse analysis is a red flag.
- Numeric sanity check for a common case: for a 5% tangential speed increase at radius R (v' = 1.05 v0 with v0 = sqrt(mu/R)), the correct results are approximately a ≈ 1.114 R, e ≈ 0.102, and r_a ≈ 1.227 R. A reported deviation near 22–23% is consistent; answers near 9–10% typically arise from the incorrect circular-orbit assumption and should be flagged.

Rationale: An impulsive velocity change at a fixed position changes the orbital energy and angular momentum instantaneously but cannot instantaneously change the position. The resulting orbit is conic (elliptical here), not circular, unless a specific additional action circularizes the orbit.

rules.title: Correct apsis identification after tangential speed change from circular orbit
rules.description:
Checks that solutions correctly identify which apsis (perigee/apogee) coincides with the impulse/collision point when an instantaneous tangential speed change is applied on a circular orbit. Specifically:
- If the event reduces speed (retrograde Δv < 0, e.g., inelastic collision), the impulse point must be the apogee (r_a = r0). The perigee is on the opposite side of the ellipse, with r_p = 2a − r0 and r_p < r_a. Flag if the solution sets the perigee equal to the collision radius (r_p = r0) or states that the collision point is the perigee/closest approach.
- If the event increases speed (prograde Δv > 0), the impulse point must be the perigee (r_p = r0). The apogee is opposite, with r_a = 2a − r0 and r_a > r_p. Flag if the solution sets the apogee equal to the collision radius (r_a = r0) or states that the collision point is the apogee/farthest point.
- Consistency check using speeds: At the impulse point, if Δv < 0 then the post-impulse speed must be less than the local circular speed (v' < sqrt(μ/r0)), which corresponds to apogee; if Δv > 0 then v' > sqrt(μ/r0), corresponding to perigee. Flag any mismatch between claimed apsis and the implied speed relation.
This rule catches the common conceptual error of misidentifying the collision/burn point as the perigee after a retrograde impulse from a circular orbit; the correct identification is that the collision/burn point becomes the apogee, with the perigee opposite on the new ellipse.

rules.title: Validate Earth-orbit orbital speed against vis-viva (μ/a) to catch order-of-magnitude errors
rules.description:
This rule checks that any computed orbital speed for a satellite orbiting Earth is consistent with the vis-viva relation using Earth's standard gravitational parameter. It is designed to detect large numerical mistakes or unit confusions (e.g., reporting km/s as m/s) that propagate through a solution.

What the rule does:
- Trigger: When a solution provides an orbital speed v for an Earth satellite and either a semi-major axis a, an orbital radius r, or an orbital period T.
- Constants: Use Earth's μ in the range 3.95e14 to 3.99e14 m^3/s^2.
- Reference speed computation:
  - If the orbit is stated or implied to be circular (or near-circular), compute v_ref = sqrt(μ/a).
  - If an elliptical orbit is specified with both semi-major axis a and instantaneous radius r, compute v_ref = sqrt(μ * (2/r - 1/a)).
  - If only the period T is given, first compute a via a = (μ * T^2 / (4π^2))^(1/3), then apply the circular formula for v_ref.
- Comparison: Extract the student's reported speed v_stud (ensure units). Flag an error if the relative deviation |v_stud − v_ref| / v_ref > 0.15 (15%).
- Unit-consistency checks:
  - If v_stud is closer to v_ref/1000 or v_ref*1000 within 10%, flag likely m/s vs km/s confusion.
- Sanity range checks for Earth orbits:
  - For a in [6.4e6, 1e8] m, expected speeds are roughly 1.9–7.9 km/s. Flag speeds below 1 km/s or above 10 km/s unless the solution justifies non-Keplerian effects.

Example of error this catches: For μ ≈ 3.95e14 m^3/s^2 and a ≈ 4.52e7 m, the correct circular speed is ≈ 2.96 km/s (≈ 2960 m/s). A reported value ≈ 933 m/s deviates by ~69% and is flagged.

rules.title: Heliocentric speed must be computed by vector subtraction and vis-viva; Δv ≠ v0
rules.description: Checks retrograde (antiparallel) burns at Earth’s orbit intended to send a spacecraft ballistically to the Sun. The rule enforces two required relations: (1) frame transformation: the post-burn heliocentric speed must be v_S = |v0 − v_E|, where v0 is Earth’s heliocentric orbital speed and v_E is the Earth-frame impulse (Δv), and (2) orbital energy/geometry: v_S at aphelion must satisfy the vis-viva relation for an ellipse with aphelion r_a ≈ Earth–Sun distance and perihelion r_p ≤ Solar radius (or derived from the given solar angular diameter α without small-angle approximation via r_p ≈ r_a·tan(α/2)). Using v0^2 = μ_☉/r_a to eliminate μ_☉, a correct solution should obtain v_S = v0·sqrt(2 r_p/(r_a + r_p)) and then Δv = v_E = v0 − v_S. The rule flags errors if any of the following are detected: • The solution sets v_S = v0 in the Sun frame after a retrograde burn, or asserts Δv = v0 without deriving v_S from vis-viva/geometry. • The solution equates the spacecraft speed in the Earth frame to the Sun-frame speed (treats both as v0) or otherwise ignores the subtraction v_S = v0 − v_E. • The solution uses an incorrect sign (v_S = v0 + v_E) for an antiparallel burn. • The solution violates 0 < v_S < v0 for a finite solar target size (α > 0 or r_p > 0). • Numeric outputs where Δv/v0 ≥ 0.95 with finite α (or r_p > 0) and no energy-based justification are flagged as likely equating Δv to v0. This rule targets internal consistency between frames and the required orbital-energy reduction to achieve a Sun-grazing/impact trajectory.

rules.title: Missing rotational inertia factor in period of rolling small oscillations
rules.description: Checks solutions to small-oscillation problems where a rigid body rolls without slipping (e.g., a cylinder or sphere on a circular track) to ensure the period T includes the rotational inertia correction required by the rolling constraint. Trigger conditions: the problem statement contains phrases like "rolls without slipping" and asks for the period of small oscillations about equilibrium; the final period is expressed as T = 2π √(L/g) with L a geometric length (e.g., R or R − r) and lacks the dimensionless factor √(1 + I/(m r^2)). Correct formulation: for a body of mass m, radius r, and moment of inertia I about its center, moving on a path of effective radius L (e.g., L = R − r for rolling inside a cylinder), the period must scale as T = 2π √(L/g) × √(1 + I/(m r^2)). Shape-specific checks: solid cylinder I = (1/2) m r^2 ⇒ factor √(3/2); solid sphere I = (2/5) m r^2 ⇒ factor √(7/5); hoop I = m r^2 ⇒ factor √(2). Flag as an error if the reported T omits this factor or uses a factor inconsistent with the object's stated geometry/inertia. Also flag if the derivation shows kinetic energy or equations of motion that include only translational terms (½ m v^2) while explicitly stating rolling without slipping, since the rotational term (½ I ω^2) must be present and leads to the same correction.

rules.title: Verify Angular Frequency and Linear Frequency Relationship
rules.description: For Simple Harmonic Motion, angular frequency ω is related to linear frequency f by ω = 2πf. This relationship is fundamental for oscillatory systems.
rules.check_logic: Ensure ω = 2πf is used correctly in calculations relating angular frequency and linear frequency, and verify unit consistency (e.g., radians per second for ω and hertz for f).
common_errors: Incorrect conversion factor between ω and f
Using linear frequency instead of angular frequency in equations

rules.title: Check Energy Conservation in SHM Systems
rules.description: In ideal Simple Harmonic Motion, mechanical energy is conserved. The sum of kinetic and potential energy in the system remains constant.
rules.check_logic: Verify if E_total = E_kinetic + E_potential remains constant over time, and ensure proper expressions for kinetic energy (1/2 mv²) and potential energy (1/2 kx²) are used.
common_errors: Ignoring potential energy contributions near maximum displacement
Forgetting kinetic energy at equilibrium position
Incorrect expressions for energy terms

rules.title: Validate Position and Velocity Equations for Spring-Mass Systems
rules.description: Position x(t) and velocity v(t) of a mass on a spring are given by x(t) = A cos(ωt + φ) and v(t) = -Aω sin(ωt + φ), where A is amplitude and φ is the phase constant.
rules.check_logic: Verify that position and velocity equations are correctly applied with proper amplitude, angular frequency, and phase constants. Ensure units are consistent and trigonometric functions are correctly evaluated.
common_errors: Incorrect sign for velocity expression
Misidentifying amplitude or missing phase shift
Using incorrect angular frequency in equations

rules.title: Ensure Correct Sign Convention for Forces and Displacements
rules.description: In SHM, the restoring force is typically considered negative in direction opposite to displacement (F = -kx for spring systems).
rules.check_logic: Check that restoring forces are consistently negative when displacements are positive, and verify that Hooke's Law is applied correctly.
common_errors: Misinterpretation of force directions
Incorrect sign usage when applying Hooke's Law
Confusion between restoring force and applied force

rules.title: Verify Validity Conditions for SHM Applicability
rules.description: SHM applies in systems where net restoring forces are proportional to displacement and damping forces are negligible.
rules.check_logic: Ensure system criteria such as linear restoring force proportionality (e.g., Hooke's Law) and negligible damping are met. Verify that the system is not influenced by external forces or significant non-linearities.
common_errors: Applying SHM principles in non-linear force systems
Ignoring damping effects which invalidate ideal SHM assumption
Overlooking external forces affecting the system

rules.title: Ensure Dimensional Consistency in SHM Equations
rules.description: All equations in SHM should be dimensionally consistent. Units must balance, specifically for ω, x(t), and v(t).
rules.check_logic: Check if each term in equations maintains consistent dimensions, particularly length [L], time [T], and mass [M]. Ensure angular frequency is in radians per second, position in meters, and velocity in meters per second.
common_errors: Using incorrect units for angular frequency
Mixing units inconsistently in calculations
Overlooking dimensional consistency in derived equations

rules.title: Validate Period-Time Relation in Oscillations
rules.description: The period T of a mass-spring oscillator is calculated as T = 2π√(m/k). This applies under ideal conditions of simple harmonic oscillators.
rules.check_logic: Verify whether the calculated period matches T = 2π√(m/k) using the correct formula, proper unit conversion, and accurate values for mass and spring constant.
common_errors: Incorrect physical constant usage
Using period formulas outside applicable contexts
Neglecting unit consistency in mass or spring constant

rules.title: Check for Phase Shift Due to Damping in Real Oscillators
rules.description: Real-world oscillators may exhibit phase shifts due to damping forces. Evaluate phase changes in the presence of damping.
rules.check_logic: Determine if phase shifts have been correctly factored into calculations where damping is present. Verify that the damping coefficient and its effect on the phase constant are accurately considered.
common_errors: Ignoring phase shift in damped systems
Incorrect adjustment of phase constant in damped scenarios
Overlooking the relationship between damping and angular frequency

rules.title: Verify Initial Conditions for SHM Systems
rules.description: Initial conditions, such as initial displacement and velocity, determine the phase constant and amplitude in SHM equations.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that initial conditions are correctly applied to determine the phase constant φ and amplitude A. Verify that x(0) and v(0) are consistent with the given equations.
common_errors: Incorrectly calculating phase constant from initial conditions
Ignoring initial velocity or displacement in calculations
Using inconsistent initial conditions in equations

rules.title: 区分受迫驻波与自由振动本征模
rules.description:
触发条件：题目给定驱动频率 ω 且一端固定、一端受迫振动时
检查逻辑：驻波表达式必须以驱动频率 ω 为自变量，且分母通常包含 sin(kL) 或 cos(kL) 项，不能假设 kL 必须等于 nπ/2。
rules.check_logic: 驻波表达式必须以驱动频率 ω 为自变量，且分母通常包含 sin(kL) 或 cos(kL) 项，不能假设 kL 必须等于 nπ/2。
rules.trigger: 题目给定驱动频率 ω 且一端固定、一端受迫振动时

rules.title: 固定端点相位突变校验
