rules.check_logic: Confirm that angles are correctly used to resolve vectors into components, with correct application of trigonometric functions and consistent units (e.g., radians or degrees).
common_errors: Incorrectly resolving velocity or displacement vectors without regard to angles
Using incorrect trigonometric functions based on angle orientation (e.g., sine versus cosine)
Failing to convert angle units consistently when necessary

rules.title: 非惯性系相对加速度合成准则
rules.description:
触发条件：物体在加速运动的容器（电梯、小车）内做自由落体或抛体运动
检查逻辑：检查相对加速度是否满足 a_rel = a_obj - a_frame。若a_obj=g(下)，a_frame=a(上)，则标量模长应相加。
rules.check_logic: 检查相对加速度是否满足 a_rel = a_obj - a_frame。若a_obj=g(下)，a_frame=a(上)，则标量模长应相加。
rules.trigger: 物体在加速运动的容器（电梯、小车）内做自由落体或抛体运动

rules.title: 脱离瞬间相对初速度归零律
rules.description:
触发条件：物体从运动载体上“松脱”、“掉落”或“静止释放”
检查逻辑：确认在载体参考系下，物体脱离瞬间的相对初速度 v_rel 必须设为 0，而非载体对地速度。
rules.check_logic: 确认在载体参考系下，物体脱离瞬间的相对初速度 v_rel 必须设为 0，而非载体对地速度。
rules.trigger: 物体从运动载体上“松脱”、“掉落”或“静止释放”

rules.title: Initial relative velocity must be zero at release in the platform frame
rules.description: Checks solutions that analyze motion in the frame of a moving platform (e.g., elevator, vehicle) for incorrect initialization of the object's relative velocity when the object is released/detaches/drops from the platform. If the object was mechanically attached and moving with the platform up to the release instant, then its initial velocity relative to the platform at t = 0 must be v_rel0 = 0 unless the problem explicitly states a throw/kick/projection relative to the platform. The rule flags cases where: (1) v_rel0 is set equal to the platform's absolute speed at release (a common error), or any non-zero value without explicit justification; (2) the relative displacement equation s_rel = v_rel0·t + (1/2)·a_rel·t^2 includes a non-zero v_rel0 term while the text indicates simple release; (3) the narrative claims 'relative to the elevator' (or similar) but uses the platform's absolute speed as the object's initial relative speed. As a consistency aid, the rule also checks that, for vertical motion under gravity, the relative acceleration magnitude in the platform frame is |a_rel| = g + |a_platform,vertical| (sign according to the chosen axis), so the time to traverse a fixed elevator gap should come from s_rel = (1/2)·a_rel·t^2 without a v_rel0 term when there is no launch. Exceptions: non-zero v_rel0 is allowed only if the solution explicitly states the object is given an additional velocity relative to the platform at release or if the analysis is performed entirely in an external inertial frame (in which case v0 is the platform's absolute velocity, but the solution should not call it 'relative to the platform').

rules.title: Verify the resonance condition for driving frequency
rules.description: The resonance condition occurs when the driving frequency matches the natural frequency of the system. For a harmonic oscillator, this is given by ω_d = ω_0, where ω_d is the driving frequency, and ω_0 = sqrt(k/m) is the natural frequency.
rules.check_logic: Check if the driving frequency (ω_d) equals the natural frequency (ω_0 = sqrt(k/m)).
common_errors: Using an incorrect expression for the natural frequency, e.g., forgetting the square root.
Confusing angular frequency (ω) with linear frequency (f) by not using ω = 2πf.
Not accounting for the mass (m) or spring constant (k) in ω_0.

rules.title: Verify the equation of motion for damped oscillations
rules.description: The equation of motion for damped oscillations is m(d²x/dt²) + b(dx/dt) + kx = 0, where b is the damping coefficient.
rules.check_logic: Verify the presence and correct expression of the inertial force (m(d²x/dt²)), damping force (b(dx/dt)), and restoring force (kx).
common_errors: Omitting the damping term (b(dx/dt)).
Using incorrect sign conventions (e.g., wrong signs for forces).
Failing to include the mass (m) in the inertial term.

rules.title: Verify boundary and initial conditions for oscillations
rules.description: Ensure the initial displacement and velocity are correctly applied to the solution of the damped or driven oscillation equation.
rules.check_logic: Check if initial conditions (e.g., x(0) and dx/dt|_(t=0)) are correctly substituted into the differential equation solution.
common_errors: Using incorrect or arbitrary initial conditions.
Misinterpreting the initial velocity as initial displacement.
Failing to consistently apply initial conditions across all terms.

rules.title: Verify energy dissipation in damped oscillations
rules.description: In damped oscillations, total mechanical energy decreases over time due to the damping force. The energy at any time is E(t) = (1/2)m(dx/dt)² + (1/2)kx², decreasing monotonically.
rules.check_logic: Ensure E(t) is correctly computed and decreases over time for a damped oscillator.
common_errors: Forgetting to include kinetic or potential energy terms in E(t).
Not accounting for the work done by the damping force.
Using an incorrect sign for energy dissipation.

rules.title: Verify consistent sign conventions for forces and displacements
rules.description: In oscillatory motion, restoring forces oppose displacement and damping forces oppose velocity.
rules.check_logic: Ensure restoring force is -kx and damping force is -b(dx/dt), using negative signs to indicate opposition.
common_errors: Assigning a positive sign to the restoring force.
Reversing the direction of the damping force.
Inconsistent sign conventions across terms in the equation.

rules.title: Verify dimensional consistency of equations
rules.description: Confirm that all terms in the equation have dimensions of force (ML/T²). Check m(d²x/dt²), b(dx/dt), and kx.
rules.check_logic: Verify that each term has dimensions of force. Mass should be M, damping coefficient should be ML/T, and spring constant should be ML/T².
common_errors: Using incorrect units for mass, damping coefficient, or spring constant.
Failing to ensure consistency between angular frequency and linear frequency.
Neglecting the time squared factor in acceleration terms.

rules.title: Verify calculation of the quality factor (Q)
rules.description: The quality factor (Q) quantifies resonance sharpness, given by Q = ω_0/(2β), where β = b/(2m).
rules.check_logic: Calculate Q using Q = ω_0/(2β), ensuring β = b/(2m).
common_errors: Using an incorrect formula for damping coefficient β.
Confusing damping constant b with coefficient per unit mass.
Failing to relate Q to resonance sharpness.

rules.title: Coefficient of restitution must use justified rebound height from provided data
rules.description: When verifying a solution that computes the coefficient of restitution (e) for a ball-ground collision with negligible air resistance, ensure the rebound parameter used is traceable to the problem data. Specifically: (1) If e is computed via heights (e = sqrt(h_rebound / h_drop)), the initial drop height h_drop must match the given release height, and the rebound height h_rebound must be explicitly obtained from the provided figure/data (e.g., the first post-collision peak in y(t)) or derived from a stated, verifiable kinematic calculation. (2) Flag the solution if a numerical h_rebound (or post-impact speed) is introduced without citation/derivation from the problem’s figure or text (e.g., an arbitrary/guessed value like “h1 = 0.8 m” without reading from the graph). (3) Check consistency: h_rebound ≤ h_drop and e ∈ [0,1] for passive collisions; flag if violated. (4) If the problem specifies reporting precision (e.g., three significant figures), flag if the final e does not adhere. This rule targets unsupported or incorrect numerical inputs for rebound height/velocity in restitution calculations, especially when a graph is provided and must be read to obtain h_rebound.

rules.title: Normal force on a riding mass must exclude spring force and depend on platform acceleration
rules.description: This rule verifies the force balance and normal-force expression for a mass m riding on/top of another mass M that is attached to a vertical spring. It checks that the free-body diagram of m includes only gravity (m g) and the contact normal force N, and that the equation of motion for m is written as N - m g = m a (with a equal to the vertical acceleration of the supporting platform). The rule flags the following errors: (1) Inclusion of spring force terms (e.g., ± k x) or any other forces not directly acting on m in the force balance for m, such as equations of the form N - k x = m a or N = m g + k x. (2) Expressing the normal force N(t) directly as a function of spring extension x(t) rather than platform acceleration x''(t), e.g., using N = m g - k x instead of N = m g - m x''(t). (3) Having N(t) scale incorrectly with M (e.g., N ∝ M g cos(ω t)) rather than with m, or using M as the leading multiplicative factor outside acceleration ratios for the oscillatory part. (4) When an explicit maximum is computed for the typical “released from support” SHM setup, failing the structural relation N_max = m g + m |a_min| (equivalently N(t) = m[g - x''(t)] with the maximum occurring at the most downward acceleration). The rule is intended to catch calculation errors arising from incorrect free-body isolation of m and misattribution of spring forces to m, as well as physically inconsistent dependence of N on the wrong mass or on spring extension rather than acceleration.

rules.title: Improper linear momentum conservation in collisions with fixed pivots/rigid supports
rules.description: This rule flags solutions that assert conservation of linear momentum (e.g., total or horizontal momentum) during a brief collision for a system attached to a fixed pivot/hinge/cantilever/rigid support, without demonstrating that the constraint exerts zero impulse in the claimed conserved direction. Checks: (1) Problem context mentions an anchored constraint to ground (keywords: pivot O, hinge, cantilever, axle, fixed support, rigidly mounted). (2) Event involves a collision/impact/instantaneous interaction (keywords: collision, impact, strike, impulsive). (3) Solution text claims that linear momentum is conserved (keywords: linear momentum is conserved, horizontal momentum conserved, no external forces/impulses during the collision, external forces negligible because collision is instantaneous) for the combined system (keywords: system as a whole, bullet+block, composite system). The rule triggers if these are present and there is no explicit justification that the constraint impulse is zero in the stated direction (e.g., ideal vertical string so no horizontal impulse, frictionless slider that cannot transmit impulse along the claimed direction). Gravity being negligible is not a sufficient justification: constraint reactions at fixed supports can deliver finite impulsive forces, often with horizontal components. The rule also flags self-contradiction where a solution first asserts linear momentum conservation due to 'negligible external forces' and later acknowledges that pivot/support reactions invalidate momentum conservation. Exceptions: Do not trigger if the solution explicitly demonstrates that the constraint force cannot provide impulse along the conserved direction (e.g., ideal string tension purely vertical and conservation claimed only for horizontal momentum), or if conservation is applied to an appropriately isolated larger system that includes the support/ground or is restricted to directions orthogonal to any possible constraint impulse.

rules.title: Rigid-body point-velocity sign analysis under off-center impulse
rules.description: This rule checks for incorrect assumptions about the direction of the rotational (ω × r) contribution relative to the translational center-of-mass (COM) velocity when computing the velocity of a point on a rigid body immediately after an impulse is applied at an offset from the COM. The verifier scans solutions to problems where a lateral impulse P is applied at a point located a distance from the COM (e.g., a rod of length 2ℓ with COM at ℓ above the bottom, impulse applied at height h). Correct analysis requires: (1) determining the sign of the induced angular velocity from the angular impulse L_z = (r_imp-from-CM) × P, which for the rod is proportional to (h − ℓ)P and thus ω_z ∝ sgn(h − ℓ); and (2) computing the point velocity using v_point = v_C + ω × r_point, so that the component along the impulse direction can be opposite to v_C depending on geometry. The rule flags solutions that: (a) unconditionally state that the rotational contribution at a specific point (e.g., the top end A) is in the same direction as the COM translational velocity without evaluating the sign via the cross product or the (h − ℓ) factor; (b) combine magnitudes as v_A = v_C + ω d (e.g., d = ℓ) without a sign or conditional dependence on h; or (c) present |v_A| = v_C + ω d as a magnitude expression without acknowledging that the correct magnitude is |v_C ± ω d| with the sign set by sgn(h − ℓ) via the right-hand rule. The rule accepts solutions that explicitly include the sign through a cross-product calculation, use a sgn(h − ℓ) factor, or write the magnitude as |v_A| = |v_C − ω ℓ| (or equivalently |v_C + sgn(h − ℓ) ω ℓ|), reflecting that the rotational term aligns with v_C only if the impulse point is above the COM (h > ℓ) and opposes it if h < ℓ. This rule generalizes to any rigid-body impulse problem where point velocities are formed by combining COM translation with rotation; unconditional same-direction claims for the rotational term are considered conceptual errors.

rules.title: Misuse of v_cm = ω r without instantaneous center/pivot justification
rules.description:
This rule flags the unjustified use of the kinematic relation v_cm = ω r (e.g., v_cm = ω (l/2) for a rod) to couple translational and rotational motion in plane rigid-body problems. The equality v_cm = ω r is only valid when the body undergoes pure rotation about a stationary point (fixed pivot/hinge) or about an instantaneous center of rotation (ICR) that is at rest relative to the ground (e.g., rolling without slipping with v_contact = 0). In general plane motion (such as a freely falling or sliding rod without a fixed pivot or no-slip constraint), v_cm and ω are independent and must be related via proper constraints or dynamics.

Detection criteria:
- Identify steps where the solution sets v_cm equal to ω times a geometric length (R, l/2, l, etc.), or uses this to eliminate variables in energy/momentum equations (e.g., substituting v_cm = ω r into KE = 1/2 m v_cm^2 + 1/2 I ω^2).
- Check whether, prior to using v_cm = ω r, the solution explicitly establishes one of the following: (1) a fixed pivot/hinge at a known point; (2) a no-slip condition at a contact point with v_contact = 0, thereby defining an ICR; or (3) an explicit identification of an ICR accompanied by a statement that the chosen point’s velocity relative to the ground is zero.
- If none of these justifications are present, flag the step as an invalid kinematic constraint.

Context-specific note for impacts: Post-impact use of v_cm = ω r is permitted only if the solution clearly states that the contact point sticks (perfectly inelastic with sticking) so that v_contact = 0 immediately after impact, establishing a pivot. Otherwise, the relation must not be imposed.

Corrective guidance: Require the use of general rigid-body kinematics v_P = v_CM + ω × r_P/CM and derive any relations between v_CM and ω from actual constraints (fixed pivot, no-slip, sticking contact) or from dynamics (impulse-momentum, energy) rather than imposing v_cm = ω r by default.

rules.title: Rolling ring small-oscillation frequency must include V-dependent gyroscopic term
rules.description: This rule verifies the small-oscillation frequency for a high-speed rolling ring oscillating near the vertical plane. In this context (CM approximately along x-axis with constant speed V; small y, θ, φ), the lowest-order linearization must produce a frequency that depends on V due to gyroscopic stabilization. Specifically, the correct leading-order result is Ω^2 = (8 V^2)/(3 R^2) − (2 g)/(3 R). The rule flags errors when: (a) Ω is reported as √(g/R) or any expression independent of V; (b) the Ω^2 expression lacks both terms proportional to V^2/R^2 and g/R; (c) the numerical coefficients in Ω^2 differ from 8/3 and 2/3 at lowest order; (d) the stability threshold V_min is not computed from Ω^2 ≥ 0, i.e., V_min must equal √(g R)/2. It also checks that the derivation retains the lowest-order V-dependent coupling terms arising from rolling constraints and gyroscopic effects; omitting these terms indicates an incorrect linearization.

rules.title: Circular band tension must use total circumferential extension ΔL = 2π(r − R)
rules.description: Applies to problems modeling a uniform circular ring/band with an undeformed radius R and a single stiffness coefficient k (for the entire band). The rule verifies that the elastic relation uses the total change in circumference, ΔL = 2πr − 2πR = 2π(r − R), not just the radial change r − R. Specifically: (1) If the solution writes the elastic tension/force as T = k(r − R), or uses elastic energy U = (1/2)k(r − R)^2, flag an error for omitting the 2π factor. Correct forms include T = k·ΔL = 2πk(r − R), τ (tension per unit circumference) = T/(2πr) = k·ΔL/(2πr), and U = (1/2)k(ΔL)^2. (2) If the solution claims the tension is 'per unit length' but still uses the same k given in the statement (units N/m for the whole ring), require an explicit redefinition to a per-length stiffness k' = k/(2π) with units N/m^2; otherwise flag as a constitutive misuse. (3) Unit consistency check: with k in N/m (global stiffness), the length argument must be ΔL; using r − R directly without converting to circumference is a modeling error. This rule is triggered whenever the problem text provides a single stiffness coefficient k for a ring and the solution relates T or U to r − R without introducing ΔL or an explicit, correctly-unitized per-length stiffness.

rules.title: Static ring on surface of revolution: must use geometric force balance, not energy minimization
rules.description: Flags solutions that model a non-rotating (horizontal equilibrium) elastic ring resting on a surface of revolution by minimizing an energy functional instead of enforcing mechanical equilibrium. Trigger if the solution includes energy-based phrasing (e.g., 'minimize total potential energy', 'energy minimization', 'energy functional', 'Euler–Lagrange', 'variational', 'stationary energy', or 'minimize energy per unit length') AND lacks explicit force-balance equations tied to the surface geometry. Required equilibrium content that must be present: (1) identification of a distributed normal force per unit length n along the ring; (2) use of the surface slope via f'(x) to relate the contact angle ψ (e.g., tanψ = |f'(x)| or cosψ = 1/sqrt(1+f'(x)^2)); (3) vertical balance of forces, with the total vertical component of the normal force equal to the weight: 2π x n cosψ = mg; (4) radial (in-plane) balance per unit length, with the inward normal component supplying the curvature requirement: n sinψ = T/x, where T is the ring tension; and (5) a constitutive relation for T from elasticity (e.g., T = k(x − a) or derived from circumference extension). If these mechanical equilibrium steps are omitted or replaced by energy minimization, flag as a modeling error. Note: This rule applies to static, non-rotating contact problems; energy methods are inappropriate unless explicitly shown to be equivalent to the stated force balances using the geometry of the surface.

rules.title: Rigid pivoted rod implies tangential velocity (perpendicular to rod)
rules.description: Check problems where a point mass is connected to a rigid rod of fixed length L with the other end fixed (pivot). The admissible path is a circle of radius L centered at the pivot; the instantaneous velocity must be tangential to the circle, i.e., perpendicular to the rod (radial line). Flag a conceptual error if the solution: (a) states the body’s motion/velocity is along or parallel to the rod; or (b) sets velocity components using the rod’s angle φ as v_x = v cos φ and v_y = v sin φ (aligning v with the rod). Expected kinematics: position r_x = L cos φ, r_y = L sin φ; velocity v_x = −L φ̇ sin φ, v_y = L φ̇ cos φ; speed v = L |φ̇|; and perpendicularity v ⋅ r̂ = 0 where r̂ is the rod direction. Any use of the rod direction for velocity, or failure of the perpendicularity condition, should trigger this rule.

rules.title: Unjustified rolling/no-slip assumption after inelastic landing
rules.description: Flags solutions that, after a rigid body undergoes a landing or perfectly inelastic collision with the ground, impose a rolling-without-slipping or no-slip constraint (e.g., use v = ωR or state "it rolls along the ground") without explicitly modeling or justifying frictional contact. The rule checks for: (1) Post-impact kinematics invoking rolling/no-slip or equating translational and rotational speeds at contact immediately after an impact. (2) Absence of a friction model: no kinetic/static friction coefficient (μ_k or μ_s) and no tangential impulse analysis (J_t) relative to the normal impulse (J_n), i.e., no check of |J_t| ≤ μ_s J_n for sticking or specification of sliding with μ_k. (3) Extended contact misuse: applying rolling to geometries that contact the ground along a line/area (e.g., a rod lying flat) where point-contact rolling is inapplicable; the correct post-impact motion should be sliding with kinetic friction unless a stick condition is demonstrated. (4) Use of mechanical energy conservation across a perfectly inelastic collision to determine the post-impact horizontal speed, instead of using impulse-momentum with frictional impulses. If any of these are detected, prompt the solver to introduce a friction model (μ_k/μ_s), compute tangential vs normal impulses to decide slip vs stick, or justify an idealized infinite-friction assumption; for rods landing flat, require modeling as sliding with kinetic friction unless sticking is proven.

rules.title: Rolling-without-slip must use kinematic constraint; friction limit (f=μN) or T=μmg is not a valid substitute
rules.description:
This rule flags solutions that (a) equate the static friction force to its maximum value (f = μN) or set an applied horizontal force equal to μmg to claim 'rolling without slipping' or to locate a turning point in a rotational coordinate, and/or (b) omit the rolling-without-slip kinematic constraint. Detection criteria:
- If the solution claims or implies 'rolling without slipping' (phrases like 'no slip', 'rolls without slipping') but does not introduce the kinematic relation v_cm = r·ω (or a_cm = r·α with appropriate sign), flag.
- If the solution directly sets f = μN (or |f| = μN) without explicitly arguing impending slip or deriving f from Newton/Euler equations with the inequality |f| ≤ μN, flag.
- If the solution asserts a critical force condition like T = μmg (or T/(μmg) = 1) as the criterion for no slip or for a local extremum of an angle, flag unless it is clearly justified as a slip-threshold check after solving dynamics.
- For problems where a force is applied at a point that moves with the body (e.g., a constant horizontal tension at the rim of a rotating hoop), check torque expressions: if torque is treated as constant in time/angle and contains no θ-dependence (e.g., no sinθ/cosθ factor for the changing lever arm), flag any conclusions about local maxima/minima of θ based solely on constant-force equalities (like T = μmg).
Rationale: Rolling without slipping is enforced by the kinematic constraint (v_cm = r·ω or a_cm = r·α), not by equating forces to the friction limit. The friction limit |f| ≤ μN only saturates at impending slip. Conditions for an extremum in θ(t) must come from the time/angle-dependent torque and the friction inequality, not from setting T equal to μmg.

rules.title: Incorrect rolling-without-slipping constraint on inner surface (frame-mixing)
rules.description: Checks kinematic constraints for a body rolling without slipping on the INNER surface of a cylinder. For a small cylinder of radius r rolling inside a larger cylinder of radius R, the correct no-slip relation between its spin about its own axis (φ) and the orbital angle of its center (θ) is r·φ̇ = (R − r)·θ̇ (equivalently φ̇ = ((R − r)/r)·θ̇, up to an overall sign). The rule flags the following violations: (1) Frame-mixing: φ̇ written with an additive term in the container’s angular velocity ω (e.g., φ̇ = ((R − r)/r)·θ̇ + ω, φ̇ = θ̇ + (R − r)/r·ω, or any φ̇ = a·θ̇ + b·ω with b ≠ 0) in the no-slip constraint. The container’s ω must not enter additively; the constraint must be stated in a single frame (typically the container frame), relating φ̇ solely to θ̇. (2) Use of absolute values in the constraint (e.g., |φ̇| = ((R − r)/r)|θ̇|), which drops the physically relevant sign and direction of rolling. (3) Incorrect geometric factor: using (R + r)/r, R/r, or φ̇ = θ̇ for inner rolling. (4) Setting the contact-point velocity to zero in the lab frame (e.g., v_contact(lab) = 0) rather than equating the velocities of the two contacting surfaces in the same frame. If any of these patterns are detected in the stated no-slip relation, flag a concept error: mishandled rolling constraint on inner surface.

rules.title: Include rotational inertia and rolling constraint for inner rolling cylinder oscillations
rules.description: When a uniform solid cylinder (mass m, radius r) rolls without slipping on the inner surface of a larger cylinder (radius R), the model must include both translational and rotational kinetic energy and enforce the rolling constraint. The correct small-oscillation dynamics about the bottom position uses: I = (1/2) m r^2, the no-slip constraint φ̇ = ((R - r)/r) θ̇, total kinetic energy K = (1/2) m (R - r)^2 θ̇^2 + (1/2) I φ̇^2 = (3/4) m (R - r)^2 θ̇^2, and potential U ≈ (1/2) m g (R - r) θ^2. This yields the linearized equation (3/2) m (R - r)^2 θ̈ + m g (R - r) θ = 0, natural frequency ω0^2 = 2 g / [3 (R - r)], and period T = 2π √[3 (R - r)/(2 g)]. The verifier should flag a modeling error if: (a) the rotational kinetic energy term is omitted or I is not used for a solid cylinder, (b) the rolling constraint linking the spin φ̇ and the orbital angle θ̇ is missing or incorrect, (c) the effective inertia in front of θ̈ is m (R - r)^2 (simple pendulum) rather than (3/2) m (R - r)^2, or (d) the reported period reduces to the simple pendulum form T = 2π √[(R - r)/g] (or equivalent) instead of T = 2π √[3 (R - r)/(2 g)]. Additionally, check that the final expression depends on R and r only through (R - r), consistent with the rolling constraint for a solid cylinder.

rules.title: Use total mass in translational dynamics for multi-component rolling systems
rules.description:
This rule checks that, in problems involving rolling without slipping where a system is composed of multiple components with specified masses (e.g., a chassis/body plus wheels), the translational application of Newton's second law uses the total mass of all moving parts, not just a subset. Specifically:
- If the problem statement provides separate masses for components (e.g., states that M excludes the wheels, and gives wheel masses), then the net force along the direction of motion must be written using m_total = sum of all component masses.
- For motion along an incline at angle θ, the driving gravitational component must be m_total g sin(θ), and the normal component must sum to m_total g cos(θ) when considering the entire system's external forces.
- The inertial term on the right-hand side must be m_total a, not a single component's mass times a.
- If multiple contacts exist (e.g., four wheels), the friction term in the translational equation should represent the total external friction (sum over contacts), not a single-wheel friction unless explicitly defined as total.
Flag a modeling error when the solution writes F_net_parallel = M g sin(θ) − f = M a (or analogous forms) using only a subset mass (such as the body mass) while the problem provides additional component masses that contribute to both weight and translational inertia. The correct form is F_net_parallel = m_total g sin(θ) − f_total = m_total a, where m_total includes all moving components.

rules.title: Stick-at-separation impulse for spinning solid sphere: v_after must be (2/7) R ω0
rules.description: Checks the tangential impulse-momentum reasoning for a homogeneous solid sphere (I = 2/5 m R^2) that is dropped with zero initial horizontal COM speed and nonzero spin ω0, contacting a rough horizontal plane. In the case where slipping ceases before the end of the impact (stick at separation), the solution must: (1) enforce the kinematic no-slip condition at separation v_after = R ω_after, (2) use only the tangential frictional impulse J_t to change both horizontal linear momentum and spin (normal impulse produces no torque about the center for a sphere), via m v_after = J_t and I ω_after = I ω0 − R J_t, and (3) combine these to obtain v_after = (I R ω0)/(I + m R^2). For a solid sphere (I = 2/5 m R^2) this simplifies to v_after = (2/7) R ω0 in magnitude. The rule flags solutions that: • Omit or misapply the no-slip-at-separation condition v_after = R ω_after. • Attribute the angular impulse to the normal impulse instead of the tangential frictional impulse (e.g., using R N in ΔL rather than R J_t). • Derive an incorrect post-impact horizontal speed such as v_after = (2/5) R ω0 or any expression not equal to (I R ω0)/(I + m R^2) for the stick-at-separation case (sign differences are tolerated, magnitudes are checked). This rule targets the connection between frictional impulse and the coupled linear/angular changes that determine the horizontal speed after the first impact, which directly affects the horizontal flight distance to the second impact.

rules.title: Pure rolling on a horizontal plane: enforce ω_tangential = (ẑ × v_cm)/R
rules.description: Applies when a rigid sphere/ball is stated to roll without slipping on a horizontal surface (surface normal ẑ, radius R). The verifier checks that the no-slip kinematic relation at the contact point is used: v_cm + ω × (−R ẑ) = 0, i.e., v_cm = R (ẑ × ω). Component-wise this implies ω_x = V_y/R and ω_y = −V_x/R; ω_z is not constrained by the no-slip condition (spin about ẑ does not affect slip). The rule flags a concept error if any of the following are present: (1) ω is assumed parallel to ẑ to satisfy rolling (e.g., ω = (V/R) ẑ or ω_z = V/R); (2) ω components are set proportional to the same velocity components (e.g., ω_x = V_x/R or ω_y = V_y/R) instead of the cross-coupled relations; (3) the scalar relation v = ω R is applied without the vector cross-product (direction ignored), implying v_cm and ω are parallel. This check should be applied to the stated initial conditions before collision/torque/angular-momentum calculations.

rules.title: Require correct spin-up relation for translation-to-rolling due to friction (no global energy conservation through slip)
rules.description: This rule verifies solutions involving a rigid body that enters a contact with friction while initially not rotating and exits rolling without slipping (e.g., a sphere with I = β m r^2 rubbing until it rolls). It checks that the solution: (1) does not apply global conservation of mechanical energy across the slipping (spin-up) phase, since kinetic friction dissipates energy; (2) explicitly establishes or correctly uses the necessary kinematic-dynamic relation between the post-slip translational speed v_exit and the initial translational speed v0 for a body with I = β m r^2: v_exit = v0 / (1 + β) and ω_exit = v_exit / r at the onset of rolling; (3) does not leave v_exit dependent on the friction coefficient (the result is independent of μ for constant kinetic friction); and (4) uses v_exit (not v0) as the initial speed for any subsequent conservative phase (e.g., computing ascent height via m g h = 1/2 m v_exit^2 + 1/2 I (v_exit^2 / r^2) if energy is then conserved). The rule flags solutions that: (a) set 1/2 m v0^2 = 1/2 m v^2 + 1/2 I ω^2 + m g h across the slip phase; (b) compute the height h without deriving or citing the v_exit–v0 relation; (c) use an incorrect relation (e.g., omit the 1+β factor or include μ) or fail to impose ω_exit = v_exit / r at rolling. This catches the common error of trying to determine the height from energy conservation without first finding the correct exit speed produced by frictional spin-up.

rules.title: Torque-friction multiplicity consistency in multi-wheel rolling
rules.description: Checks that the rotational torque balance uses a friction term consistent with the number of rolling contacts when a total (multi-wheel) moment of inertia is used. In problems with multiple wheels/rollers that roll without slipping, the ground friction at each contact provides the torque driving rotation. If the solution aggregates the wheels' inertia (I_total = sum of all wheels' inertias, e.g., N * I_wheel for N wheels) and writes a single-contact torque equation like f * R = I_total * α, this is only correct if f is explicitly defined as the total friction (sum over all contacts). The rule flags cases where: (1) I_total is clearly the sum over multiple wheels (detected via phrases like "total inertia of the wheels", formulas such as I_total = N * I_wheel with N > 1, or explicit counts like "4 wheels"), and (2) the torque equation includes only a single friction term (e.g., f R = I_total α) without an explicit sum or multiplier N and without an explicit definition that f represents the total friction across all contacts. Acceptable formulations that will not be flagged include: (a) per-wheel torque equations f_i R = I_wheel α followed by summing over wheels (Σ f_i R = I_total α), (b) using N f R = I_total α with N equal to the number of wheels, and (c) explicitly defining f as the total friction (f_total = Σ f_i) before using f_total R = I_total α. The rule also symmetrically flags the inverse mismatch: using a summed friction term (e.g., N f R) together with a single-wheel inertia (I_wheel) without per-wheel context. This rule helps catch logical inconsistencies in torque setup for multi-contact rolling systems.

rules.title: Require total mass (chassis + wheels) in translational F=ma for rolling systems
rules.description: When a problem states that the chassis/bus mass excludes the wheels and provides wheel masses, the translational Newton’s second law along the incline must use the total mass m_total = m_chassis + sum(m_wheels). The gravitational component and normal force must likewise use m_total (m_total g sinθ and m_total g cosθ). Verification checks: (1) If the student writes F_net = m a with m = m_chassis only, flag an error. (2) If wheel rotational dynamics (torques/inertias) are included (e.g., f_i = I_i a / R_i^2 per wheel) but the translational equation still uses only m_chassis, flag an error for inconsistent mass usage. (3) Consistency check for acceleration: for rolling without slipping with no bearing losses, a should follow a = (m_total g sinθ) / (m_total + Σ(I_i/R_i^2)). If the student’s expression replaces m_total by m_chassis anywhere in the numerator or denominator, flag a calculation error for omitted wheel mass in translation.

rules.title: Do not equate fall distance to geometric rope length in taut-rope scenarios
rules.description:
Checks solutions to rope/climbing/bungee problems where the rope is stated to be taut (e.g., phrases like 'rope always tight/taut', 'no slack', 'the segment between the clip and carabiners is always tight'). In such setups, the climber’s additional drop during arrest is produced by elastic extension of the rope (or the segment attached to the climber), not by the preexisting geometric separation to the anchor/protection. The rule flags the following patterns:
- Asserting or implying a free-fall distance equal to the rope segment length L (e.g., 'the climber falls a distance L' or setting the kinematic/energy displacement to L) when the rope is taut from the start.
- Using fall distance = L + ΔL, or using an mg L term in an energy balance before/while the rope is already exerting force, despite the no-slack assumption.
- Stating that maximum acceleration/tension occurs 'after falling L' in a taut-rope setting.
- Reusing a variable L defined as the geometric distance between the climber and the last anchor/carabiner as the arrest distance, instead of using the rope’s elastic extension (e.g., ΔL or the integral of strain over the segment attached to the climber).
The rule expects, under no-slack assumptions, that the displacement relevant for work/energy and peak-force timing equals the rope extension (e.g., Δy = Δℓ of the segment attached to the climber, or Δy = ∫strain ds), not the preexisting geometric length. Exceptions: Do not trigger if the solution explicitly states the presence of slack, intentional payout, or a mechanism delaying rope engagement before stretch (e.g., 'belayer gives slack', 'device slips until length L'). The rule is intended to catch conceptual misuse of geometric separation as fall distance when immediate rope tension is implied by the problem statement.

rules.title: Use ω × r with the object's radius in rotating-frame velocity transformations
rules.description: This rule verifies correct modeling of velocity transformations between an inertial frame and an Earth-fixed (ground) rotating frame. The physically correct relation is v_rot = v_inertial − ω × r, where ω is Earth's angular velocity and r is the object's position vector from the rotation axis. Flag solutions that: (a) define Earth's rotational speed as v_earth = ω R_earth (equatorial surface speed) and then add or subtract this scalar to an object's velocity to convert frames when the object is not on the surface (e.g., a satellite at altitude r ≈ R_earth + h); (b) perform scalar addition/subtraction v_ground = v_object ± v_earth without using the vector cross product ω × r; or (c) use R_earth in ω × r instead of the object's actual radius r. The rule applies especially to equatorial motion (where directions may align, but the magnitude must still be ω|r| at the object's position). Do not flag if the solution explicitly and consistently adopts the approximation r ≈ R_earth (e.g., h ≪ R_earth) and states this assumption; otherwise, using surface speed for non-surface objects is a modeling inconsistency that distorts computed velocities and kinetic energies.

rules.title: Explicit accounting for imposed rotation ω in small-oscillation analysis
rules.description:
Checks that when a problem specifies a system constrained to rotate at a constant angular velocity (ω), the solution explicitly incorporates ω into the equations of motion or provides a clear derivation showing that ω does not affect the small-oscillation period. The rule triggers if ω is introduced and then omitted without justification, or if the final period is independent of ω but the solution does not demonstrate why.

Pass criteria (any one is sufficient):
- The solution works in the co-rotating frame and includes centrifugal (m ω^2 r_eff) and, where applicable, Coriolis terms in the equation of motion; identifies the shifted equilibrium due to ω; linearizes about that equilibrium; and shows that ω-dependent terms cancel from the small-oscillation frequency.
- The solution works in the inertial frame and incorporates the rotation of the constraint (e.g., moving contact point/geometry) so that ω appears in the kinematics/dynamics; then shows by derivation that ω only shifts the equilibrium and does not enter the linearized frequency.
- The solution explicitly states and proves that the equilibrium position depends on ω (e.g., via an effective potential or force balance) and that the second derivative (stiffness) at equilibrium is ω-independent, yielding a period independent of ω.

Fail conditions (any one triggers an error):
- ω is mentioned in the problem setup but is absent from the equations of motion, energy, or constraint relations, and no explanation is provided for its irrelevance.
- The final expression for the small-oscillation period omits ω without an explicit derivation demonstrating ω-independence (e.g., no equilibrium shift analysis and no cancellation shown).
- In a rotating-frame approach, pseudo forces (centrifugal/Coriolis) are not included or discussed, or the equilibrium about which linearization is performed is not adjusted for ω.

Scope notes: This rule targets small-oscillation problems with externally imposed constant rotation. It does not require ω to appear in the final period if the solution shows, step-by-step, why ω cancels or affects only the equilibrium position. It is acceptable to use either inertial or rotating frames, but the chosen approach must make the role of ω explicit and justify its absence from the final frequency, if applicable.

rules.title: Rotating-frame time-derivative and acceleration transform completeness
rules.description: This rule verifies correct application of vector time-derivative transformations between inertial and rotating frames and checks that the resulting acceleration expression includes all required terms. It targets problems involving a constant angular velocity Ω (e.g., Earth’s rotation). The rule enforces: (1) The general derivative identity must be used correctly: (dA/dt)_inertial = (dA/dt)_rot + Ω × A for any vector A expressed in the rotating basis. (2) If the solution states v = v_R + Ω × r (with r or r' as the position vector in the rotating frame), then the inertial acceleration must be written as a_inertial = a_R + 2 Ω × v_R + Ω × (Ω × r) when Ω is constant. If Ω is time-dependent, the Euler term +(dΩ/dt) × r must also be included. (3) When writing equations of motion in the rotating frame, the fictitious-force form must be consistent: m a_R = F_real − 2 m Ω × v_R − m Ω × (Ω × r) − m (dΩ/dt) × r (with the Euler term zero for constant Ω). The rule flags any of the following errors: • Misstating the derivative identity for velocity, e.g., writing dv/dt = dv_R/dt + Ω × v_R without accounting for the derivative of Ω × r. • Using an incomplete acceleration transform such as a_inertial = a_R + Ω × v_R or a_inertial = a_R + Ω × v, which omits the second Coriolis contribution and the centrifugal term. • Missing the Ω × (Ω × r) term entirely. • Incorrect coefficients (e.g., using 1×Ω × v_R instead of 2×Ω × v_R). • Wrong vector usage in cross products (e.g., using v instead of v_R in the Coriolis term). • Sign errors in the rotating-frame force form (e.g., using +2 m Ω × v_R instead of −2 m Ω × v_R). The verifier should scan the solution for the presence of these transformations and cross-product terms; if any of the required terms are missing, mis-signed, or mis-scaled, or if the derivative identity is applied to v without accounting for v = v_R + Ω × r, the solution is flagged.

rules.title: Rotating-frame net force definition consistency (no fictitious terms inside a_R)
rules.description: Checks for consistent use of the net force in a rotating frame and proper placement of fictitious forces. Trigger this rule if the solution defines F_R as m d^2 r'/dt^2 (i.e., F_R = m a_R) and then (a) adds Coriolis/centrifugal/Euler forces to F_R directly (e.g., F_R = m a_R + F_coriolis + F_centrifugal), or (b) embeds fictitious-force terms inside the definition of a_R (e.g., a_R = d v_R/dt + 2 Ω × v_R + Ω × (Ω × r)). In a rotating frame with angular velocity Ω, the only correct kinematic relation is a = a_R + 2 Ω × v_R + Ω × (Ω × r) + dΩ/dt × r, hence F_R = m a − 2 m (Ω × v_R) − m Ω × (Ω × r) − m (dΩ/dt × r). Flag if: 1) signs of the Ω-terms are wrong when moving from a to a_R (e.g., F_R = m a + 2 m Ω × v_R + ...), 2) v (inertial velocity) is used in the Coriolis term instead of v_R, 3) fictitious terms appear on both sides (double counting), or 4) the student states that “a_R includes Coriolis/centrifugal” as part of its definition. Acceptable alternatives: writing Newton’s second law in the rotating frame as m a_R = F_real + F_coriolis + F_centrifugal (+ F_Euler) is fine provided F_R is kept equal to m a_R and the same fictitious terms are not added again elsewhere. This rule is intended to catch the common confusion between defining F_R = m a_R and adding fictitious forces within a_R or to F_R, leading to inconsistent or double-counted dynamics.

rules.title: Incorrect velocity transformation between inertial and rotating (ground) frame
rules.description: This rule flags solutions that mis-handle the transformation of an object's velocity from an inertial frame to the Earth's rotating ground frame. Specifically, it checks for statements or formulas that: (a) assert the satellite's velocity in the ground frame is the vector sum of its orbital velocity and the Earth's rotational (surface) velocity, e.g., v_total = v_satellite ± v_earth with v_earth = R_earth·ω; (b) use the Earth's equatorial surface speed R_earth·ω as the frame velocity instead of ω × r evaluated at the object's location; or (c) treat the transformation as scalar addition without the vector nature and correct sign. The correct relation is v_rotating = v_inertial − ω × r_object, with r_object the position vector of the object relative to Earth's rotation axis (at its altitude, not the surface). The rule also checks kinetic energy comparisons in the ground frame: KE should be based on |v_inertial − ω × r_object|^2, not on (v_satellite ± R_earth·ω)^2. Any use of surface speed for the frame velocity at the satellite, or claiming a simple sum of orbital and Earth rotation speeds, is flagged as a conceptual error.

rules.title: Correct sign for hydrostatic balance in a rotating frame
rules.description: Applies to problems where a fluid/gas in a spacecraft or cylindrical container is analyzed in a rotating frame with angular speed ω and radial coordinate r. The rule verifies the sign of the radial hydrostatic equilibrium used by the solution. In a rotating frame, the outward centrifugal acceleration is a_r = ω^2 r, so the correct equilibrium is dp/dr = ρ ω^2 r (pressure increases with radius). The verifier should: (1) scan the solution for a force-balance or hydrostatic equation involving dp/dr, ρ, ω, and r; if the equation is written with a negative sign (dp/dr = -ρ ω^2 r), flag an error. (2) If the solution provides a closed-form pressure profile under isothermal ideal-gas assumptions (ρ = μ p / (R T) and boundary p(0) = p0), check that p(r) increases with r and matches p(r) = p0 exp[(μ ω^2 r^2)/(2 R T)]; if the exponent is negative (e.g., p(r) = p0 exp[-(μ ω^2 r^2)/(2 R T)]) or dp/dr < 0 for r > 0, flag an error. (3) If the solution uses an effective potential method, verify that Φ_eff = -½ ω^2 r^2 and that p ∝ exp[-μ Φ_eff/(R T)] yields a positive exponent; if Φ_eff is taken as +½ ω^2 r^2 or the sign is otherwise flipped, flag an error. The rule targets sign inconsistencies that cause pressure to decrease with radius in a rotating system, which is physically incorrect.

rules.title: Rotating isothermal gas: pressure must increase with radius (sign/exponent check)
rules.description: Applies to solutions that derive the radial pressure distribution p(r) for a gas in rigid-body rotation at angular speed ω under isothermal, ideal-gas conditions. Checks: (1) The radial force balance must use dp/dr = ρ ω^2 r (positive outward), not dp/dr = -ρ ω^2 r; (2) Integrating with p = ρ R T / μ at constant T must yield p(r) = p0 * exp[(μ ω^2 r^2)/(2 R T)] or equivalently p(r) = p0 * exp[(m ω^2 r^2)/(2 k_B T)], i.e., the exponent is positive and includes the 1/2 factor and r^2 dependence; (3) p(r) must be monotonically increasing with r and satisfy p(r) ≥ p0 with equality at r = 0. Flag an error if the expression has a negative exponent (e.g., p ∝ exp[-(μ ω^2 r^2)/(2 R T)]), if the force-balance sign is stated as negative, or if the text asserts that pressure decreases outward. Also flag if the integrated form is linear in r or missing the 1/2 factor when isothermal ideal-gas assumptions are explicitly used.

rules.title: Incorrect averaging of centrifugal force to balance ring tension
rules.description: Flags solutions for rotating rings/rubber bands that compute the required inward force by dividing the total centrifugal force M·ω²·r by the circumference 2πr to obtain a uniform 'force per unit length' F_c = M·ω²/(2π), and then directly equate this value to the tension T or to a Hooke-like tension k(r−R). This approach improperly balances a per-length quantity (N/m) with a force (N) and skips the necessary local small-arc force balance. The correct method is to analyze a differential arc of length dl (angle dθ = dl/r): the net inward component of the two end tensions is T·dθ = T·(dl/r), which must equal the centripetal force on that arc λ·ω²·r·dl, where λ = M/(2πr) is the linear mass density. This yields T = λ·ω²·r² = M·ω²·r/(2π). The rule triggers if a solution: (a) explicitly derives F_c = M·ω²/(2π) by 'dividing by the circumference' and uses it to balance T or k(r−R) without the T·dθ = λ·ω²·r·dl step; (b) claims tension is independent of r (e.g., T = M·ω²/(2π)); or (c) omits the geometric relation between tension components and centripetal force for a small arc. It also notes unit inconsistency (equating N/m directly to N) and absence of the curvature factor (dθ = dl/r) as indicators of this error.

rules.title: Rotating ring must use local centripetal balance (T/r = λω²r); flag constant per-length centrifugal force and missing closure
rules.description: Scope: Solutions for uniformly rotating flexible circular rings/hoops/rubber bands whose radius may change due to rotation and elasticity. Check that the solution establishes the correct local force balance for an infinitesimal arc and consistently closes with the elastic law. What to verify: (1) Presence of a correct local equilibrium for a small arc: T dθ = dm·ω²·r, which is equivalent to T/r = λ·ω²·r, or T = λ·ω²·r², or, after substituting λ = M/(2πr), T = M·ω²·r/(2π). Any of these is acceptable. (2) If a “centrifugal force per unit length” is formed by dividing total inertial force M·ω²·r by the circumference, ensure the r-dependence is treated correctly; flag the specific error F_per_length = M·ω²/(2π) (i.e., constant with respect to r) unless it is immediately reconciled via the correct local balance to yield T/r = λ·ω²·r. (3) Closure requirement: If an elastic constitutive relation is introduced (e.g., T = k(r − R) or tension proportional to circumferential strain), it must be explicitly equated to the centripetal requirement to solve for r. Flag if the solution leaves these relations unconnected or does not solve for r. (4) Logical consistency: Flag circular or inconclusive reasoning patterns where the solution asserts intermediate expressions are “not correct” or repeatedly redefines per-length inertial force without replacing them with the correct geometric balance leading to T/r = λ·ω²·r or T = M·ω²·r/(2π). Rationale: For a rotating ring, the radial components of the end tensions on a small element produce a net inward force ≈ T dθ that must equal dm·ω²·r. Omitting this geometry or using a per-length inertial force independent of r leads to incorrect or non-closable derivations. Energy/Lagrangian alternatives are acceptable only if they produce an equivalent tension–radius relation consistent with T = M·ω²·r/(2π).

rules.title: Missing curvature (1/r) in rotating ring force balance
rules.description: Checks solutions for rotating circular bands/hoops that equate elastic tension directly to the centrifugal line load and erroneously eliminate the radius. Correct local radial equilibrium for a thin ring requires the geometric curvature factor: T/r = λ ω^2 r, with λ = M/(2π r), which implies T ∝ r (specifically T = (M ω^2 r)/(2π)). The rule flags any of the following patterns: (1) Using λ = M/(2π r) to form a centrifugal force per unit length and canceling r, then setting T = λ ω^2 r or T = M ω^2/(2π) (i.e., tension independent of r). (2) Equating k(r − R) directly to the centrifugal force per unit length without dividing the tension by r (e.g., k(r − R) = M ω^2/(2π)). (3) Statements that the centrifugal force per unit length being independent of r allows r to drop out of the final equilibrium, yielding T or the radius solution without r-dependence in the centrifugal term. Dimensional sanity check enforced: in a correct balance for a rotating ring, tension must scale as M ω^2 r; derived forms scaling as M ω^2 (no r) are flagged. Rationale: Even if the centrifugal line load can be constant in r for a uniform ring, the curvature introduces a 1/r projection of tension into the radial direction, so r must appear in the equilibrium equation and resulting tension.

rules.title: Explicit radius and correct tension–centrifugal balance for a rotating ring
rules.description:
This rule checks solutions to problems that ask for the deformed radius of a uniformly rotating thin circular ring/band. It enforces both completeness and correct mechanics. The verifier will: 
- Require an explicit final expression for the radius r in terms of the given parameters (e.g., M, k, R, ω). If no equation of the form r = ... (or an equivalent solved relation) is present, flag as incomplete.
- Validate the ring force balance: for a uniformly rotating thin ring of mass M and radius r, the correct equilibrium between tension and centrifugal effects is T = (M ω^2 r)/(2π). This comes from dm = (M/(2π r)) r dθ, centrifugal force dm r ω^2 = (M ω^2 r)/(2π) dθ, and radial resultant of tension T dθ. If the solution equates tension to a centrifugal quantity that is independent of r (e.g., T = M ω^2/(2π)) or otherwise does not recover T ∝ r, flag as a force-balance error.
- Check for a constitutive (elastic) relation linking tension to stretch of the ring (e.g., tension proportional to change in circumference or radius). If no elastic law is stated or tension is written without reference to the ring’s extension (e.g., only T = k without ΔL or r − R), flag as missing/incorrect constitutive modeling.
- Ensure the mechanics (T = (M ω^2 r)/(2π)) is combined with the elastic law to solve for r. If the argument terminates before combining these to produce r, flag as incomplete logic.

rules.title: Correct simplification of ω_after using solid sphere inertia
rules.description: Checks algebraic simplification of the post-impact angular velocity when the solution derives ω_after from an expression of the form ω_after = (I/(I − mR^2))·ω0 for a solid, homogeneous sphere with I = (2/5)mR^2. The verifier will: (1) detect any step where ω_after is presented as k·ω0 or computed via k = I/(I − mR^2); (2) substitute I = (2/5)mR^2 and simplify k, expecting k = −2/3 (negative sign because I < mR^2); (3) compare the stated coefficient to −2/3 within tolerance and ensure the negative sign is retained; (4) flag an error if the coefficient magnitude or sign is altered (e.g., k reported as 2/5, +2/3, or |−2/3|) without explicit and correct physical justification. The rule also flags any unjustified replacement of k with a different moment-of-inertia factor not derived from I/(I − mR^2).

rules.title: Require lever-arm/line-of-action justification for zero torque about pivot
rules.description: This rule checks justifications for conservation of angular momentum about a pivot during an impulsive collision. It flags solutions that assert zero external torque about the pivot using imprecise direction-only arguments (e.g., 'tension exerts no torque because it acts along the string') without referencing the correct criterion. The correct criterion is: a force has zero torque about a chosen point if its point of application is at that point (lever arm is zero) or its line of action passes through that point (r × F = 0 due to colinearity). The rule triggers when: (1) the student concludes angular momentum is conserved about a pivot; and (2) the justification for zero torque mentions only that a force acts 'along the string/radius/connection' or relies solely on force direction, without explicitly stating that the force’s line of action passes through the pivot or that the lever arm is zero. It also flags misstatements that attribute zero torque to a force because of its direction while incorrectly identifying the point of application (e.g., claiming a force at the pivot has zero torque due to direction rather than zero lever arm). Acceptable explanations must explicitly connect zero torque to lever arm being zero or the line of action passing through the pivot, and should recognize that pivot reactions have zero torque about the pivot and that tension in a string gives zero torque about the pivot because its line of action goes through the pivot. If these conditions are not met, the justification is marked conceptually inconsistent.

rules.title: Dimensional and scaling check for rotational flattening ε
rules.description:
This rule verifies that any expression used for the rotational flattening factor ε (defined by ε = (re − rp)/rp) is dimensionless and scales correctly with rotation for a self-gravitating body. It targets common errors where ε is computed from angular speed ω, radius R, mass M, and gravitational constant G with incorrect powers of R.

Checks performed:
1) Dimensional consistency: If ε is expressed using only ω, R, G, and M, the expression must be dimensionless. The canonical dimensionless rotation parameter is q = ω^2 R^3 / (G M). The rule flags expressions of the form ε ≈ k · ω^2 R^n / (G M) with n ≠ 3. In particular, ε ∝ ω^2 R^2 / (G M) is flagged (units 1/length).
2) Accepted equivalent forms: ε expressed as k · ω^2 R^3 / (G M) or as k · ω^2 / (G ρ) (with ρ the mean density, e.g., ρ = 3M/(4πR^3)) are accepted, since they are dimensionless and equivalent up to constants.
3) Scaling/magnitude sanity check: Compute q = ω^2 R^3 / (G M) from the same inputs. For small flattening (Maclaurin spheroid, small-eccentricity limit), ε should be O(q) (e.g., ε ≈ (1–2)×q in order of magnitude; for a uniform Maclaurin spheroid ε ≈ (5/4)·q). If a provided numerical ε differs from q by more than one order of magnitude (|log10(ε/q)| > 1) without a justified model-dependent coefficient, flag it.
4) Specific pattern flag: Directly flag the use of ε = 3 ω^2 R^2 / (8 G M) or any equivalent that has R^2 instead of R^3 in the numerator when only ω, R, G, M are present.

Trigger conditions (any one is sufficient):
- The parsed ε expression simplifies to k · ω^2 R^n / (G M) with n ≠ 3.
- The ε expression has units other than dimensionless (e.g., 1/length).
- The computed ε is orders of magnitude smaller or larger than q by more than a factor of 10 without explicit justification.

Rationale: ε must be dimensionless; incorrect radius power leads to unphysical magnitudes (e.g., ε ~ 10^−8 for neutron-star parameters where q ~ 10^−3). This rule catches dimensionally inconsistent formulas and cross-checks magnitude against the expected scaling.

rules.title: Validate angular acceleration and linear–angular mapping
rules.description: Check consistency of rotational kinematics and torque relations involving angular acceleration. The rule enforces that angular acceleration α is the second time derivative of angular displacement: α = d²θ/dt² (i.e., α = θ¨), and must not include geometric factors like radius R. Flag any occurrence of α defined as θ¨/R, ω˙/R, or any expression putting 1/R with purely angular quantities. Verify the no-slip kinematic mapping between linear and angular motion: a_t = R α and α = a_t / R; flag incorrect mappings such as a_t = α, a_t = θ¨, α = a_t R, or y¨ = θ¨ (missing the factor R) when relating a translating element to pulley rotation. In torque balance τ = I α, ensure α refers to angular acceleration (θ¨) and that reduction to linear variables is done via a_t = R α (e.g., substituting α = y¨/R is acceptable, but substituting α = θ¨/R is not). Dimensional check: α must have units s⁻²; flag any expression for α that carries length units (e.g., s⁻²/m or m·s⁻²) unless it appears as part of the correct relation a_t = R α or α = a_t / R. This rule catches confusion between α and θ¨, and misuse of R in angular acceleration definitions that leads to downstream errors in torque/force relations.

rules.title: Verify rotational kinematic equation consistency
rules.description: Ensure that the rotational kinematic equations (e.g., θ = ω₀t + 0.5αt², ω = ω₀ + αt) are applied correctly. These equations require constant angular acceleration.
rules.check_logic: Check if the problem explicitly states or implies constant angular acceleration. If angular acceleration is variable or unspecified, rotational kinematic equations cannot be used.
common_errors: Using rotational kinematic equations when angular acceleration is not constant.
Incorrect substitution of angular acceleration (α) or initial angular velocity (ω₀).
Mixing up linear and rotational variables (e.g., using linear acceleration in place of angular acceleration).

rules.title: Ensure consistent sign conventions for angular quantities
rules.description: Angular displacement, velocity, and acceleration can be positive or negative depending on the chosen coordinate system. Ensure consistency in the sign conventions throughout the solution.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the student has explicitly chosen a direction (e.g., counterclockwise as positive) and maintained this convention for all angular quantities. Ensure that any changes in sign are justified by the problem's setup.
common_errors: Switching sign conventions partway through the solution.
Incorrectly assigning signs to angular quantities based on direction.
Confusing clockwise and counterclockwise directions in the coordinate system.

rules.title: Validate torque equation application
rules.description: Torque (τ) is given by τ = r × F = rFsin(θ), where r is the lever arm, F is the force, and θ is the angle between r and F. This equation is valid for rigid bodies with forces applied at a fixed distance.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the student calculates torque using the correct r, F, and θ, and ensures the force is not passing through the axis of rotation. Confirm that the direction of torque is consistent with the right-hand rule.
common_errors: Forgetting to include the sin(θ) factor when torque is not perpendicular to the lever arm.
Using the wrong value for r (e.g., distance to the wrong axis of rotation).
Omitting torque contributions when multiple forces act on the body.

rules.title: Check conservation of rotational mechanical energy
rules.description: The total rotational mechanical energy (K_rot = 0.5Iω²) is conserved in the absence of non-conservative torques, such as friction. Ensure this principle is applied only when valid.
rules.check_logic: Verify that no non-conservative torques are present before applying rotational energy conservation. If friction or other dissipative forces exist, include their work in the energy balance. Ensure that all forms of energy (rotational, translational, potential) are accounted for.
common_errors: Applying conservation of rotational energy in the presence of non-conservative torques.
Forgetting to include rotational kinetic energy in total energy calculations.
Incorrectly calculating the rotational inertia (I) of the object.

rules.title: Verify correct calculation of moment of inertia
rules.description: Moment of inertia (I) depends on the mass distribution relative to the axis of rotation. Using the correct formula or integral is critical.
rules.check_logic: Check if the student uses the appropriate formula for I based on the geometry and axis of rotation (e.g., I = 0.5MR² for a solid disk about its central axis). For irregular objects, verify the use of integration. Ensure the parallel axis theorem is applied when the axis of rotation is shifted.
common_errors: Using the wrong formula for the shape and axis of rotation.
Forgetting to apply the parallel axis theorem when necessary.
Incorrectly calculating or integrating for non-standard geometries.

rules.title: Validate conservation of angular momentum
rules.description: Angular momentum (L = Iω) is conserved in a system with no external torques. Ensure this principle is applied only when external torques are absent.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the problem specifies or implies no external torques before assuming conservation of angular momentum. Confirm that changes in angular momentum are consistent with changes in I or ω when mass distribution changes.
common_errors: Applying conservation of angular momentum in the presence of external torques.
Incorrectly calculating angular momentum (e.g., using the wrong I or ω).
Failing to account for changes in I when the distribution of mass changes.

rules.title: Ensure correct linkage between linear and rotational kinematics
rules.description: For rolling objects or systems combining linear and rotational motion, ensure correct use of the relation v = ωr, a_t = αr, and s = θr.
rules.check_logic: Check if the student uses the correct relationship between linear and angular quantities based on the rolling condition or constraint. Verify that rolling without slipping is explicitly stated or implied before using these relations.
common_errors: Using v = ωr when the object is not rolling without slipping.
Confusing tangential and radial acceleration.
Forgetting to apply rolling constraints when required.

rules.title: Verify dimensional and unit consistency in rotational quantities
rules.description: Ensure that all equations involving angular quantities (e.g., torque, angular momentum) are dimensionally consistent and use appropriate units (e.g., radians, N·m).
rules.check_logic: Verify that units for angular displacement (radians), angular velocity (rad/s), angular acceleration (rad/s²), torque (N·m), and moment of inertia (kg·m²) are consistent throughout the solution. Ensure radians are used in calculations involving angular quantities.
common_errors: Using degrees instead of radians in rotational equations.
Mixing linear and angular units (e.g., using m/s instead of rad/s).
Incorrectly simplifying or canceling units in torque or energy calculations.

rules.title: Verify understanding of gyroscopic precession
rules.description: For rotating objects experiencing a torque perpendicular to their angular momentum, ensure the precession motion is correctly analyzed.
rules.check_logic: Check if the student uses the relation Ω = τ / L, where Ω is the precession angular velocity, τ is the applied torque, and L is the angular momentum. Verify that the direction of precession is consistent with the right-hand rule.
common_errors: Incorrectly calculating the precession angular velocity.
Ignoring the direction of precession determined by the torque and angular momentum.
Confusing precession with simple rotational motion.

rules.title: 约束脱离临界判定规则
rules.description:
触发条件：物体沿约束面（墙面/球面）滑动问脱离点时
检查逻辑：检查是否误用力矩平衡代替动力学方程。正确逻辑是：列出法向/水平牛顿第二定律，令约束正压力 N=0，并结合能量守恒求角速度。
rules.check_logic: 检查是否误用力矩平衡代替动力学方程。正确逻辑是：列出法向/水平牛顿第二定律，令约束正压力 N=0，并结合能量守恒求角速度。
rules.trigger: 物体沿约束面（墙面/球面）滑动问脱离点时

rules.title: 非完整约束滚动建模检查
rules.description:
触发条件：物体在平面上“纯滚动”且涉及多维坐标（如x, y, theta, phi）
检查逻辑：检查是否列出了速度约束方程（如 v = R * omega）。若涉及倾斜，需检查质心速度与转动角速度在接触点坐标系下的投影匹配。
rules.check_logic: 检查是否列出了速度约束方程（如 v = R * omega）。若涉及倾斜，需检查质心速度与转动角速度在接触点坐标系下的投影匹配。
rules.trigger: 物体在平面上“纯滚动”且涉及多维坐标（如x, y, theta, phi）

rules.title: 组合体动力学质量一致性检查
rules.description:
触发条件：题目给出‘排除某部件后的质量’或‘由多个组件构成的系统’时
检查逻辑：核实牛顿第二定律 F=ma 中的 m 是否等于系统总质量（车身+所有车轮），而非仅为车身质量。
rules.check_logic: 核实牛顿第二定律 F=ma 中的 m 是否等于系统总质量（车身+所有车轮），而非仅为车身质量。
rules.trigger: 题目给出‘排除某部件后的质量’或‘由多个组件构成的系统’时

rules.title: 非保守力做功判定
rules.description:
触发条件：题目出现‘rubs against’, ‘friction’, ‘starts rolling’等描述滑动摩擦过程时
检查逻辑：检查是否错误使用了机械能守恒；滑动摩擦力使物体达到纯滚动过程中，机械能必然不守恒。
rules.check_logic: 检查是否错误使用了机械能守恒；滑动摩擦力使物体达到纯滚动过程中，机械能必然不守恒。
rules.trigger: 题目出现‘rubs against’, ‘friction’, ‘starts rolling’等描述滑动摩擦过程时

rules.title: 纯滚动初态关联律
rules.description:
触发条件：物体从平动通过摩擦转为纯滚动（rolling without slipping）
检查逻辑：必须通过对接触点的角动量守恒（L=const）或动量定理与角动量定理联立来求解末速度，而非能量方程。
rules.check_logic: 必须通过对接触点的角动量守恒（L=const）或动量定理与角动量定理联立来求解末速度，而非能量方程。
rules.trigger: 物体从平动通过摩擦转为纯滚动（rolling without slipping）

rules.title: 滚动体摆动周期修正
rules.description:
触发条件：物体在圆弧面上“无滑动滚动”（Roll without slipping）进行小角度摆动时
检查逻辑：检查等效摆长是否计入转动惯量修正系数 (1 + I/mr^2)。对于实心圆柱，该系数为 3/2。
rules.check_logic: 检查等效摆长是否计入转动惯量修正系数 (1 + I/mr^2)。对于实心圆柱，该系数为 3/2。
rules.trigger: 物体在圆弧面上“无滑动滚动”（Roll without slipping）进行小角度摆动时

rules.title: 非线性摆动时间积分规则
rules.description:
触发条件：给出 ∫csc(x)dx 等三角函数积分提示且涉及大角度变加速运动时
检查逻辑：禁止使用简谐运动线性近似。必须通过能量守恒 E=K+V 导出 dθ/dt = g(θ)，再构造 dt = dθ/g(θ) 进行定积分计算。
rules.check_logic: 禁止使用简谐运动线性近似。必须通过能量守恒 E=K+V 导出 dθ/dt = g(θ)，再构造 dt = dθ/g(θ) 进行定积分计算。
rules.trigger: 给出 ∫csc(x)dx 等三角函数积分提示且涉及大角度变加速运动时

rules.title: 滑动摩擦力方向一致性
rules.description:
触发条件：涉及滑动摩擦力 $\vec{f}_k$ 与相对速度单位向量 $\hat{u}$ 的矢量表达
检查逻辑：检查动力学方程中加速度方向是否与 $-\hat{u}$ 一致，力矩方向是否满足右手定则 $\vec{r} \times (-\mu mg \hat{u})$。
rules.check_logic: 检查动力学方程中加速度方向是否与 $-\hat{u}$ 一致，力矩方向是否满足右手定则 $\vec{r} \times (-\mu mg \hat{u})$。
rules.trigger: 涉及滑动摩擦力 $\vec{f}_k$ 与相对速度单位向量 $\hat{u}$ 的矢量表达

rules.title: 高速旋转体稳定性判别
rules.description:
触发条件：题目涉及“高速旋转”、“不倒”、“稳定性条件”或“小扰动近似”
检查逻辑：必须建立包含自旋角动量与重力矩平衡的动力学方程（陀螺近似），检查是否考虑了进动角速度与自旋角速度的耦合项。
rules.check_logic: 必须建立包含自旋角动量与重力矩平衡的动力学方程（陀螺近似），检查是否考虑了进动角速度与自旋角速度的耦合项。
rules.trigger: 题目涉及“高速旋转”、“不倒”、“稳定性条件”或“小扰动近似”

rules.title: 临界滑动条件一致性
rules.description:
触发条件：题目要求求解“开始滑动”时的物理量（如摩擦系数）
检查逻辑：检查是否同时满足：1.转动定律求角加速度；2.质心运动定理求支持力和摩擦力；3.库仑摩擦定律 f = μN。
rules.check_logic: 检查是否同时满足：1.转动定律求角加速度；2.质心运动定理求支持力和摩擦力；3.库仑摩擦定律 f = μN。
rules.trigger: 题目要求求解“开始滑动”时的物理量（如摩擦系数）

rules.title: 刚体接触力矩矢量定义
rules.description:
触发条件：计算球体或圆柱体在平面上滑行/滚动受到的摩擦力矩时
检查逻辑：核实转动方程的力矩项是否为 $\vec{r}_{contact} \times \vec{f}$，其中 $\vec{r}_{contact}$ 是从质心指向接触点的位移矢量（通常沿法线方向），而非沿摩擦力方向。
rules.check_logic: 核实转动方程的力矩项是否为 $\vec{r}_{contact} \times \vec{f}$，其中 $\vec{r}_{contact}$ 是从质心指向接触点的位移矢量（通常沿法线方向），而非沿摩擦力方向。
rules.trigger: 计算球体或圆柱体在平面上滑行/滚动受到的摩擦力矩时

rules.title: 刚体定点转动受力分析
rules.description:
触发条件：涉及刚体绕固定点（或瞬心）转动且需计算地面支持力或摩擦力时
检查逻辑：必须通过质心运动定理列出竖直和水平方向方程：N - mg = m*a_y 以及 f = m*a_x，其中a为质心加速度，不能假设N=mg或N=mgcosθ。
rules.check_logic: 必须通过质心运动定理列出竖直和水平方向方程：N - mg = m*a_y 以及 f = m*a_x，其中a为质心加速度，不能假设N=mg或N=mgcosθ。
rules.trigger: 涉及刚体绕固定点（或瞬心）转动且需计算地面支持力或摩擦力时

rules.title: 滚动不下滑约束的功/力矩耦合检查
rules.description:
触发条件：出现‘rolls without slipping’且涉及复杂转动惯量时
检查逻辑：检查加速度公式 a = (M_total * g * sinθ) / (M_total + I_total / R^2) 中，M_total 与 I_total 的质量基准是否统一。
rules.check_logic: 检查加速度公式 a = (M_total * g * sinθ) / (M_total + I_total / R^2) 中，M_total 与 I_total 的质量基准是否统一。
rules.trigger: 出现‘rolls without slipping’且涉及复杂转动惯量时

rules.title: Correct rotational kinetic energy for a two-mass dipole (I = μℓ^2)
rules.description: Checks that the rotational kinetic energy for a rigid two-point-mass dipole (dumbbell) rotating about its center of mass uses the correct moment of inertia. Applicability: two point masses m1 and m2 connected by a massless rod of length ℓ (ℓ is the full separation between masses), rotation about the center of mass with angular speed ω. Expected relations: I_expected = μ ℓ^2, where μ = (m1 m2)/(m1 + m2). Thus E_rot_expected = (1/2) I_expected ω^2. Special case (equal masses m): I_expected = m ℓ^2 / 2 and E_rot_expected = (1/4) m ℓ^2 ω^2. The rule flags errors if any of the following are detected: (a) the solution sets I = (m1 + m2) ℓ^2 or, in the equal-mass case, I = m ℓ^2 or I = 2 m ℓ^2; (b) the solution states E_rot = (1/2) m ℓ^2 ω^2 for equal masses when ℓ is defined as the rod length (full separation); (c) the coefficient of m ℓ^2 ω^2 in E_rot for equal masses is not 1/4; (d) the solution misinterprets ℓ as the radius to each mass (leading to I = 2 m ℓ^2) despite the problem defining ℓ as the distance between the masses. As a consistency cross-check, the rule also verifies that the translational kinetic energy of the center of mass uses the total mass: E_trans = (1/2) (m1 + m2) v_CM^2 (for equal masses: E_trans = m v_CM^2), and flags use of m or μ in place of (m1 + m2). The rule is insensitive to electromagnetic details (B-field) because the moment of inertia depends only on the mass distribution.

rules.title: Torque from kinetic friction must be r × F = μ_k m g R (z × u)
rules.description: For a sphere slipping on a horizontal plane, the kinetic friction at the contact is F_f = -μ_k N u with N = mg, and the lever arm from the center to the contact is r_c = -R z. The rotational equation must use the torque  = r_c × F_f = μ_k m g R (z × u), so I d/dt = . Flag solutions that: (a) set I d/dt parallel to ±u (i.e., torque colinear with the slip direction), (b) replace the cross product with a scalar product such as  = ±R |F_f| u or any expression lacking the r × F structure, (c) omit the factor R or mg in the torque magnitude when expressing , or (d) use the wrong cross-product order yielding  = μ_k m g R (u × z) (sign error), or produce a torque not lying in the xy-plane and perpendicular to u. This rule verifies that the rotational dynamics are derived with  = μ_k m g R (z × u) and I d/dt = .

rules.title: Do not double-count propagation delay in range equations
rules.description: Checks signal propagation modeling for satellite-to-receiver ranging in an inertial frame (no relativistic corrections). The geometric range between receiver and satellite i must be tied to a single time-of-flight term. Correct forms are either: (1) sqrt((x − x_i)^2 + (y − y_i)^2 + (z − z_i)^2) = c · (t − t_i), where t is the unknown reception time and t_i is the known emission time, or (2) sqrt((x − x_i)^2 + (y − y_i)^2 + (z − z_i)^2) = c · Δt_i, where Δt_i is explicitly defined as the time delay between emission and reception (Δt_i = t − t_i). The rule flags any equation that adds both representations of the same delay, e.g., distance or range expressed as c · (t − t_i + Δt_i), c · (Δt_i + τ_i), or any RHS where two distinct time-of-flight terms appear additively under a single factor of c. Rationale: Δt_i is not independent of t − t_i; adding it double-counts the propagation delay and biases the solved range and time. If the problem statement indicates the receiver has no clock or uses a global time t as an unknown, any extra additive delay term beyond (t − t_i) is rejected unless it is a properly introduced clock bias for a different time base explicitly justified by the model. The verifier should parse propagation equations for satellite ranging and flag when (t − t_i) and a named delay variable (e.g., Δt_i, tau_i, time_delay_i) both appear additively in the same propagation term.

rules.title: Consistency of equilibrium-referenced displacement in spring-force and net-force expressions
rules.description: Trigger when a solution defines a displacement variable explicitly relative to the equilibrium position (e.g., 'x measured from equilibrium') and then writes the spring force as F_s = -k x while also retaining an uncompensated constant bias force in the net force or equation of motion (e.g., mg sinθ, a constant C). Specifically: (1) If x is defined from equilibrium, the correct spring force referenced to the natural length is F_s = -k(x + x0), with x0 the equilibrium extension satisfying k x0 = (constant bias along the direction). After substituting k x0, the constant term must cancel, yielding m x'' = -k x for SHM. (2) Flag an error when the text/equations contain both 'x from equilibrium' and expressions like F_net = -k x + (constant) or m x'' = -k x + (constant) without introducing x0 and showing cancellation via k x0 = (constant). This indicates the net force would be nonzero at x = 0, contradicting the equilibrium definition and producing an internally inconsistent model.

rules.title: Unnecessary 'small displacement' assumption in SHM with ideal springs
rules.description: This rule flags solutions that incorrectly restrict the validity of simple harmonic motion (SHM) to 'small displacements' when the system is a mass attached to an ideal (Hookean) spring and displacement is measured from the equilibrium position. Detection criteria: (a) The model context or equations include Hooke’s law (F = -k x) and the linear ODE m x'' + k x = 0 or ω = sqrt(k/m); (b) The text contains phrases such as 'for small x', 'for small displacements', 'for small oscillations', 'assuming small amplitude', or mentions of linearization that suggest the result holds only approximately; (c) No nonlinear restoring-force terms (e.g., x^2, x^3) or geometry-dependent nonlinearities are present. The rule also flags misuse of small-angle approximations in this context, e.g., replacing sin θ with θ for a fixed incline angle θ, which is unrelated to the oscillation amplitude. Rationale: For an ideal spring obeying Hooke’s law and with x measured from equilibrium, SHM is exact for any amplitude; introducing a small-amplitude qualification is conceptually incorrect unless a non-Hookean or otherwise nonlinear force model is explicitly used.

rules.title: Do not treat constant forces as restoring forces in SHM
rules.description: This rule flags solutions that incorrectly treat a constant force component (e.g., mg sinθ on an incline) as a restoring force in simple harmonic motion problems. It triggers when: (1) The text claims that the constant gravitational component along the axis 'pulls the mass back to equilibrium' or 'provides restoring force'; (2) The equation of motion is written as m x'' = -k x + C (with C constant, such as mg sinθ) and the solution asserts SHM without redefining displacement relative to the static equilibrium x0 = C/k; (3) A displacement variable is stated to be measured from equilibrium, yet a constant term remains in the force or acceleration expression; (4) The reported period depends on g or θ for a frictionless incline spring system. Correct treatment requires recognizing that constant forces only shift the equilibrium (k x0 = C), the restoring force about equilibrium is solely -k ξ with ξ = x − x0, and the period is T = 2π√(m/k), independent of g and θ.

rules.title: SHM Linearization Restoring-Sign Consistency
rules.description: Checks for sign consistency when linearizing the equation of motion near equilibrium and subsequently asserting simple harmonic motion (SHM). Detection logic: (1) Identify a defined perturbation variable (e.g., Δq = q − q_eq, δq, or similar). (2) Parse any linearized second-order ODE of the form d^2q/dt^2 = C·Δq or d^2Δq/dt^2 = C·Δq, where C is taken as a constant near equilibrium. (3) Verify that the sign of C matches the claimed behavior: for SHM about a stable equilibrium, the restoring acceleration must oppose displacement, i.e., d^2Δq/dt^2 = −|C|·Δq, and ω^2 = |C| > 0. (4) Flag inconsistency if the solution derives d^2q/dt^2 = +C·Δq (C > 0) and then immediately writes the SHM form d^2Δq/dt^2 + C·Δq = 0, or claims oscillatory motion/frequency ω = sqrt(C) without addressing the required negative sign (i.e., without showing C < 0 or redefining Δq with opposite sign). (5) Ensure the equivalence d^2Δq/dt^2 = d^2q/dt^2 is respected: flipping sign between consecutive lines without explicit justification is flagged. Example trigger: a derivation yielding d^2 y/dt^2 = (γ g / y_i)·Δy followed by d^2Δy/dt^2 + (γ g / y_i)·Δy = 0 or ω^2 = γ g / y_i; this indicates a sign inconsistency because stable SHM requires d^2Δy/dt^2 = −(γ g / y_i)·Δy. The rule applies to any coordinate and perturbation variable; it ignores cases where the perturbation is explicitly defined with opposite sign (e.g., Δq = q_eq − q) and the sign is handled consistently.

rules.title: Misclassification of unstable linearized rotational dynamics as SHO
rules.description: Flags solutions that treat an unstable second-order ODE as simple harmonic motion.
