rules.description: Check whether the uncertainty in position (Δx) and the uncertainty in momentum (Δp) satisfy the inequality Δx * Δp ≥ ħ/2, where ħ is the reduced Planck's constant. This is the fundamental relation of the Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle.
rules.check_logic: Ensure the product of Δx and Δp is evaluated and compared against ħ/2. If it violates the inequality, the solution is incorrect.
common_errors: Using Planck's constant (h) instead of reduced Planck's constant (ħ = h/2π)
Misinterpreting the inequality as Δx * Δp = ħ/2 instead of ≥
Incorrect computation or omission of Δx or Δp values

rules.title: Ensure correct sign convention for uncertainties
rules.description: Uncertainties Δx and Δp are always positive quantities since they represent standard deviations. Ensure no negative values or incorrect sign conventions are used.
rules.check_logic: Verify that Δx > 0 and Δp > 0. Negative uncertainties or zero uncertainty would invalidate the solution.
common_errors: Assigning negative values to uncertainties
Using Δx or Δp as zero, which violates the principle

rules.title: Check applicability of Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle
rules.description: The Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle applies only to conjugate variables such as position and momentum or energy and time. Ensure it is not applied to unrelated quantities.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the uncertainty relation is applied only to conjugate variables (e.g., Δx and Δp, or ΔE and Δt).
common_errors: Applying the uncertainty principle to non-conjugate quantities (e.g., position and energy)
Using the principle for macroscopic systems where quantum effects are negligible

rules.title: Verify dimensional consistency in uncertainty calculations
rules.description: Ensure that the product of Δx and Δp has the correct dimensions, which are [L][M][T^-1] (length × mass × velocity). Similarly, for energy and time, ΔE * Δt should have dimensions of [E][T] (energy × time).
rules.check_logic: Check the units of Δx (e.g., meters) and Δp (e.g., kg·m/s) to ensure their product matches ħ's units. For ΔE and Δt, verify that their product matches the units of ħ.
common_errors: Mismatch in units for Δx and Δp (e.g., using position in cm and momentum in kg·m/s without conversion)
Omitting unit conversions when necessary

rules.title: Ensure geometric constraints are respected for Δx and Δp
rules.description: In confined systems (e.g., particles in a box), the uncertainty in position Δx cannot exceed the physical dimensions of the system. Similarly, Δp is bounded by the maximum momentum achievable.
rules.check_logic: Verify that Δx is less than or equal to the system's spatial dimensions and that Δp is consistent with the physical momentum bounds.
common_errors: Assigning Δx values larger than the system's dimensions
Ignoring physical constraints on Δp

rules.title: Validate uncertainty relation for energy and time
rules.description: For energy and time, the uncertainty principle states ΔE * Δt ≥ ħ/2. This applies to scenarios where energy fluctuations and time durations are conjugate variables.
rules.check_logic: Verify that ΔE * Δt is calculated and satisfies the inequality ΔE * Δt ≥ ħ/2, ensuring that ΔE and Δt are positive quantities.
common_errors: Using ΔE or Δt as negative or zero
Confusing ΔE * Δt with Δx * Δp

rules.title: Check connection with wave-particle duality
rules.description: Ensure that the relationship between Δx and Δp aligns with the wave-particle duality, where Δp ≈ ħ/Δx for wave-like particles.
rules.check_logic: If the problem involves wave-particle duality, verify that Δp is inversely proportional to Δx, consistent with de Broglie's wavelength λ ≈ h/p.
common_errors: Ignoring the inverse relationship between Δx and Δp in wave-particle duality scenarios
Incorrectly assuming Δx * Δp = ħ instead of the inequality Δx * Δp ≥ ħ/2

rules.title: Verify quantum applicability for microscopic systems
rules.description: The Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle primarily applies to microscopic systems (e.g., electrons, atoms). Ensure it is not misapplied to classical, macroscopic systems where quantum effects are negligible.
rules.check_logic: Check that the system under consideration involves quantum scales (e.g., small particles or atomic dimensions).
common_errors: Applying the uncertainty principle to macroscopic objects where quantum effects are negligible
Ignoring the classical-to-quantum transition threshold

rules.title: Verify complementarity principle in uncertainty
rules.description: Ensure that the uncertainty principle is consistent with the complementarity principle, which states that precise knowledge of one conjugate variable (e.g., position) implies greater uncertainty in the other (e.g., momentum).
rules.check_logic: Verify that increasing precision in Δx leads to a corresponding increase in Δp, and vice versa, consistent with the complementarity principle.
common_errors: Ignoring the trade-off between Δx and Δp
Assuming both Δx and Δp can be minimized simultaneously

rules.title: 衰变常数与时间不确定性映射
rules.description:
触发条件：题目给出 decay time (τ) 要求计算能量不确定性时
检查逻辑：验证是否将平均寿命 τ 直接等同于 Δt。注意区分半衰期 T1/2 与平均寿命 τ，公式通常基于 τ。
rules.check_logic: 验证是否将平均寿命 τ 直接等同于 Δt。注意区分半衰期 T1/2 与平均寿命 τ，公式通常基于 τ。
rules.trigger: 题目给出 decay time (τ) 要求计算能量不确定性时

rules.title: 能量时间不确定性单位对齐
rules.description:
触发条件：计算 ΔE · Δt ≥ ħ/2 且参考答案单位为 Joule 时
检查逻辑：检查 ħ 是否使用了 J·s 单位（1.054e-34）而非 eV·s（6.582e-16），或最后是否执行了 eV 到 J 的乘积换算。
rules.check_logic: 检查 ħ 是否使用了 J·s 单位（1.054e-34）而非 eV·s（6.582e-16），或最后是否执行了 eV 到 J 的乘积换算。
rules.trigger: 计算 ΔE · Δt ≥ ħ/2 且参考答案单位为 Joule 时

rules.title: Inverse Compton does not require photon energy > m0 c^2; enforce vector momentum conservation
rules.description: Flag solutions to photon–electron scattering (Compton or inverse Compton) that infer from γ>1 or from an algebraic inconsistency that the incident photon must have energy comparable to or greater than the electron rest mass energy (E_photon ≥ m0 c^2 or '≫ m0 c^2'). In inverse Compton scattering, the photon gains energy from the relativistic electron; the incident photon need not exceed m0 c^2 and is often far below it. Also verify that momentum conservation is applied as a vector equation. Trigger if the solution: (a) invokes only scalar energy conservation without writing the vector momentum balance, (b) treats momentum magnitudes additively/subtractively (e.g., |p_e| = |p_i| − |p_0|) instead of using the vector relation p_e = p_i − p_0 with directions, or (c) explains contradictions by claiming 'insufficient photon energy' or that ICS requires E_photon ≳ m0 c^2. This rule catches concept errors that misattribute inconsistencies to energy scale rather than incorrect or incomplete momentum conservation.

rules.title: Consistent reference-isotope normalization for mixed vs pure samples in U–Pb dating
rules.description:
This rule checks that, when deriving equations for radiogenic lead buildup in a mixed uranium–lead ore using a pure lead ore as reference, the normalization to the reference isotope (e.g., 204Pb) is taken from the same sample whose ratios are being modeled. Specifically:
- When converting the difference in measured lead isotope ratios between the mixed sample and the pure reference into absolute radiogenic amounts, the relation must use the mixed sample's reference isotope count C = N_204_mixed: Δ206 = (R_206_mixed − R_206_pure) · N_204_mixed and Δ207 = (R_207_mixed − R_207_pure) · N_204_mixed.
- Equivalently, ratio equations for the mixed sample must use the mixed sample's reference normalization: R_206_mixed = R_206_pure + (N_238_initial / N_204_mixed) · f(T) and R_207_mixed = R_207_pure + (N_235_initial / N_204_mixed) · g(T), where f(T) and g(T) are the appropriate decay factors (e.g., e^{λT} − 1 or 1 − e^{−λT}, depending on formulation).
- The same normalization variable (C = N_204_mixed) must appear consistently in both the 206Pb and 207Pb equations; using N_204_pure (or any denominator derived from the pure sample) in equations for the mixed sample is a modeling error and should be flagged.
- Detection criteria: Flag any equation where added radiogenic terms for the mixed sample (e.g., contributions proportional to U decay) are divided by N_204_pure or otherwise normalized to the pure sample’s reference isotope. Also flag if the normalization switches between samples or differs between the 206Pb and 207Pb equations.
- Scope: U–Pb (or similar) isotope dating problems involving comparison of mixed samples to pure reference samples and conversion of ratio differences to absolute counts.

rules.title: Cross-sample normalization misuse in isotope ratio dating
rules.description:
Checks for flawed setups that equate normalization or reference counts across distinct samples in isotope ratio problems (e.g., mixed uranium–lead ore vs pure lead ore). The rule flags derivations that: 
- Introduce a single normalization variable (e.g., N_total, N_ref, N_204) and apply it to multiple distinct samples as if they share the same total atom count or reference count.
- Explicitly set N_204 (non-radiogenic lead reference) equal between samples (e.g., N_204^mixed = N_204^pure) or assume equal totals across samples.
- Use a cross-sample scaling factor derived from one sample’s Pb isotope ratios to relate uranium initial counts (N_238^0, N_235^0) to lead counts in another sample.
- Combine ratio sets from different samples under a single denominator or normalization, attempting to cancel sample-dependent quantities.
Correct reasoning must use within-sample ratios (e.g., (206/204)_mixed, (206/204)_pure) and compare their differences to isolate radiogenic lead, then incorporate the given U isotope ratio (N_238:N_235 = 137:1). Any derivation violating these constraints is flagged as a cross-sample normalization error.

rules.title: Two-photon annihilation: lab-frame angle completeness and momentum check
rules.description: Applies to electron–positron annihilation into two photons of equal energy when one particle (the positron) is at rest and the electron travels along the z-axis with kinetic energy T. The rule verifies that the solution is completed in the lab frame and that the angle α between the z-axis and a photon’s momentum is correctly derived using energy–momentum conservation with equal photon energies. Required checks: (1) The solution must provide an explicit formula for α and a numeric value for the given inputs. (2) It must use the lab-frame momentum relation 2 (Eγ/c) cos α = p_e, with Eγ = (T + 2 m_e c^2)/2 and p_e c = sqrt(T^2 + 2 T m_e c^2). Acceptable final forms include α = arccos[p_e c / (2 Eγ)], α = arccos[sqrt(T/(T + 2 m_e c^2))], or α = arccos[1 / sqrt(1 + 2 m_e c^2 / T)]. For T = 1 MeV (m_e c^2 ≈ 0.511 MeV), the expected numeric result is α ≈ 45.3°. The rule flags errors if: (a) α is not computed or the derivation is left incomplete; (b) the momentum relation is incorrect (e.g., missing the factor 2, using cos α = p_e c / Eγ, or assuming back-to-back z components without transverse cancellation); (c) an intermediate COM-frame transformation is used without returning to and resolving α in the lab frame; or (d) the numeric value deviates from the expected result beyond a reasonable tolerance (e.g., >2% for the given parameters).

rules.title: Misuse of free-particle uncertainty to estimate kinetic energy in uniform magnetic field
rules.description: This rule flags solutions that estimate the kinetic energy of an electron in a uniform magnetic field using a free-particle uncertainty argument (E ≈ (Δp)^2/(2m) with Δp ≈ ħ/(2Δx)) instead of Landau quantization. Trigger context: the problem involves a charged electron in 2D under a strong uniform B-field (e.g., FQHE, Hall effect, cyclotron motion, Landau levels). Detection criteria: (1) The solution explicitly invokes the Heisenberg relation Δx Δp ≥ ħ/2 and substitutes Δp ≈ ħ/(2Δx) (or similar inverse-length momentum estimate). (2) It then computes kinetic energy as E ≈ (Δp)^2/(2m) (or p^2/2m with p replaced by an uncertainty). (3) In the same energy estimate, there is no mention of magnetic quantization quantities: cyclotron frequency ω_c = eB/m, Landau level energies E_n = ħ ω_c (n + 1/2), magnetic length l_B = sqrt(ħ/(eB)), or minimal coupling p → p + eA / kinetic momentum π. (4) The resulting energy scale is expressed as E ∝ ħ^2/(m Δx^2) or uses Δx taken as a geometric/vortex/cyclotron radius r = mv/(eB), leading to energy that depends on v or yields coefficients like E ≈ ħ ω_c/8, i.e., not proportional to ħ ω_c with the correct lowest-level factor 1/2. If conditions (1)-(3) hold and the energy does not reduce to E0 = ħ ω_c/2 (e.g., by setting Δx = l_B), flag the solution. Rationale: In a uniform magnetic field the correct kinetic energy scale is set by Landau levels; using free-particle uncertainty ignores 2D motion and minimal coupling, causing systematic underestimates (commonly by a factor ~4) and incorrect B or v dependencies.

rules.title: Doppler sign and resonance consistency for emitted photon energy
rules.description: This rule checks Doppler-sign usage and resonance consistency in laser cooling/optical molasses solutions involving an atom moving relative to a counterpropagating laser beam. The verifier should: (1) Detect geometry: if the atom moves toward the laser (e.g., atom velocity +x and laser propagates −x), the nonrelativistic Doppler shift seen by the atom must be ω' = ω_L (1 + v/c) to O(v/c). Flag a sign error if ω' = ω_L (1 − v/c) is used in this approaching geometry. (2) Enforce resonance: if the solution asserts ω' = ω_0, then the lab laser frequency must satisfy ω_L ≈ ω_0 (1 − v/c) to first order. Flag if ω_L ≈ ω_0 (1 + v/c) or any inconsistent mapping is derived. (3) Check emitted photon energy consistency: for spontaneous emission, the average emitted photon energy in the lab must be ħω_0 to O(v/c) (first-order terms cancel), and if expressed via ω_L it must be ħ ω_L (1 + v/c) under the resonance constraint. Flag if the final expression is ħ ω_L (1 − v/c) or any linear-in-v deviation from ħω_0 that does not cancel after substituting the resonance relation. (4) Detect internal contradiction: if a solution simultaneously uses ω' = ω_0 and concludes an emitted energy that decreases linearly with +v (e.g., dE/dv < 0 via ħ ω_L (1 − v/c)), flag as violating the resonance-consistent dependence. This rule targets logic errors where the Doppler sign for approaching motion and the resonance condition are misapplied, leading to incorrect v/c dependence in the emitted energy.

rules.title: Magnetic moment scaling: exponent and unit consistency
rules.description: This rule checks for order-of-magnitude mistakes when computing a magnetic moment via scaling in Stern–Gerlach-type solutions. Trigger when a solution uses k = μ0/Δz0 and then μ = k × Δz (or equivalently μ = μ0 × Δz/Δz0). Procedure: (1) Normalize Δz and Δz0 to the same length unit (e.g., both in meters or both in centimeters). (2) Compute μ_expected = μ0 × (Δz/Δz0). (3) Compare the student’s μ against μ_expected and flag if: (a) the relative error |μ − μ_expected|/μ_expected > 0.2; or (b) the base-10 exponent of μ differs from that of μ_expected by ≥ 1 when 0.1 ≤ (Δz/Δz0) ≤ 10; or (c) the units of k × Δz do not reduce to J/T (e.g., k in J/T·cm⁻¹ requires Δz in cm, k in J/T·m⁻¹ requires Δz in m). Additionally, for numeric multiplications of the form (a × 10^n) × b where 0.1 ≤ b < 10 and b has no explicit power-of-ten, verify that the exponent n is unchanged in the product (i.e., result is (a·b) × 10^n). Flag if the exponent is incremented/decremented without a corresponding power-of-ten factor in b. This catches mistakes like yielding 1.456×10^-22 J/T instead of the correct 1.456×10^-23 J/T when multiplying k = 5.2×10^-23 by Δz = 0.28 (same units).

rules.title: Account for neutrino energy loss when using pp-chain Q-value for core heating
rules.description: Checks calculations that use nuclear fusion/fission Q-values for thermal energy or power deposition when the written reaction includes neutrinos among the products. Trigger conditions: (1) The solution writes or references a reaction with neutrino products (e.g., symbols "ν", "ν_e", "nu", "neutrino", "anti-neutrino"). Common example: 4p → He-4 + 2 e+ + 2 ν_e (pp-chain). (2) The solution computes per-reaction energy from mass defect/Q-value (e.g., Δm c^2 ≈ 26.7 MeV for 4p→He-4) and uses it directly to represent energy deposited in the star/plasma (keywords like "heats core", "thermal energy", "power in the core", "luminosity"), or multiplies by a reaction/production rate to get power. (3) No explicit subtraction or allowance for neutrino-carried energy is present (no mention of neutrino losses; no term removing E_ν; the deposited energy per 4p→He equals the full Q within a small tolerance, e.g., within ±1–3%). If all conditions hold, flag a conceptual error: the full mass defect/Q is not deposited as heat because neutrinos escape. Guidance for acceptance: the solution should either (a) explicitly subtract neutrino energy, e.g., E_deposited = Q − E_ν,total, or (b) use a stated deposited energy per 4p→He less than Q by a plausible amount (e.g., not equal to 26.73 MeV; typical deposited energy is slightly lower and depends on pp-branch; an explicit fractional reduction such as ~2% or a subtraction term per reaction is acceptable). Do not trigger if: (i) the reaction used has no neutrinos among products (e.g., D + T → He-4 + n), (ii) the solution clearly states it is computing the total nuclear Q (including energy carried by neutrinos) rather than thermal deposition, or (iii) the solution includes a neutrino-loss term or cites a deposited energy that is demonstrably less than the full Q and justified by neutrino escape.

rules.title: Use provided reaction and isotope masses for nuclear Q-value/energy calculations
rules.description:
This rule verifies that nuclear reaction and energy/Q-value calculations strictly use the reaction(s) and isotope masses supplied by the problem. It flags solutions that switch to a different reaction or import external mass values. Checks: 
- Reaction consistency: If the prompt explicitly provides one or more reactions (e.g., D–T fusion: 2H + 3H -> 4He + n; or a specific fission), the analyzed reaction must match one of those. Using an unrelated reaction (e.g., 4 1H -> 4He + 2 e+ + 2 νe) is flagged. 
- Isotope set adherence: Any isotope symbol used in equations or mass-defect/Q-value computations must be among those listed in the problem’s isotope table. Reference to isotopes not listed (e.g., 1H when only 2H, 3H, 4He, n are given) is flagged. 
- Mass source validation: Numeric mass values used must correspond to the provided table entries. Employing standard/known atomic masses not present in the table (e.g., 1.007825 u for 1H) is flagged. 
- Product/stoichiometry alignment: For D–T fusion, reactants/products must be {2H, 3H} -> {4He, n} without additional leptons unless specified. For any provided fission reaction, ensure the listed fragments and neutron count match. 
- Energy-rate linkage: When converting per-reaction energy to power using a production rate, ensure the rate corresponds to the product of the specified reaction (e.g., helium-4 rate for D–T fusion) and not to a different, unlisted process.
The rule aims to catch logical inconsistencies where the solver chooses a reaction or mass data outside the problem’s specified dataset, leading to incorrect Q-values or energies.

rules.title: Verify total binding energy calculation using mass defect
rules.description: The binding energy of a nucleus is calculated from the mass defect using the equation E = Δm * c^2, where Δm is the mass defect and c is the speed of light. This equation applies universally to nuclei.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that Δm is calculated as the difference between the total mass of individual nucleons (protons and neutrons) and the mass of the nucleus. Also, verify that the total binding energy is computed using the correct value of c (approximately 3.00 × 10^8 m/s).
common_errors: Incorrect calculation of mass defect (e.g., summing masses incorrectly)
Using an incorrect or approximate value for the speed of light
Failing to convert mass into energy units (e.g., not using Joules or MeV appropriately)

rules.title: Check stability criteria using binding energy per nucleon
rules.description: Stability of a nucleus is determined by its binding energy per nucleon. A higher binding energy per nucleon generally indicates a more stable nucleus. The peak stability occurs near iron (Fe-56).
rules.check_logic: Verify that the binding energy per nucleon is calculated by dividing the total binding energy by the number of nucleons. Compare the value to known benchmarks (e.g., Fe-56 ~ 8.8 MeV/nucleon).
common_errors: Forgetting to divide total binding energy by the number of nucleons
Incorrectly comparing stability to inappropriate benchmarks (e.g., lighter nuclei with heavy elements)

rules.title: Verify radioactive decay law calculations
rules.description: Radioactive decay follows the equation N(t) = N_0 * e^(-λt), where λ is the decay constant, N_0 is the initial number of nuclei, and N(t) is the number of nuclei at time t.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that the decay constant λ is correctly calculated using λ = ln(2)/T_1/2, where T_1/2 is the half-life. Verify the exponential decay formula is applied correctly and all units match appropriately.
common_errors: Using incorrect or inconsistent units for half-life and time
Using a wrong formula for decay constant (e.g., λ = 1/T_1/2 instead of λ = ln(2)/T_1/2)
Mistakes in exponential calculations or forgetting the negative sign in the exponent

rules.title: Check energy released in nuclear reactions
rules.description: Energy released in a nuclear reaction is calculated from the mass defect using E = Δm * c^2. The mass defect is the difference between the total mass of reactants and products.
rules.check_logic: Verify that Δm is computed as the difference between the mass of reactants and products. Ensure E is computed using the correct value of the speed of light, and maintain proper unit conversion.
common_errors: Failing to differentiate between reactants and products when calculating mass defect
Incorrectly handling unit conversions for mass or energy
Forgetting to square the speed of light in the energy calculation

rules.title: Verify conservation laws in decay chains
rules.description: In a decay chain, conservation of mass-energy and charge must be maintained. The sum of masses and charges before and after the decay must be equal.
rules.check_logic: Check whether the sum of atomic numbers (Z) and mass numbers (A) is conserved across each step of the decay chain.
common_errors: Ignoring conservation of charge or mass number in intermediate steps
Misidentifying the daughter nuclei or particles emitted during decay
Failing to account for neutrino or gamma emission in reactions

rules.title: Validate boundary conditions for radioactive decay
rules.description: Radioactivity equations assume a closed system where no external nuclei are added or removed. Additionally, t = 0 must correspond to N(t) = N_0.
rules.check_logic: Check that the initial number of nuclei N_0 and time t = 0 are consistent with the given data. Ensure no external processes interfere with the decay.
common_errors: Setting incorrect initial conditions (e.g., N_0 ≠ initial number of nuclei)
Failing to treat the system as closed (e.g., adding new nuclei during decay)
Misinterpreting time t = 0 or its role in the equation

rules.title: Verify sign convention for energy release
rules.description: Energy released in nuclear reactions is considered positive, while energy absorbed is negative. This sign convention must be maintained consistently.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that energy release is assigned a positive sign and energy absorption is assigned a negative sign in all calculations. Double-check the nature of the reaction (exothermic or endothermic).
common_errors: Assigning the wrong sign to energy release or absorption
Failing to distinguish between exothermic and endothermic reactions
Interchanging signs during intermediate steps of the calculation

rules.title: 天体物理极限值量级校验
rules.description:
触发条件：计算白矮星临界质量（钱德拉塞卡极限）或中子星质量极限时
检查逻辑：校验结果是否在 1.4 Ms 左右的物理合理区间。若计算结果偏离 1-10 倍太阳质量量级，需重点检查普朗克常数与引力常数的幂次运算。
rules.check_logic: 校验结果是否在 1.4 Ms 左右的物理合理区间。若计算结果偏离 1-10 倍太阳质量量级，需重点检查普朗克常数与引力常数的幂次运算。
rules.trigger: 计算白矮星临界质量（钱德拉塞卡极限）或中子星质量极限时

rules.title: 基本物理量纲一致性预检
rules.description:
触发条件：当推导或引用复杂的组合常数公式（如涉及 G, h, c, m）时
检查逻辑：检查公式各项的量纲组合是否等于目标物理量的量纲。例如质量 [M] 应对应 (hc/G)^3/2 * m^-2 等形式，若量纲不符则公式必错。
rules.check_logic: 检查公式各项的量纲组合是否等于目标物理量的量纲。例如质量 [M] 应对应 (hc/G)^3/2 * m^-2 等形式，若量纲不符则公式必错。
rules.trigger: 当推导或引用复杂的组合常数公式（如涉及 G, h, c, m）时

rules.title: 铀铅测年丰度比时间一致性
rules.description:
触发条件：题目给出238U:235U比例且涉及长时间跨度衰变时
检查逻辑：需区分该比例是“初始”还是“当前”。若为当前比例，方程两端需分别对应各自母核的衰变项，通常表现为 (207Pb*/206Pb*) = (U235/U238)_{now} * [(e^{\lambda_1 T}-1)/(e^{\lambda_2 T}-1)]。
rules.check_logic: 需区分该比例是“初始”还是“当前”。若为当前比例，方程两端需分别对应各自母核的衰变项，通常表现为 (207Pb*/206Pb*) = (U235/U238)_{now} * [(e^{\lambda_1 T}-1)/(e^{\lambda_2 T}-1)]。
rules.trigger: 题目给出238U:235U比例且涉及长时间跨度衰变时

rules.title: 核反应自发性结合能判据
rules.description:
触发条件：涉及核衰变（如alpha、beta衰变）或裂变/聚变的自发性判断时
检查逻辑：检查是否满足：生成物总结合能 > 反应物总结合能。对于 alpha 衰变：B(A,Z) < B(A-4, Z-2) + B(4,2)。
rules.check_logic: 检查是否满足：生成物总结合能 > 反应物总结合能。对于 alpha 衰变：B(A,Z) < B(A-4, Z-2) + B(4,2)。
rules.trigger: 涉及核衰变（如alpha、beta衰变）或裂变/聚变的自发性判断时

rules.title: 比结合能线性近似建模
rules.description:
触发条件：题目要求使用 linear approximation 处理 B/A 随 A 变化的关系时
检查逻辑：建立函数 f(A) = kA + b，总结合能 B = A * f(A) = kA^2 + bA。求导或差分时需保留 A 的二阶项贡献。
rules.check_logic: 建立函数 f(A) = kA + b，总结合能 B = A * f(A) = kA^2 + bA。求导或差分时需保留 A 的二阶项贡献。
rules.trigger: 题目要求使用 linear approximation 处理 B/A 随 A 变化的关系时

rules.title: 放射性定年参考同位素法
rules.description:
触发条件：出现非放射性成因同位素（如204Pb）作为参考且给出比例时
检查逻辑：必须以参考同位素数量为分母构建比值差方程：(i/ref)_mixed - (i/ref)_pure = (Δi/ref)，从而消去绝对质量干扰。
rules.check_logic: 必须以参考同位素数量为分母构建比值差方程：(i/ref)_mixed - (i/ref)_pure = (Δi/ref)，从而消去绝对质量干扰。
rules.trigger: 出现非放射性成因同位素（如204Pb）作为参考且给出比例时

rules.title: Use provided reaction and isotope masses for Q-value (flag pp-chain vs D–T mismatch)
rules.description:
This rule checks that the energy (Q-value) for a nuclear reaction is computed using the exact reaction and isotope masses specified in the problem. It flags solutions that model a different net reaction (e.g., the solar pp-chain 4 1H -> 4He + 2 e+ + 2 ν_e) when the prompt provides a different reaction (e.g., D–T fusion 2H + 3H -> 4He + n).

Trigger conditions:
- The problem statement contains an explicit nuclear reaction equation and isotope mass data for its isotopes (e.g., 2H, 3H, 4He, n for D–T fusion).
- The solution’s mass-defect formula or reaction text includes species not in the provided reaction (e.g., uses 1H, e+, ν_e, or omits the neutron when n is a product), or cites the pp-chain net reaction.
- The computed/assumed Q-value magnitude is characteristic of a different reaction (e.g., ~26–27 MeV per 4He for pp-chain) instead of the value implied by the provided masses (e.g., for D–T with given masses: Δm = m(2H)+m(3H) − [m(4He)+m(n)] ≈ 0.0188 u, Q ≈ 17.6 MeV using 931.5 MeV/u).

Checks enforced:
1) Reaction consistency: The isotopes used in Δm must match the provided reaction’s reactants and products exactly. For D–T fusion: Δm = m(2H)+m(3H) − [m(4He)+m(n)]. Using m(1H) or introducing e+, ν_e, or omitting n triggers a mismatch.
2) Mass source consistency: Isotope masses used must be drawn from the provided table (or standard values for neutron) corresponding to the specified isotopes.
3) Q-value tolerance: Compute the expected Q from the provided masses. If the solution’s reported or implied Q deviates by more than 15% from this value, or falls near a known alternate-reaction value (e.g., ~26–27 MeV for pp-chain) when the provided reaction is D–T, flag an error.

On flag: Report a modeling error: “Use the given reaction and isotope masses. For 2H+3H->4He+n, include the neutron on the product side and use Δm = m(2H)+m(3H) − [m(4He)+m(n)] to obtain Q ≈ 17.6 MeV, not the pp-chain ~26.7 MeV.”

rules.title: Verify conservation of mass-energy in nuclear reactions
rules.description: In nuclear reactions, the total mass-energy (rest mass energy + kinetic energy) before and after the reaction must be conserved. This principle is derived from Einstein's equation E=mc².
rules.check_logic: Ensure the total mass-energy before the reaction equals the total mass-energy after the reaction. Apply E=mc² for any mass defect and include the energy of emitted photons or radiation.
common_errors: Failing to account for the mass defect in calculations.
Ignoring the energy of emitted photons or radiation.
Incorrectly summing the rest mass without converting to energy using c².

rules.title: Check conservation of linear momentum
rules.description: Linear momentum must be conserved in all nuclear reactions. This principle applies to both fission and fusion reactions, accounting for all particles and emitted radiation.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the total momentum (vector sum) of all particles and radiation before the reaction equals the total momentum after the reaction. Include the momentum of emitted photons (p = E/c) and account for the recoil momentum of the nucleus.
common_errors: Forgetting to include the momentum of emitted photons (p = E/c).
Incorrectly assuming scalar momentum instead of vector momentum.
Ignoring the recoil momentum of the nucleus.

rules.title: Validate binding energy calculations
rules.description: The binding energy is the energy required to separate a nucleus into its component nucleons. It is calculated using the mass defect and E=mc².
rules.check_logic: Compare the sum of the masses of individual nucleons with the mass of the nucleus and compute the binding energy using E=mc². Ensure the sign of the binding energy is negative for stable nuclei.
common_errors: Ignoring the mass defect in the calculation of binding energy.
Mistaking the sign of binding energy (it should be negative for stable nuclei).
Incorrectly using atomic mass instead of nuclear mass (omitting electron mass corrections).

rules.title: Verify conditions for nuclear reaction feasibility
rules.description: For a nuclear reaction to occur, specific conditions must be met, such as overcoming the Coulomb barrier (fusion) or sufficient neutron absorption (fission).
rules.check_logic: Ensure that input energy exceeds the Coulomb barrier for fusion or that sufficient neutrons are present for fission to sustain a chain reaction. Verify that the reaction meets the required activation energy or threshold conditions.
common_errors: Neglecting the Coulomb barrier requirement for fusion.
Overlooking the critical mass and neutron multiplication factor for fission.
Misinterpreting reaction thresholds or activation energy.

rules.title: Confirm sign conventions for energy and mass changes
rules.description: In nuclear reactions, energy released is typically considered positive, while energy absorbed is negative. Similarly, mass defect is positive when mass is converted to energy.
rules.check_logic: Check whether energy released is marked as positive and energy absorbed is negative. Verify that mass defect is positive for energy release and ensure consistency in sign conventions across calculations.
common_errors: Reversing the sign of energy release and absorption.
Assigning a negative mass defect for energy-releasing reactions.
Confusing the direction of energy flow in exothermic and endothermic reactions.

rules.title: Ensure dimensional and unit consistency
rules.description: In nuclear physics, quantities like energy (MeV), mass (u or kg), and momentum (kg·m/s) must be dimensionally consistent. Often, energy is expressed in MeV, and mass is related to it using E=mc².
rules.check_logic: Verify that calculations involving energy, mass, and momentum maintain consistent units. Convert mass defect to energy using c² and ensure units match. Check for proper conversions between SI and non-SI units.
common_errors: Mixing SI and non-SI units (e.g., MeV and Joules) without proper conversion.
Incorrectly applying E=mc² without converting mass to kilograms.
Using inconsistent units for velocity or momentum.

rules.title: Assess fusion reaction efficiency
rules.description: Fusion reactions are most efficient when the reactants are light nuclei, such as hydrogen isotopes, due to the higher binding energy per nucleon. Efficiency decreases for heavier nuclei.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the fusion reaction involves light nuclei (e.g., hydrogen isotopes). Compute the energy yield and compare it to the binding energy per nucleon curve. Ensure optimal conditions for fusion, such as high temperature and pressure, are met.
common_errors: Attempting to fuse heavy nuclei without considering the energy losses.
Ignoring the optimal conditions for fusion (e.g., temperature and pressure).
Using incorrect data for binding energy per nucleon.

rules.title: Validate chain reaction sustainability in fission
rules.description: A fission chain reaction is sustained if the multiplication factor (k) is greater than or equal to 1, meaning each fission event leads to at least one more.
rules.check_logic: Check whether the multiplication factor k ≥ 1 and whether neutron losses are minimized to sustain the chain reaction. Verify that the number of neutrons produced per fission is sufficient to maintain criticality.
common_errors: Ignoring neutron leakage or absorption in non-fissionable materials.
Misinterpreting subcritical (k < 1), critical (k = 1), and supercritical (k > 1) states.
Failing to account for the number of neutrons produced per fission.

rules.title: Verify energy yield calculations in nuclear reactions
rules.description: The energy yield of a nuclear reaction is determined by the difference in binding energy between reactants and products. This energy is released or absorbed during the reaction.
rules.check_logic: Calculate the binding energy of reactants and products using E=mc². Verify that the energy yield matches the difference in binding energy and ensure proper sign conventions are applied.
common_errors: Failing to calculate binding energy differences accurately.
Ignoring the contribution of emitted radiation to the energy yield.
Using incorrect mass or energy data for reactants and products.

rules.title: Do not assume k=0 when deriving evolution of Omega-1
rules.description: This rule flags solutions to cosmology problems that ask for the time or scale-factor dependence of curvature deviations (e.g., (Omega(t) - 1), curvature parameter evolution, or deviations from critical density) when the solution prematurely assumes a flat universe (k = 0) or uses the flat Friedmann equation. Checks performed: (1) The prompt contains targets such as 'Omega - 1', 'deviation from flatness', 'curvature evolution', or 'how Omega approaches 1' in radiation- or matter-dominated eras. (2) The solution sets k = 0, declares 'flat universe', or omits the curvature term (kc^2/a^2) from the Friedmann equation at the outset, thereby making Omega - 1 identically zero. (3) The solution does not later reinstate curvature or use the identity Omega - 1 = (k c^2)/(a^2 H^2), nor does it derive the scaling of Omega - 1 with a(t) or t for the specified era. If all these conditions are met, the solution is flagged for a modeling error: the student has eliminated the very quantity whose evolution is requested. Expected correct approach: retain k symbolically, use Omega - 1 = (k c^2)/(a^2 H^2), combine with the era-specific behavior of H(a) (e.g., H^2 ∝ a^-4 for radiation, H^2 ∝ a^-3 for matter) to obtain how |Omega - 1| scales with a or t; only then may the flat limit be discussed as a special case.

rules.title: Completeness of Omega(t)−1 evolution across cosmological eras
rules.description: This rule verifies that solutions to problems requesting the time-dependence of (Omega(t) − 1) provide a complete and explicit derivation for each specified cosmological regime (e.g., radiation-dominated and matter-dominated). The checker will flag an answer if any of the following are true: (1) Missing regimes: the solution fails to treat all regimes requested (e.g., includes only radiation or only matter, or treats neither explicitly). (2) No final functional dependence: the solution does not present an explicit functional form or power-law for (Omega(t) − 1) as a function of time t (or equivalently scale factor a), for each regime. Acceptable endpoints include, for example, Omega − 1 ∝ t for radiation (w = 1/3) and Omega − 1 ∝ t^{2/3} for matter (w = 0), or the equivalent scale-factor scalings Omega − 1 ∝ a^2 (radiation) and Omega − 1 ∝ a (matter), or the general relation Omega − 1 = −k c^2/(a^2 H^2) combined with a(t) or H(a) to yield the time dependence. (3) Premature termination/incompleteness: the solution stops after stating the Friedmann equations or definitions (e.g., H, rho_crit) without carrying through the derivation to the requested dependence, or ends abruptly/mid-derivation. (4) Inappropriate flatness assumption: the solution assumes k = 0 (flat universe) when asked to derive the evolution of Omega − 1, which makes Omega = 1 identically and evades the requested analysis. The rule is triggered for tasks that explicitly ask for the dependence of (Omega(t) − 1) on time in specified eras; it passes only if each requested era is addressed and a correct explicit dependence is provided for each.

rules.title: Require Ω−1–curvature relation in Friedmann-based derivations
rules.description: This rule verifies that any solution deriving the time dependence of the density parameter deviation (Ω(t) − 1) or discussing flatness uses the curvature term from the first Friedmann equation. Specifically, the solution must explicitly relate deviation from flatness to spatial curvature via Ω − 1 = k c^2 / (a^2 H^2), or equivalently 1 = Ω + Ω_k with Ω_k = −k c^2 / (a^2 H^2). The rule flags solutions that: (1) set k = 0 (assume exact flatness) while attempting to derive Ω − 1 as a function of time; (2) define Ω = ρ/ρ_c but never connect Ω − 1 to the curvature term −k c^2/a^2 in the Friedmann equation; (3) present the curvature–Ω relation with the wrong sign (e.g., Ω − 1 = −k c^2/(a^2 H^2) or Ω_k = +k c^2/(a^2 H^2)); (4) omit the curvature term entirely when using H^2 = (8πG/3)ρ − k c^2/a^2. For problems requesting time dependence in radiation- or matter-dominated regimes, the rule additionally checks consistency that the stated scaling of Ω − 1 follows from a(t) and H(t): radiation-dominated should yield Ω − 1 ∝ a^2 (∝ t), matter-dominated should yield Ω − 1 ∝ a (∝ t^{2/3}). Any derivation of Ω − 1 without invoking the curvature relation or with incorrect sign/conclusions is flagged.

rules.title: Energy accounting in cascaded photomultipliers must include bypass fractions (1−η) and (1−σ)
rules.description:
This rule checks energy accounting in problems involving photomultiplier tubes or similar cascaded, multi-gap accelerators with dynodes, where parameters η (photocathode-to-first-dynode collection efficiency), σ (inter-dynode collection efficiency), δ (secondary emission per collected electron), V (uniform gap potential), and n (number of dynodes) are given or implied.

What the rule verifies:
1) Completeness of branch contributions: The total energy to amplify one photoelectron must equal e·V times the expected number of gap crossings by all electrons produced. A correct solution must explicitly account for:
   a) Direct-to-anode photoelectrons: a (1−η) fraction of initial photoelectrons that bypass the first dynode and traverse all n+1 gaps to the anode, contributing a term proportional to (1−η)(n+1)eV.
   b) Bypass at each dynode: at dynode i (1 ≤ i ≤ n), a (1−σ) fraction of the δ·N_i emitted electrons that go straight to the anode, crossing (n−i+1) gaps, contributing terms proportional to (1−σ)×(n−i+1)×eV×δ×N_i (or an equivalent aggregated expression).
   c) Forward-collected electrons: the σ fraction that proceeds to the next dynode, each crossing one gap and contributing eV per stage (e.g., eV×N_{i+1}).

2) Presence of bypass factors: Flag solutions that omit (1−η) and/or (1−σ) in the energy computation, or that implicitly set η = 1 or σ = 1 without justification.

3) Parameter dependence and scaling: The final energy expression must depend on η, σ, δ, V, and n. For δσ > 1, the average energy should grow with the cascade multiplication, typically showing dependence like (δσ)^n (or an equivalent exponential-in-n growth). Flag solutions that yield energy independent of n, only linear in n without δσ multiplicative growth, or that lack δ and σ in the dominant scaling term.

4) Gap-count correctness: Verify that energy contributions weight eV by the correct number of gaps traversed (e.g., n+1 for direct photoelectrons, n−i+1 for dynode bypasses). Flag solutions that count only one gap for electrons that go straight to the anode or otherwise miscount path lengths.

5) Dimensional consistency: Energy must be proportional to e·V times a dimensionless expected count of crossings. Flag use of incorrect units (e.g., e^2, V^2) or missing e·V factor.

This rule triggers when a solution computes the average/total energy required to amplify one photoelectron in a multi-dynode system and will flag modeling errors where bypass paths to the anode are ignored or miscounted, or where the cascade multiplication and gap traversal are not properly reflected in the energy sum.

rules.title: Verify conservation of baryon and lepton numbers
rules.description: In particle physics, baryon number and lepton number must be conserved in all interactions (exceptions occur with certain anomalies or in neutrino oscillations). This rule ensures that the sum of baryon and lepton numbers remains unchanged before and after any reaction.
rules.check_logic: Sum the baryon number and lepton number for all particles on both sides of the equation and verify that the totals before and after the reaction are equal.
common_errors: Neglecting neutrinos' lepton number contribution
Incorrectly assigning baryon number to non-baryonic particles
Forgetting to include antiparticles with negative baryon or lepton numbers

rules.title: Check charge conservation in particle interactions
rules.description: The total electric charge in a particle interaction must remain conserved. This applies to decays, annihilations, and collisions involving quarks, leptons, and bosons.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that the sum of electric charges of all particles before the interaction equals the sum of electric charges after the interaction.
common_errors: Incorrect charge assignment for quarks (+2/3 or -1/3)
Forgetting the charge of neutral particles like neutrinos or photons
Misinterpreting the charge of antiparticles (opposite to their corresponding particles)

rules.title: Verify mass-energy conservation
rules.description: Mass-energy equivalence (E = mc^2) must be maintained in all high-energy interactions. For processes involving particle creation or annihilation, the total energy, including rest mass energy, kinetic energy, and potential energy, must remain constant.
rules.check_logic: Calculate the total energy before and after the reaction, ensuring that rest mass energy, kinetic energy, and other forms of energy are accounted for and balanced.
common_errors: Ignoring mass-energy equivalence for intermediate particles
Forgetting to include relativistic kinetic energy in high-speed scenarios
Miscalculating photon energy (use E = hf for photons)

rules.title: Ensure spin conservation in particle reactions
rules.description: In particle interactions, the total spin, including intrinsic spin and orbital angular momentum, must be conserved. Exceptions include weak interactions where parity violation occurs.
rules.check_logic: Add the quantum spin states of all particles pre- and post-interaction, ensuring that total angular momentum is conserved.
common_errors: Neglecting the contribution of orbital angular momentum in multi-particle systems
Misinterpreting spin states for bosons (integer spin) versus fermions (half-integer spin)
Overlooking spin alignment in reactions involving polarized particles

rules.title: Validate exchange of force carrier bosons
rules.description: In interactions mediated by fundamental forces, check that the appropriate boson (photon, W/Z boson, gluon, or graviton) is involved as the force carrier. Ensure the boson's properties (mass, charge, spin) align with the interaction.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the boson involved matches the force type (e.g., photon for electromagnetic, gluon for strong, W/Z bosons for weak) and possesses the correct properties.
common_errors: Assigning a gluon to electromagnetic interactions
Using a massless boson for weak interactions instead of W/Z bosons
Incorrect spin or charge attribution for a given boson

rules.title: Check quark confinement and color neutrality
rules.description: Quarks cannot exist in isolation due to color confinement. All observable particles (hadrons) must be color-neutral, forming either baryons (three quarks) or mesons (quark-antiquark pairs).
rules.check_logic: Ensure that all final-state particles are color-neutral and that quarks combine properly to form baryons or mesons.
common_errors: Allowing free quarks in final states
Incorrect color-neutral combinations (e.g., two quark states without an antiquark)
Misinterpreting color charge conservation in intermediate steps

rules.title: Verify weak interaction constraints
rules.description: Weak interactions involve flavor-changing processes and are mediated by W and Z bosons. Ensure that such interactions follow rules of charge conservation, allow for specific flavor transitions (except neutrino mixing), and account for parity violation where applicable.
rules.check_logic: Check for charge conservation and allowed flavor transitions, ensuring that parity violation is considered in processes involving neutrinos.
common_errors: Neglecting neutrino involvement in beta decay
Violating charge conservation in weak interactions
Applying parity conservation to weak interactions (which is not valid)

rules.title: Check if the Pauli Exclusion Principle applies to fermions
rules.description: The Pauli Exclusion Principle states that no two identical fermions (particles with half-integer spin, such as electrons, neutrons, or protons) in a system can occupy the same quantum state simultaneously. This principle does not apply to bosons (particles with integer spin).
rules.check_logic: Ensure the particles under consideration are fermions by verifying their spin quantum number (half-integer values like ±1/2, ±3/2, etc.).
common_errors: Applying the Pauli Exclusion Principle to bosons (e.g., photons or helium-4 nuclei).
Incorrectly identifying the spin of the particle.

rules.title: Verify quantum state uniqueness for fermions
rules.description: Each quantum state is defined by a unique set of quantum numbers (n, l, ml, ms). For fermions obeying the Pauli Exclusion Principle, no two identical particles in the same atom or system can have the same set of quantum numbers.
rules.check_logic: Confirm that for all fermions in the system, no two particles share the same full set of quantum numbers (n, l, ml, ms).
common_errors: Allowing two electrons in the same atom to have identical quantum numbers.
Neglecting the spin quantum number (ms) when verifying uniqueness.

rules.title: Ensure correct sign convention in quantum states
rules.description: Quantum numbers such as magnetic quantum number (ml) and spin quantum number (ms) can take positive and negative values depending on the system's coordinate axes. Incorrect sign usage leads to invalid quantum states.
rules.check_logic: Verify that ml values range from -l to +l and ms values are either +1/2 or -1/2 for fermions.
common_errors: Using positive-only values for ml or ms.
Assigning an ms value outside the valid range for fermions.

rules.title: Check validity within atomic structure constraints
rules.description: The Pauli Exclusion Principle governs electron configurations in atoms. Electrons fill orbitals in a way that obeys this principle, along with the Aufbau principle and Hund's rule.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that each orbital (defined by n and l) has at most two electrons, and these two electrons must have opposite spins (ms = +1/2 and -1/2).
common_errors: Placing more than two electrons in the same orbital.
Assigning the same spin to both electrons in an orbital.

rules.title: Verify dimensional consistency of quantum numbers
rules.description: Quantum numbers are dimensionless quantities. Using incorrect units or dimensions in quantum number calculations or assignments is invalid.
rules.check_logic: Ensure quantum numbers (e.g., n, l, ml, ms) are dimensionless integers or half-integers as appropriate.
common_errors: Assigning dimensional quantities (e.g., energy or length) to quantum numbers.
Misinterpreting quantum numbers as having physical units.

rules.title: Check constraints on multi-particle wavefunctions
rules.description: For a system of identical fermions, the total wavefunction must be antisymmetric under particle exchange. This is a direct consequence of the Pauli Exclusion Principle.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the total wavefunction changes sign (antisymmetric) when two identical fermions are swapped.
common_errors: Using a symmetric wavefunction for identical fermions.
Neglecting to check antisymmetry during multi-particle system analysis.

rules.title: Verify consistency with Fermi-Dirac statistics
rules.description: Fermions obey Fermi-Dirac statistics, which determine the probability of occupancy of quantum states at a given temperature. The Pauli Exclusion Principle enforces that occupancy probabilities do not exceed 1.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that the probability of occupancy for any quantum state is between 0 and 1, inclusive, and that Fermi-Dirac statistics are used for fermions.
common_errors: Assigning occupancy probabilities greater than 1.
Using Bose-Einstein statistics or Maxwell-Boltzmann statistics for fermions.

rules.title: Ensure compatibility of spin with magnetic properties
rules.description: The spin quantum number (ms) contributes to the magnetic moment of a particle. For electrons, spin values of +1/2 and -1/2 correspond to different orientations of the magnetic moment.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the spin quantum number contributes correctly to the magnetic moment calculations or interactions in the system, and ensure the relationship between spin and magnetic properties is consistent with physical laws.
common_errors: Neglecting the contribution of ms to magnetic moment.
Misinterpreting the relationship between spin and magnetic properties.

rules.title: Verify interaction of fermions with external fields
rules.description: Fermions interact with external electric and magnetic fields based on their charge, spin, and magnetic moment. These interactions must respect the Pauli Exclusion Principle and quantum mechanical constraints.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that the interaction of fermions with external fields does not violate the Pauli Exclusion Principle, and verify that spin and magnetic moment contributions are correctly accounted for.
common_errors: Ignoring the effect of external fields on spin alignment.
Violating the Pauli Exclusion Principle during field interactions.

rules.title: Require exponential decay model and time-constant bound for persistent current tests
rules.description: Scope: Solutions to problems that bound superconducting resistivity from long-term stability of a persistent current in a closed loop (e.g., single-turn superconducting coil) with given initial current I0, measurement resolution ΔI, and observation time T. What to check: (1) Dynamic model: The solution must model the current decay in a closed loop with a tiny residual resistance as exponential, using either I(t) = I0·exp(−t/τ) or dI/dt = −I/τ, where τ is a decay time constant (e.g., τ = Lc/R for an RL loop). (2) Measurement constraint: The solution must translate the “no measurable change” statement into a lower bound on τ via |I(T) − I0| ≤ ΔI, giving τ ≥ T / ln(I0/(I0 − ΔI)) ≈ (T·I0/ΔI) when ΔI ≪ I0. (3) Mapping to resistivity: To bound ρ, the solution must either (a) use the microscopic Drude relation ρ = m/(n e^2 τ) when n (and fundamental constants) are provided, or (b) use τ = Lc/R together with R = ρ·(Lwire/A) when geometric data and loop inductance are available. (4) Avoidance of improper steady-state modeling: Flag solutions that treat the situation with a static Ohm’s law V = IR across a closed loop without invoking inductive dynamics and a time constant, or that base the bound solely on constant power/energy dissipation arguments without an explicit exponential decay model. (5) Inductance handling: If inductance L is not provided and no geometry is given, the solution should not require L to proceed; it should instead employ the Drude relation to eliminate L. Flag solutions that get stuck or introduce a needed L without subsequently eliminating it. Violation indicators include: absence of an exponential decay or time-constant equation; failure to convert (ΔI, T) into a bound on τ; claims of a steady nonzero voltage drop around a closed superconducting loop as the primary reasoning; or reliance solely on V = IR or Joule heating without temporal decay.

rules.title: Verify Einstein’s photoelectric equation
rules.description: Ensure the equation K_max = hf - ϕ is correctly applied, where K_max is the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted electrons, hf is the energy of the incident photon, and ϕ is the material's work function.
rules.check_logic: Check that the maximum kinetic energy (K_max) is calculated as the difference between the photon's energy (hf) and the material's work function (ϕ), ensuring hf > ϕ for photoemission. If hf ≤ ϕ, no photoemission should occur.
common_errors: Forgetting to subtract the work function (ϕ).
Incorrect calculation of hf using Planck’s constant and frequency.
Using the wrong sign for the work function.
Allowing photoemission when hf ≤ ϕ.

rules.title: Validate threshold frequency condition
rules.description: Ensure that the photon frequency (f) is greater than or equal to the threshold frequency (f_threshold = ϕ/h) for photoelectric emission to occur.
rules.check_logic: Verify that f >= ϕ/h; if not, no photoemission should be calculated. Ensure Planck's constant (h) and the work function (ϕ) are in consistent units.
common_errors: Calculating photoemission for frequencies below the threshold.
Using incorrect units for frequency or Planck's constant.
Neglecting the threshold frequency condition entirely.

rules.title: Check energy conservation in Compton scattering
rules.description: In Compton scattering, total energy is conserved. Ensure that the sum of the incident photon energy and the target electron's initial energy equals the sum of the scattered photon energy and the recoiling electron's energy.
rules.check_logic: Check that E_photon_initial + E_electron_initial = E_photon_scattered + E_electron_recoil. Ensure the electron's initial rest energy (m_e * c^2) is included in E_electron_initial.
common_errors: Neglecting the electron's initial rest energy.
Incorrectly calculating the scattered photon's energy.
Using inconsistent units for energy terms.
Ignoring relativistic effects for high-energy photons.

rules.title: Verify momentum conservation in Compton scattering
rules.description: Momentum is conserved in Compton scattering. Ensure that the vector sum of the initial momenta equals the vector sum of the final momenta of the photon and the electron.
rules.check_logic: Verify that p_photon_initial + p_electron_initial = p_photon_scattered + p_electron_recoil, ensuring vector components are resolved correctly. Include relativistic momentum for the electron if necessary.
common_errors: Forgetting to account for the vector nature of momentum.
Incorrectly resolving momentum components into x and y directions.
Using the wrong expressions for photon or electron momentum.
Neglecting relativistic momentum for high-energy interactions.

rules.title: Validate Compton wavelength shift formula
rules.description: Ensure the formula for Compton wavelength shift, Δλ = (h/mc)(1 - cosθ), is correctly applied, where θ is the scattering angle, h is Planck's constant, m is the electron mass, and c is the speed of light.
rules.check_logic: Check that Δλ is calculated as (h/mc)(1 - cosθ), ensuring θ is in radians. Verify that h, m, and c are in consistent units.
common_errors: Using θ in degrees instead of radians.
Misplacing the factor (h/mc).
Incorrect evaluation of (1 - cosθ).
Using inconsistent units for h, m, or c.

rules.title: Ensure unit consistency for photoelectric equations
rules.description: Verify that the units in the photoelectric equation K_max = hf - ϕ are consistent, particularly ensuring energy terms are in joules or electron volts.
rules.check_logic: Check that Planck's constant (h) and frequency (f) produce energy in joules, and the work function (ϕ) is in the same unit as the kinetic energy (K_max). Ensure proper conversion between joules and electron volts if necessary.
common_errors: Mixing units like joules and electron volts without conversion.
Using incorrect units for Planck's constant (e.g., J·s vs eV·s).
Neglecting unit conversion between ϕ and K_max.

rules.title: Check validity conditions for Compton scattering
rules.description: Compton scattering applies only to high-energy photons (e.g., X-rays or gamma rays) interacting with free or loosely bound electrons. Ensure the problem setup satisfies these conditions.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the incident photon energy is sufficiently high (e.g., > keV range), and the electron is either free or loosely bound. Ensure the photon energy is much greater than the electron's binding energy if the electron is not free.
common_errors: Applying Compton scattering to low-energy (visible light) photons.
Assuming tightly bound electrons instead of free electrons.
Ignoring the incident photon energy range requirement.

rules.title: Verify sign conventions in photoelectric equations
rules.description: Ensure correct sign conventions are used in the photoelectric equations, where energy terms are positive and subtractive terms (e.g., ϕ) are appropriately negative.
rules.check_logic: Confirm that energy terms (hf, ϕ, K_max) are positive, and their relationships respect the equation K_max = hf - ϕ. Ensure no negative kinetic energy is calculated.
common_errors: Assigning the wrong sign to the work function (ϕ).
Incorrectly using negative kinetic energy.
Flipping the direction of subtraction in K_max = hf - ϕ.

rules.title: Verify photon energy-wavelength relationship
rules.description: Ensure the relationship E = hc/λ is correctly applied, where E is the photon energy, h is Planck's constant, c is the speed of light, and λ is the wavelength.
rules.check_logic: Check that E is calculated as hc/λ, ensuring λ is in meters and h and c are in consistent units. Verify proper conversion to electron volts if necessary.
common_errors: Using incorrect units for wavelength (e.g., nm instead of m) without conversion.
Misplacing the factors h or c in the formula.
Neglecting unit conversion for energy (e.g., joules to electron volts).

rules.title: 各向同性发射的平均能量守恒
rules.description:
触发条件：出现“等概率向相反方向自发辐射”或“各向同性发射”
检查逻辑：在实验室系下，平均发射能量应等于原子运动系能量乘以(1+β_avg)，若发射对称则平均速度贡献项不应抵消吸收项的频移。
rules.check_logic: 在实验室系下，平均发射能量应等于原子运动系能量乘以(1+β_avg)，若发射对称则平均速度贡献项不应抵消吸收项的频移。
rules.trigger: 出现“等概率向相反方向自发辐射”或“各向同性发射”

rules.title: 多普勒频移方向一致性检查
rules.description:
触发条件：涉及波源与观察者相对运动（如激光冷却、原子吸收光谱）
检查逻辑：若两者相互靠近（counterpropagating），频率必增大（蓝移，1+v/c）；若相互远离，频率必减小（红移，1-v/c）。
rules.check_logic: 若两者相互靠近（counterpropagating），频率必增大（蓝移，1+v/c）；若相互远离，频率必减小（红移，1-v/c）。
rules.trigger: 涉及波源与观察者相对运动（如激光冷却、原子吸收光谱）

rules.title: 阿伦尼乌斯图表参数提取
rules.description:
触发条件：出现形如 i = i0 * exp(-E/kT) 的指数演化图表时
检查逻辑：检查是否通过取对数转化为线性关系 ln(i) = -E/k * (1/T) + ln(i0)，并利用斜率提取激活能或能隙 E。
rules.check_logic: 检查是否通过取对数转化为线性关系 ln(i) = -E/k * (1/T) + ln(i0)，并利用斜率提取激活能或能隙 E。
rules.trigger: 出现形如 i = i0 * exp(-E/kT) 的指数演化图表时

rules.title: 热源激发阈值匹配原则
rules.description:
触发条件：要求估算“刚好能激发”某种能隙的热源温度时
检查逻辑：需建立光子能量 E=hf 与能隙 ΔEg 的等值关系，再结合维恩位移定律或平均热能 E≈k_B*T 进行量级估算。
rules.check_logic: 需建立光子能量 E=hf 与能隙 ΔEg 的等值关系，再结合维恩位移定律或平均热能 E≈k_B*T 进行量级估算。
rules.trigger: 要求估算“刚好能激发”某种能隙的热源温度时

rules.title: Incorrectly summing all stage voltages for energy of a single electron in PMT/dynode chains
rules.description: This rule flags solutions in photomultiplier or secondary-emission dynode contexts that compute the energy to accelerate a single electron as e times the sum of all stage voltages (e.g., (n+1)eV) or assert that one electron crosses all gaps. In a PMT, each electron only traverses one gap per transit and is absorbed at a dynode; new electrons are emitted and then cross subsequent gaps. Therefore, the per-electron transit energy is eΔV for the specific gap crossed, not e times the total device voltage. The correct total energy consumption for amplifying one photoelectron is the sum over all electrons of eΔV for each gap they individually cross, accounting for δ (secondary emission gain) and collection efficiencies (η, σ). Trigger conditions include: (a) presence of PMT/dynode keywords (photomultiplier, dynode, secondary emission, η, σ, δ) and (b) expressions or statements like E_per_electron = e*(n+1)*V, energy per electron equals total tube voltage, or equivalent summations over all gaps without aggregating over the multiplied electrons and their per-gap transits.

rules.title: Equal-energy two-photon annihilation: lab-frame angle consistency
rules.description: Checks momentum-conservation consistency for problems where a moving particle (net initial momentum along a coordinate axis, typically z) annihilates with a target at rest to produce two photons of equal energy in the lab. Common error: assuming the photons are back-to-back in the lab (e.g., θ_B = 180° − θ_A or p_B = −p_A) because they are back-to-back in the COM frame. If the student imposes θ_B = 180° − θ_A with E_A = E_B while the initial longitudinal momentum p_initial ≠ 0, the final z-momentum sums to zero (p_Az + p_Bz = 0), violating conservation. The correct lab-frame configuration for equal-energy photons is same polar angle and opposite azimuths (θ_A = θ_B = α, φ_B = φ_A + π), so transverse components cancel and longitudinal momentum adds: 2 (E_γ / c) cos α = p_initial_z. This rule flags solutions that (a) claim or enforce back-to-back polar angles in the lab for equal-energy photons when p_initial ≠ 0, (b) yield p_Az + p_Bz = 0 with E_A = E_B despite nonzero p_initial_z, or (c) omit azimuthal opposition while assigning unequal polar angles for equal-energy photons. It allows back-to-back only in the COM frame (p_initial = 0), and accepts solutions that use the correct relation cos α = (p_initial c) / (2 E_γ) or explicitly set θ_A = θ_B and φ_B = φ_A + π.

rules.title: Incorrect symmetry justification for equilibrium in asymmetric potentials
rules.description: Flag any solution that claims a potential is symmetric (even) about the expansion point and uses that symmetry to justify V'(x0)=0 when the potential provided is not actually even. Typical case: the Morse potential (e.g., V(x) = V0(e^{-αx} − 2e^{-βx}) or V(x) = D(e^{-a(x−x0)}−1)^2) is asymmetric and does not satisfy V(x0+δ) = V(x0−δ). Detection cues include phrases like 'symmetric around x=0', 'even potential', 'V(−x)=V(x)', or 'by symmetry, dV/dx|_{x0}=0' applied to Morse or any potential whose functional form is not even about the expansion point. Required reasoning: V'(x0)=0 should be justified because x0 is a minimum (equilibrium) or shown by explicit differentiation, not by symmetry unless evenness has been correctly established.

rules.title: Do not infer spectral index from particle-number conservation alone
rules.description: This rule flags solutions that claim the post-process spectral index (q) of a power-law electron energy distribution is determined by particle-number conservation (N_final = N_initial) without providing a justified energy-space mapping. Number conservation constrains only the integrated count or normalization, not the exponent of the distribution. The verifier will look for arguments that equate integrals of the form ∫ κ0 ε^{-p} dε = ∫ κ ε^{-q} dε and conclude q = p from N conservation, or statements such as 'by number conservation, the spectral index is unchanged'. To pass, the solution must explicitly present the distribution transform via the energy mapping ε_f = g(ε_i) and the Jacobian: f_f(ε_f) = f_i(ε_i) · |dε_i/dε_f|, and justify why g is energy-independent (e.g., ε_f = α ε_i) or invoke appropriate invariants (e.g., adiabatic invariants/Liouville theorem) that preserve the shape. If no energy mapping/Jacobian is given, or if the conclusion q = p is drawn solely from N conservation, the rule triggers a logic error. This applies to adiabatic expansion/compression, cooling, or any process where number conservation is invoked without addressing energy dependence.

rules.title: Check Wavefunction Normalization
rules.description: The wavefunction must be normalized such that the integral of its absolute square over all space equals 1, representing total probability.
rules.check_logic: Verify that ∫|Ψ(x)|² dx = 1 across all space, ensuring proper boundary conditions are included.
common_errors: Failing to normalize the wavefunction
Ignoring boundary conditions in infinite potential wells

rules.title: Verify de Broglie Wavelength Calculation
rules.description: Particles exhibit wave-like properties with a de Broglie wavelength given by λ = h/p, where h is Planck's constant and p is momentum.
rules.check_logic: Ensure calculation of λ uses λ = h/p correctly. Check that momentum is derived from mass and velocity appropriately.
common_errors: Incorrect substitute of mass or velocity for momentum
Using frequency instead of momentum

rules.title: Apply Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle
rules.description: The principle states that ΔxΔp ≥ ħ/2, indicating limits on simultaneous precision of position and momentum measurements.
rules.check_logic: Verify scenarios where ΔxΔp ≥ ħ/2 is used, and ensure measurements account for inherent uncertainty.
common_errors: Misinterpreting uncertainty as error
Confusing uncertainty in measurement with uncertainty in prediction

rules.title: Verify Energy-Momentum Relation Consistency
rules.description: Consistent application of E = p²/2m for non-relativistic quantum particles to relate energy and momentum.
rules.check_logic: Confirm energy calculations use E = p²/2m appropriately, avoiding relativistic mass substitutions.
common_errors: Using relativistic mass instead of static mass
Confusing kinetic energy with total energy

rules.title: Adherence to Sign Conventions in Coordinate Systems
rules.description: Proper application of sign conventions for potential energy and wavefunction direction in chosen coordinate systems is necessary.
rules.check_logic: Ensure differentiation between positive directions for momentum and potential in chosen coordinates and verify consistency in vector orientation.
common_errors: Using incorrect sign for potential energy
Misalignment of kinematic vectors in wave functions

rules.title: Validate Conditions for Photon Wave-Particle Duality
rules.description: Wave-particle duality for photons is evidential under conditions such as double-slit interference patterns.
rules.check_logic: Ensure system meets criteria for interference conditions like slit separation comparable to wavelength, and that light's coherence is maintained.
common_errors: Assuming duality in classical macroscopic conditions
Ignoring slit geometry requirements

rules.title: Ensure Dimensional and Unit Consistency
rules.description: Physical quantities involved must be dimensionally consistent, ensuring equations balance respective units.
rules.check_logic: Check all derived equations ensure unit consistency, particularly in the dimensions of energy, time, and action.
common_errors: Using incorrect units for wavelength, energy, or momentum
Discrepancies in derived units for modified equations

rules.title: Implement Probabilistic Interpretation of Quantum Mechanics
rules.description: The square of a wavefunction's amplitude gives the probability density; ensure interpretations abide probabilistic norms.
rules.check_logic: Examine probability calculations for adherence to Ψ*Ψ norms, ensuring correct integration bounds.
common_errors: Misinterpreting wavefunction absolute value for probability
Incorrect integration bounds for probability distribution

rules.title: Verify Time-Dependent Schrödinger Equation Application
rules.description: Ensure proper application of the time-dependent Schrödinger equation iħ∂Ψ/∂t = HΨ, where H is the Hamiltonian operator.
rules.check_logic: Validate that systems being analyzed account for the Hamiltonian and potential energy constraints.
common_errors: Ignoring potential energy variations over time
Incorrect formulation of the Hamiltonian

rules.title: 不确定关系估算动能能级
rules.description:
触发条件：要求使用不确定关系 (Uncertainty Relation) 估算基态动能或能量惩罚时
检查逻辑：动能估算公式应满足 E ~ (hbar^2) / (2 * m * Δx^2)，确保 Δp ~ hbar/Δx 的量级一致性。
rules.check_logic: 动能估算公式应满足 E ~ (hbar^2) / (2 * m * Δx^2)，确保 Δp ~ hbar/Δx 的量级一致性。

rules.title: 强磁场量子限长度选取
rules.description:
触发条件：涉及强磁场 (B) 下电子的二维局限或量子霍尔效应估算时
检查逻辑：应优先使用磁长度 l_B = sqrt(hbar/eB) 作为位置不确定度 Δx 的基准，而非经典回旋半径。
rules.check_logic: 应优先使用磁长度 l_B = sqrt(hbar/eB) 作为位置不确定度 Δx 的基准，而非经典回旋半径。
rules.trigger: 涉及强磁场 (B) 下电子的二维局限或量子霍尔效应估算时

rules.title: Verify Schrödinger equation for potential barrier
rules.description: The Schrödinger equation governs quantum tunneling. For a particle approaching a potential barrier, the wavefunction must satisfy continuity and the time-independent Schrödinger equation: (-ħ²/2m)(d²ψ/dx²) + V(x)ψ = Eψ.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that Schrödinger's equation is applied correctly in the regions of the potential barrier (both inside and outside). Verify that the second derivative, potential energy, and total energy terms are correctly substituted and consistent with the problem setup.
common_errors: Neglecting the second derivative of the wavefunction
Using incorrect expressions for kinetic or potential energy terms
Misidentification of the region where V(x) applies

rules.title: Ensure wavefunction continuity at barrier boundaries
rules.description: The wavefunction ψ(x) and its first derivative dψ/dx must be continuous at the boundaries of the potential barrier for quantum tunneling to occur.
rules.check_logic: Verify that ψ(x) and its derivative are equal on both sides of the barrier at the boundary points. Explicitly check the mathematical expressions for continuity.
common_errors: Ignoring the continuity condition for ψ(x)
Incorrect matching of derivatives at the boundary
Failing to evaluate boundary conditions explicitly

rules.title: Check for conservation of probability current
rules.description: The probability current (J) must be conserved throughout the tunneling process. For a one-dimensional case, J = (ħ/2mi) [ψ*(dψ/dx) - (dψ*/dx)ψ].
rules.check_logic: Ensure that the probability current is the same on both sides of the potential barrier. Verify the calculation of J explicitly and check for sign consistency.
common_errors: Not calculating probability current at all
Incorrect signs in the probability current formula
Assuming probability current is zero on one side

rules.title: Verify calculation for tunneling probability
rules.description: The tunneling probability (T) is given by T = exp(-2κa), where κ = sqrt(2m(V₀ - E))/ħ and a is the width of the potential barrier.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that the exponent in the tunneling probability formula is correctly calculated, using proper values for κ and a. Verify that all constants and units are consistent.
common_errors: Using incorrect units for barrier width or energy
Neglecting the negative sign in the exponent
Incorrect calculation of κ (e.g., forgetting ħ or using wrong mass)

rules.title: Confirm potential barrier geometry constraints
rules.description: Quantum tunneling assumes a well-defined potential barrier of finite height and width. The geometry of the barrier (e.g., rectangular) must be explicitly stated or derived.
rules.check_logic: Check that the potential barrier's height (V₀) and width (a) are finite and defined in the problem description. Ensure that the geometry is consistent with the tunneling scenario.
common_errors: Assuming an infinitely high or wide barrier without justification
Using inconsistent or undefined barrier parameters
Failing to specify the barrier geometry

rules.title: Verify wavefunction normalization
rules.description: The wavefunction must be normalized such that the total probability of finding the particle is 1. This ensures physical consistency.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the integral of |ψ(x)|² over all space equals 1. Check for proper normalization constants in the wavefunction.
common_errors: Failing to normalize the wavefunction
Using incorrect normalization constants
Ignoring the normalization condition entirely

rules.title: Radiometric dating: Misusing 238U:235U = 137:1 as an initial ratio
rules.description: Checks radiometric-dating solutions (e.g., U–Pb) for the conceptual error of treating the given 238U:235U = 137:1 ratio as the initial (formation-time) uranium isotope ratio rather than the present-day ratio. The rule flags the following patterns: (1) Explicit statements or equations setting N_238^0 : N_235^0 = 137 : 1, or wording such as "initial 238U:235U = 137:1". (2) Use of daughter growth equations with initial parent counts N_P^0 in the form N_D = N_P^0 (1 − e^{−λT}) when the problem provides present-day parent ratio and radiogenic daughter increments (correct form for using the present ratio is N_D = N_P_now (e^{λT} − 1)). (3) Final age equations that multiply by 137 instead of dividing by it (i.e., using N_238/N_235 = 137 in a way that yields (e^{λ_238 T} − 1) ∝ 137 × (e^{λ_235 T} − 1) rather than ∝ (1/137) × (e^{λ_235 T} − 1). For U–Pb problems where excess lead is obtained by subtracting the pure-lead baseline (Δ206 = 29.6 − 17.9, Δ207 = 22.6 − 15.5), the expected relation is Δ206/Δ207 = [N_238/N_235] × [(e^{λ_238 T} − 1)/(e^{λ_235 T} − 1)], with N_238/N_235 taken as the present ratio (137:1). Any derivation that instead uses initial counts or 1 − e^{−λT} with N^0, or treats 137:1 as an initial ratio, should be flagged.

rules.title: Verify the relativistic energy-momentum relation
rules.description: The fundamental equation relating energy, momentum, and mass in relativity is E² = (pc)² + (mc²)². This relation holds for all particles, whether massless or massive.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that the total energy squared equals the sum of the squared momentum term (pc)² and the squared rest energy term (mc²)².
common_errors: Incorrect computation of total energy (E).
Omitting the momentum term for moving particles.
Forgetting to square terms in the energy-momentum equation.

rules.title: Verify rest energy calculation
rules.description: Rest energy is given by the equation E_rest = mc², where m is the rest mass of the particle. This applies only when the particle is at rest (momentum p = 0).
rules.check_logic: Check if rest energy is calculated as mc² when the particle is at rest (p = 0).
common_errors: Confusing rest mass with relativistic mass.
Using velocity-dependent mass for rest energy calculation.
Incorrectly adding momentum contributions to rest energy.

rules.title: Check energy-momentum consistency for massless particles
rules.description: For massless particles (e.g., photons), the energy E and momentum p are related by E = pc. The rest mass term (mc²) drops out in this case.
rules.check_logic: Verify that for massless particles, E = pc is used, and rest energy is not included.
common_errors: Including rest energy for massless particles.
Using incorrect formulas for energy-momentum relation.
Mixing up units of energy and momentum.

rules.title: Ensure correct sign conventions for momentum and energy
rules.description: Relativistic momentum is a vector quantity, and its sign depends on the coordinate system used. Energy is always positive, as it represents a scalar quantity.
rules.check_logic: Verify that energy is non-negative and that momentum's direction is consistent with the chosen coordinate system.
common_errors: Assigning negative energy values.
Inconsistent sign conventions for momentum components.
Misinterpreting direction of momentum vectors.

rules.title: Check velocity constraints for relativistic equations
rules.description: The velocity of any particle in relativistic mechanics must always be less than the speed of light (v < c). This is a fundamental constraint of special relativity.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that any velocity used in relativistic equations satisfies the condition v < c.
common_errors: Using velocities greater than or equal to the speed of light.
Confusing relativistic velocities with classical limits.
Incorrect unit conversions leading to v >= c.

rules.title: Verify calculation of relativistic kinetic energy
rules.description: The relativistic kinetic energy is given by KE = (γ - 1)mc², where γ = 1 / √(1 - v²/c²). This applies to particles with v > 0.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that relativistic kinetic energy is calculated using KE = (γ - 1)mc² and that γ is computed correctly.
common_errors: Using classical kinetic energy formula (1/2mv²) instead of relativistic formula.
Incorrect computation of γ factor.
Forgetting to subtract the rest energy term from total energy to calculate KE.

rules.title: Check conservation of relativistic energy and momentum
rules.description: In any relativistic system, the total energy and momentum must be conserved. This applies to closed systems undergoing collisions or interactions.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the total energy and momentum before and after an interaction remain conserved.
common_errors: Omitting contributions from rest energy in total energy calculations.
Failing to account for vector nature of momentum in collisions.
Neglecting mass-energy equivalence in conservation equations.

rules.title: Verify invariant mass calculation
rules.description: Invariant mass, or rest mass, is consistent across all reference frames and is calculated using the relation E² - (pc)² = (m₀c²)².
rules.check_logic: Ensure that invariant mass is correctly calculated and consistent across different reference frames using E² - (pc)² = (m₀c²)².
common_errors: Confusing invariant mass with relativistic mass.
Incorrectly applying the invariant mass formula in varying reference frames.

检查逻辑：检查是否应使用 $s = (p_1 + p_2)^2$ 不变量。若结果含 $1/E_b$，应优先考虑相对论能量动量关系而非经典动能近似。
rules.check_logic: 检查是否应使用 $s = (p_1 + p_2)^2$ 不变量。若结果含 $1/E_b$，应优先考虑相对论能量动量关系而非经典动能近似。
